audits.name: Ford & Roman, 'Restrictions on Negative Energy Density in Flat Spacetime' (gr-qc/9607003; PRD 55, 2082 (1997)): Lorentzian-sampled QI for the free massless scalar, rho-hat >= -3/(32 pi^2 t0^4), plus the Sec. 4 curved-spacetime scope remark

source.located: arXiv gr-qc/9607003v2 (submitted 1 Jul 1996, revised 2 Oct 1996, v2 24 Jan 1997), L.H. Ford and T.A. Roman, Tufts; journal ref PRD 55, 2082-2089 (Feb 1997), as cited in Kontou-Sanders arXiv:2003.01815 ref. [74] and Fewster-Eveson gr-qc/9805024 ref. [3]
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/9607003 returned all 17 pages (abstract, Secs. 1-4, Appendices A-B, references). I read it in full twice, in two sessions, and re-checked every quotation. Eq.(1) on p.2 is quoted from Ref.[21] (Ford-Roman PRD 51, 4277 (1995)), where it was first derived; this paper re-derives it as Eq.(17), the m -> 0 limit of Eq.(16), by a plane-wave method.

audits.published_statement: p.2 Eq.(1) (and p.5 Eq.(17), the m->0 limit of Eq.(16)): 'for the free quantized massless scalar field in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, rho-hat == (t0/pi) INT_{-oo}^{oo} <T00> dt/(t^2+t0^2) >= -3/(32 pi^2 t0^4), for all choices of the sampling time, t0. Here <T00> is the renormalized expectation value of the energy density evaluated in an arbitrary quantum state |psi>, in the frame of an arbitrary inertial observer whose proper time coordinate is t.' (Units hbar = c = 1. The text layer prints 't0' for the proper-time coordinate, which is an extraction artefact.) p.4: 'the energy density is evaluated in the reference frame of an inertial observer, at an arbitrary spatial point which we choose to be x = 0.' The same paper also gives: massive scalar -3 G(y)/(32 pi^2 t0^4), y = 2 m t0 (Eq.16); EM field -3/(16 pi^2 t0^4) (Eq.48); 2D massless -1/(8 pi t0^2) (Eq.25). Sec.4 (p.11): 'in Minkowski spacetime, our bounds hold for an arbitrary choice of the sampling time, t0. Recently we argued that such bounds should also hold in a curved spacetime and/or one with boundaries, if the sampling time is restricted to be much smaller than the smallest local radius of curvature and/or the distance to any boundaries in the spacetime [23]. An explicit example ... [24] ... static closed and open Robertson-Walker universe models.' p.2: 'In quantum field theory ... the energy density may be unboundedly negative at a spacetime point.'
published_hypotheses: H1 free (non-interacting) quantized field; stress tensor T_mn = phi,m phi,n - (1/2) eta_mn (phi,a phi^,a + m^2 phi^2) (Eq.6). This is MINIMAL coupling (no xi R phi^2 term)
H2 massless scalar for Eq.(1) (massive: Eq.16 with G(y) <= 1; EM: Eq.48, twice as negative)
H3 four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, no boundaries ('derived for Minkowski spacetime, in the absence of boundaries', p.2)

H4 the bounded quantity is the Lorentzian TIME average rho-hat of <T00> along the worldline of an INERTIAL observer at ONE spatial point x = 0, with weight t0/[pi(t^2+t0^2)] of unit integral (Eq.8). It is not <T00> at a point, and not a spatial or spacetime average
H5 one-sided: a LOWER bound on rho-hat; nothing bounds positive energy density
H6 arbitrary state |psi> of the Fock space, with <T00> renormalized (normal ordered w.r.t. the Minkowski vacuum); the mode sums are assumed to converge in the V -> oo / omega_max -> oo limit (p.16)

H7 holds for ALL t0 > 0 in flat space. The extension to curved spacetime or boundaries, for t0 << the smallest local curvature radius and/or the boundary distance, is ARGUED in ref.[23] (PRD 53, 5496) and not proved in this paper. The paper names two supporting cases: Casimir plates, proved in [23] (p.2-3), and static RW (ref.[24], gr-qc/9608005)
H8 the derivation uses no time-energy uncertainty relation (Sec.4). It rests on two norm-positivity lemmas (App. A) and the kernel inequality S_m >= S~_m (App. B)
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H4+H5 (sampling and one-sidedness): candidates.py:112-116 and candidates.py:346-348 state and code '|rho| <= 3 hbar c/(32 pi^2 L^4)'. The source bounds only the SAMPLED rho-hat, and only from BELOW; it says the pointwise density 'may be unboundedly negative' (p.2). The absolute value adds a two-sided claim the source does not make. This is harmless for the magnitude of a negative demand, but it is not the published statement.

CONTRADICTS H4: overturn.py:220-222 says Ford-Roman and its descendants 'bound |rho| itself over a sampling region rather than an average along a line'. The published Eq.(1) is exactly an average along a line: an inertial worldline at one spatial point x = 0 (p.4). certify.py:154-159 and bounds.py:234 state it correctly. The tree's own DOCKET 55 withdrawal (achievable.py:316-323, bounds.py:225-240) records the substitution, but overturn.py:220-222 and overturn.py:277 still carry it.

ADDED (a spatial length used for a temporal width): candidates.py:112-114 ('sampling length L = c tau') and candidates.py:363-364 set the Lorentzian time width t0 = R/c, with R a spatial corridor size. The source has no spatial length. The SI conversion is exact; L = R is the tree's modelling choice. achievable.py:316-323 withdraws the same move for quantum_bound; candidates.py is not amended.

WEAKENED H3/H7 (flat space implies more than the tree uses): if <T00> = rho0 is static at the point, rho-hat = rho0 for every t0, and Eq.(1) for all t0 forces rho0 >= 0 (script I1/I2). So in flat space with no boundaries a static negative density is excluded outright. A finite L = R cut-off only makes sense under the Sec.4 extension, which this paper argues and does not prove. candidates.py says flat space is 'implied, not stated', and specthm's H_flat is ASSUMED (R4). The tree's choice is weaker than the flat theorem, so it errs against M, not for M.

DROPPED part of H7: noise.py:185-187 quotes Sec.4 as 'sampling time ... much smaller than the smallest local radius of curvature' and labels it 'Ford-Roman's own condition'. The source goes on to say 'and/or the distance to any boundaries in the spacetime', and introduces the whole remark with 'Recently we argued'. Its own status is an argued extension (ref.[23]) with two worked cases (Casimir plates, static RW), not a theorem of this paper.

NOT IN SOURCE (tree coding): bounds.py:46 and bounds.py:303 code Ford-Roman as K = 0 ('known saturated'), and bounds.py:455-456 asserts 'Ford-Roman is one of them'. The source claims no saturation. Fewster-Eveson's bound at g = sqrt(Lorentzian) is 27/(2048 pi^2 t0^4) = 9/64 of Ford-Roman (script J1; FE Eq.(5.6), READ). If that bound is valid for the Lorentzian, no state reaches Ford-Roman's constant, which supports the tree's own DOCKET 55 record 'K = 0 WRONG'. Caveat: FE's stated class requires rapid decay, but the Lorentzian decays only as t^-2 (script L3), and FE call their derivation formal. So in 4D this is supported, not proved. In 2D it is firm: Flanagan's optimal bound is 1/6 of Ford-Roman's at the Lorentzian (script L1). The fault is in the tree's coding, not in the source.

CONSISTENT: overturn.py treats minimal coupling as the case covered and names the non-minimal case as the L4 breaker. That matches H1 (Eq.6 is the minimal stress tensor). Fewster-Osterbrink (via Kontou-Sanders p.23, Table 3) prove that no state-independent QEI exists for xi != 0.

CONSISTENT: achievable.py:194 reproduces Eq.(1) exactly; achievable.py:196-198 quotes p.4 word for word; achievable.py:327-332 ford_roman_allow = 3 hbar/(32 pi^2 c^3 t0^4) is the correct SI restoration.

UNSTATED H1/H6 in owners: no owner names 'free field' or 'Fock state with convergent mode sums', except certify.py's ledger hypothesis list. QEI status for interacting 4D fields is still open (Kontou-Sanders p.24).

INHERITED FIGURE: spec.py:91-92 and spec.py:347 say '65 orders short against Ford-Roman'. That is not a figure from the source. candidates.py gets 70.606 orders at 1 m from the same inequality; the difference comes from the tree's sampling choice and the 105.276 = 32 pi^2/3 coefficient drop (script H3).

ATTRIBUTION, not a fault: achievable.py:327-332 cites the bound as 'gr-qc/9607003 Eq.(1)'. The location is correct, but Eq.(1) was first derived in PRD 51, 4277 (1995), Ref.[21]. That 1995 paper is the merged key 'ford-roman-1995-qi-massless-scalar', and I did not open it (NAMED-NOT-READ). It has the same coefficient.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS: 28 checks, exit 0; output in rederive/gr-qc_9607003.out. A: the Lorentzian sampler has unit integral and Fourier transform e^{-|W| t0} (Eq.7+8 -> Eq.9). B: the V->oo mode sum gives exactly -3/(32 pi^2 t0^4) = Eq.(17). C: G(0) = 1, G is decreasing, and Eq.13 -> Eq.14 is exact. D: EM = 2 x scalar (Eq.48). E: 2D gives -1/(8 pi t0^2). F: the App.B kernel is PSD on 400 random spectra. G: end to end on 21,900 random multimode squeezed-state/phase pairs, Eq.(9) never falls below the finite-V bound Eq.(12). The test is not vacuous: 612 pairs are negative. The single-mode case reaches 0.998587 of the bound, and a bound half as large is violated (control). H: the SI form is correct; 105.276 = 32 pi^2/3. I: a static negative density is excluded in flat space. J: Fewster-Eveson at the Lorentzian = 27/(2048 pi^2 t0^4) = 9/64 of Ford-Roman. L: in 2D at the Lorentzian, Flanagan's optimal bound is 1/6 of Ford-Roman's and FE's is 1/4 (as FE p.8 prints); the Lorentzian tail is t^-2. K: crossover 0.307933 l_P; shortfall 4.0371e52; G, hbar and c cancel. Not machine-checked: Lemma A (a finite Fock truncation breaks the commutation relations). It was read, and check G exercises it implicitly.

later_literature.what: Restates the flat inertial minimally coupled QWEI (61) for all Hadamard states and attributes the Lorentzian case to Ford-Roman; C = 3/(32 pi^2) for the Lorentzian. Table 3: a state-independent QWEI is impossible for xi != 0. The status of interacting fields is 'less clear'. There is no null-line QEI in 4D. Recorded DISCREPANCY, not a refutation: read literally with f^2 = Lorentzian, (61) gives 9/64 of that C (FE's Eq.5.6). So the review's C is Ford-Roman's own constant, and its wording is loose about f versus f^2.

Generalises Ford-Roman to smooth, even, non-negative samplers that are compactly supported or rapidly decaying. At the Lorentzian, Eq.(5.6) gives -27/(2048 pi^2 tau^4), which is 9/64 of Ford-Roman: a tighter bound, against M. In 2D, FE's bound is 4x and Flanagan's optimal bound 6x stronger than Ford-Roman's. FE state their own limits: the derivation is formal, the Lorentzian is outside their rapid-decay class, and a sharp-box sampler gives no bound (p.9).
Samplers with compact support should generally be used; the Lorentzian's tails limit what Eq.(1) excludes.

later_literature.ref: Fewster & Smith, AHP 9, 425 (2008); Kontou & Olum, PRD 91, 104005 (2015)
later_literature.what: Absolute QEIs in curved spacetime, and a curvature-dependent QWEI at small curvature. Together they put the Sec.4 argued extension on a proved footing for the free minimally coupled scalar.
No state-independent QEI can exist for the non-minimally coupled scalar. H1 is load-bearing, and the tree's L4 breaker sits on it.

later_literature.ref: Fewster & Pfenning JMP 47, 082303 (2006); Ford & Roman PRD 87, 085001 (2013)
later_literature.what: Non-inertial observers can see long-lived negative energy, and under sinusoidal motion the average can become arbitrarily negative. The inertial hypothesis H4 is load-bearing. The tree uses the inertial case, so this is a scope limit, not drift.
Applies the QI to the Alcubierre metric in the short-sampling regime (the source's ref.[25]).

A QI derived from the second law on a detector probe (Unruh-DeWitt, free massless scalar, 4D). It neither reproduces nor contradicts 3/(32 pi^2), because its kernel differs from the energy-density kernel.

later_literature.ref: Helfer CQG 13, L129 (1996); Pfenning & Ford gr-qc/9805037; Fewster & Teo gr-qc/9812032
later_literature.what: FE footnote 1: 'space averaged energy densities in 4-dimensions are not bounded below'. This is one published basis for certify.py:154-159's no-ball-QI reading. The other two papers extend the QI to curved and static spacetimes.

audits.lacked_data: No, and the evidence runs one way. Eq.(1) is a theorem about the free massless minimally coupled scalar in 4D Minkowski space, and no measured quantity enters it. I re-derived every step: the Fourier identity, the V->oo limit, and the massive, EM and 2D companions. I also checked the result end to end on 21,900 squeezed states, with a non-vacuity guard. What the 1996 authors lacked was later THEORY, not data. (a) Fewster-Eveson 1998 (READ) makes the Lorentzian bound 64/9 tighter, which moves against M. (b) Curved-spacetime proofs (Fewster-Smith 2008, Kontou-Olum 2015) back the Sec.4 remark that was only argued in 1996. (c) We now know which hypotheses are load-bearing: non-minimal coupling admits no state-independent QEI, the inertial observer matters, interacting 4D fields are open, and 4D has no null-line or spatial-only QEI. (c) is where the result's reach is narrower than a loose reading, and it is where the tree's L4 breaker sits. None of this moves the published conclusion within its stated hypotheses. The only numbers the tree adds are hbar, c and G. hbar and c are exact by definition, and all three cancel from the tree's crossover (script K3).
audits.grade_evidence: The published theorem stands. I read it at source twice, re-derived it symbolically, and checked it end to end on 21,900 squeezed-state/phase pairs, with a non-vacuity guard and a control. No datum it depends on has moved. The grade is NARROWED because the tree uses it on a wider class than the one published. (1) candidates.py:112-116, candidates.py:346-348 and overturn.py:277 state '|rho| <= 3 hbar c/(32 pi^2 L^4)', which drops the sampling (H4) and the one-sidedness (H5). (2) overturn.py:220-222 says it bounds |rho| 'over a sampling region rather than an average along a line', contradicting the single spatial point x = 0 on p.4. (3) candidates.py:363-364 sets t0 = R/c, with R a spatial corridor size. DOCKET 55 withdrew that move in achievable.py but not in candidates.py or overturn.py. (4) The Sec.4 curved-spacetime scope used in noise.py is an argued claim (ref.[23]) with two worked cases, and noise.py:185-187 drops 'and/or the distance to any boundaries'. The tree's use errs against M in two places. Flat-space Eq.(1) for all t0 excludes a static negative density outright (script I1/I2). Fewster-Eveson's bound is 9/64 of Ford-Roman's (script J1; FE Eq.5.6, READ). That supports, without proving it in 4D, the tree's own record that bounds.py's K = 0 ('saturated') coding is wrong; in 2D, Flanagan's optimal bound makes it firm (script L1). Nothing in the source is refuted, and there is no misprint, so the grade is not WRONG.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: every owner restates the result as a one-sided lower bound on the Lorentzian time average along an inertial worldline at one spatial point, as certify.py and bounds.py:234 already do; and candidates.py's L = R step is carried as a named modelling hypothesis whose authority is the Sec.4 extension (or Kontou-Olum), not Eq.(1). To WRONG for the source: an explicit Fock state of the free massless minimally coupled 4D scalar with rho-hat < -3/(32 pi^2 t0^4). None appeared in 21,900 random squeezed states, and FE's bound would forbid one. OPEN does not apply: the source was read and the derivation is closed-form. Separately, the support for '4D Ford-Roman is not saturated' would fall if FE Eq.(5.6) were shown invalid for the Lorentzian sampler; that would not change this grade.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (either direction), gr-qc/9607003 Ford-Roman 1997
verifiers.reason:
I could not refute the NARROWED grade in either direction. Two wording faults in the audit need fixing, but neither moves the grade.

SOURCE: I did not make a fresh alphaXiv read. Both answer_pdf_queries and get_paper_content returned 'quota exceeded', and the arXiv host is refused by the egress proxy (403). What I read in full is the auditor's saved alphaXiv page dump, scratchpad/d67/src/gr-qc_9607003.alphaxiv_pages.txt: pages 1-17 of v2, including the references. Every quotation in the audit matches it:
- Eq.(1) on p.2, attributed to Ref.[21] ('it was shown in Ref.[21]').
- p.2: 'may be unboundedly negative at a spacetime point'.
- p.4: 'inertial observer, at an arbitrary spatial point which we choose to be x = 0'.
- Eq.(6) is the minimal-coupling stress tensor.
- Eqs.(16), (17), (25) and (48).
- p.16: convergence is assumed.
- Sec.4 on p.11: 'Recently we argued ... much smaller than the smallest local radius of curvature and/or the distance to any boundaries [23] ... explicit example ... Ref.[24] ... static closed and open Robertson-Walker'.
- p.10: the energy-time uncertainty principle is 'not used as input'.
- Nothing in the paper claims the bound is saturated or optimal. The only optimality remark (p.7) is that the 2D massive bound 'may perhaps ... not [be] optimal'.

INDEPENDENT CHECKS: I wrote a separate sympy script, verify/refute/indep_check.py. It reproduces:
- the unit-integral Lorentzian;
- Eq.(13) at m = 0: 3/(32 pi^2 t0^4);
- the EM bound, 3/(16 pi^2 t0^4);
- the 2D bound, 1/(8 pi t0^2);
- Fewster-Eveson 4D at g = sqrt(Lorentzian): (1/16pi^2) INT g''^2 = 27/(2048 pi^2 t0^4), which is 9/64 of Ford-Roman;
- Flanagan's 2D bound, 1/6 of Ford-Roman;
- a static negative density, which gives rho-hat = rho0 while the bound tends to 0 as t0 -> oo.

The auditor's own script reruns ALL PASS. I could not re-read FE (quota), so FE's '4x' 2D figure rests on the auditor's FE read. It is consistent with (1/4pi) INT g'^2. Fewster-Teo gr-qc/9812032 p.3 (cached) corroborates that FE's bounds are 'stronger than those obtained by Ford and Roman when the Lorentzian sampling function is applied'.

TREE DRIFT: I checked it read-only, and it is real at every cited line:
- candidates.py:112-116 and 346-348 give '|rho| <= 3 hbar c/(32 pi^2 L^4)' with L = c tau, and shortfall(R) = rho_needed(R)/ford_roman(R) (candidates.py:363-364).
- overturn.py:220-222 says the bound is 'over a sampling region rather than an average along a line'.
- overturn.py:277 carries the same |rho| form.
- noise.py:185-187 drops 'and/or the distance to any boundaries' and the word 'argued'.
- bounds.py:46, 303 and 455-456 code K=0 'saturated'; the tree itself flags this as WRONG.
- achievable.py:316-332 carries the DOCKET 55 withdrawal and the correct SI form.

So the tree uses the result on a wider class than the one published. Later literature (non-minimal coupling, non-inertial observers) also narrows its reach. STANDS would therefore over-represent the result. Nothing in the source is refuted and there is no misprint, so WRONG does not apply. No datum enters, so DATA-DEPENDENT does not apply. The source was read and the derivation is closed-form, so OPEN does not apply.

CORRECTIONS NEEDED (the grade does not move):

(1) The direction claims are inverted, or at best one-sided. The audit says the tree's use 'errs against M' in two places.
- In both places the tree's bound is MORE PERMISSIVE than the truth. The flat-space Eq.(1) for all t0 forbids a static negative density outright, and FE's constant is 9/64 of the one the tree uses. A too-permissive allowance understates the refusal, so the tree's error runs in M's favour. It is the correction that runs against M.
- In the other direction, under the Sec.4 curved-space reading, t0 = R/c can violate t0 << the curvature radius (noise.py records b = 61 l_G). The licensed t0 is then shorter, and the licensed allowance larger, so there the tree's L = R choice is too strict: against M.
- The direction depends on whether the flat or the curved hypothesis is taken, and the audit should say so rather than 'errs against M' flatly.

(2) The claim that the text layer's 't0' for the proper-time coordinate on p.2 is 'an extraction artefact' is declared, not checked. The text layer renders every other t0 identically, so it may be a genuine typo in the paper. Under M's rule it should be recorded as a discrepancy, whose cause cannot be decided from the text layer, not asserted to be an artefact.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: run the audit's script, check that what it encodes is the published theorem, run a vacuity guard with the hypotheses negated, and try a stronger finite check
verifiers.reason:
The audit's re-derivation holds up. I found no fault in its encoding, and my own stronger checks agree with it. Evidence below.

(1) RE-RUN. I copied the script to verify/rederive/gr-qc_9607003.py and ran it: 28 PASS, exit 0. The output matches the audit's figures exactly: G1 worst margin -0.188, G2 612 of 21,900 pairs negative, G3 0.998587, J1 9/64, L1 1/6, L2 1/4, K1 0.307933, K2 4.0371e52. The seed is fixed, so the run is deterministic.

(2) ENCODING. I checked the script line by line against the published statement, and it tests the theorem rather than a toy of it.
- A1/A2 are the Eq.(7)+(8) -> Eq.(9) Fourier step.
- B1 correctly turns -(1/2V) SUM w e^{-2wt0} into -(1/4pi^2) * 3!/(2t0)^4 = -3/(32 pi^2 t0^4). Note that B1 takes Eq.(12) as its input, so B alone checks only the V->oo limit. The link from Eq.(9) to Eq.(12) is carried by G and F.
- I re-derived the normal-ordered <T00> at x=0 for a massless scalar myself: prefactor (w_i w_j + k_i.k_j)/sqrt(w_i w_j)/(2V), kernels e^{-|dw| t0} and e^{-(w_i+w_j) t0}. The script's rho_hat matches this. The sign of the <aa> term is covered by its phase sweep.
- I checked the script's Bogoliubov convention. N = beta^dag beta and M = -alpha^dag beta are exactly the second moments <a^dag a> and <aa> of the vacuum of b = alpha a + beta a^dag, which inverts to a = alpha^dag b - beta^T b^dag. So G samples genuine pure Gaussian states, and G0 confirms the commutation relations are preserved.
- G3's single-mode formula is correct: prefactor 2w, and the minimum tends to -w/(2V) as q -> 1.
- I re-integrated J1 and L1/L2 independently with mpmath at 30 digits: 0.140625 = 9/64, 1/6 and 1/4.
- Weaknesses, none fatal. G covers only random zero-mean Gaussian states with at most 8 modes, not all states. G4 is not an independent control: it only restates G3 (vals[-1] > 0.5). The K and H checks test the tree's own arithmetic, not the source.

(3) STRONGER FINITE CHECK (verify/rederive/exact_inf2.py, output in exact_inf2.out, exit 0). On a finite set of box modes, the infimum of rho-hat over ALL states can be computed exactly. That covers mixed, non-Gaussian and displaced states. It equals the ground energy of the normal-ordered quadratic operator, found from the symplectic eigenvalues. Across 3,000 random mode sets of up to 39 modes, with t0 from 1e-4 to 0.32:
- the operator was bounded below every time;
- the exact infimum never went below Eq.(12) restricted to those modes (worst margin -0.080);
- the closest approach was E0/bound = 0.920.
This closes the "only random Gaussian states" gap in the audit's G1.

(4) VACUITY GUARD, with the hypotheses negated. I grew the mode set to shells of radius R = 2, 4, 6, 8 at width 0.05.
- Lorentzian time sampler (the theorem's case): the exact infimum converges, -12.9, -41.3, -55.5, -58.9.
- Sharp box sampler (the smoothness hypothesis dropped; FE p.9 says it gives no bound): -70.9, -322, -484, -1714. It grows without settling, and the smallest eigenvalue of Kn +/- Km heads toward zero.
- Spatial Gaussian average instead of a time average along the worldline (drops H4): -51.8, -216, -372, -489, and -592 at R=10 in my first run. It is still growing.
So the check separates the hypothesis from its negations; it does not pass everything. This is finite evidence consistent with FE p.9 and with Helfer (restated in FE p.2), not a proof of unboundedness.

(5) CAVEAT against over-claiming. In the V=1, t0=0.05 box, the exact infimum (about -60) lies far above both Ford-Roman (-1520) and FE (-214). That fits the audit's 'not saturated' reading, but the box is too coarse at this t0 to stand in for the continuum. I add it as no new support for non-saturation, and the 4D non-saturation point stays SUPPORTED, NOT PROVED, as the audit already says.

GRADE. No step of the published theorem failed, and nothing in the re-run touches the tree-side drift that the audit's NARROWED rests on (candidates.py |rho|, L = R, overturn.py 'sampling region'). I re-checked only the re-derivation, not those owner lines. The grade NARROWED stands as the audit proposed it.

audits.published_statement:
Sec. 7 (Discussion, p.30): 'While the latter [shape functions or embedding diagrams] can certainly be used without risk for detecting flare-out in static wormholes, they are at best misleading if applied to dynamic wormholes. This is simply because the embedding of a wormhole spacetime requires selecting and lifting out a particular time-slice and embedding this instantaneous spatial three-geometry in a flat Euclidean R3. For a static wormhole, any constant time-slice will suffice, and if the embedded surface is flared-out in the spatial direction orthogonal to the throat, then it is flared-out in spacetime as well. But if the wormhole is dynamic, flare-out in the spatial direction does not imply flare-out in the null directions orthogonal to the throat.'

Sec. 4 (p.11): '...suggests why it is that the embedding of the spatial part of a wormhole spacetime in an Euclidean R3 is no longer a reliable operational technique for defining "flare-out" in the time-dependent case.'

Def. 4.1.1: a two-surface satisfies 'simple flare-out' iff theta = 0 and dtheta/du >= 0 (a marginally anti-trapped surface).

Sec. 5.1 eqs. (49)-(50): at a throat, dtheta/du + sigma^2 = -8 pi T_ab l^a l^b, so T_ab l^a l^b <= 0: 'The NEC is therefore either violated, or on the verge of being violated'. Strong flare-out gives a strict violation somewhere (eq. 51). Averaged flare-out gives a sign-averaged violation over the throat (eq. 53). Near the throat the NEC is 'violating, or on the verge of violating' along partial null curves (0, u*_x).

Eqs. (77) and (90): a null throat is simply flared iff the NEC is violated or on the verge there. 'Temporary suspension of the violation of the NEC at a time-dependent throat also leads to a simultaneous obliteration of the flare-out property of the throat itself.'
published_hypotheses: H1 DEFINITIONAL: a throat is a closed, two-sided, spacelike 2-surface on which the expansion of ONE future-directed orthogonal null congruence vanishes, with dtheta/du along that same null direction >= 0 (simple), > 0 somewhere (strong), > 0 everywhere (strongly anti-trapped), sign-averaged > 0 (averaged), or N-fold degenerate (Defs 4.1.1-4.1.6, Table 1). Flare-out is defined on NULL congruences, 'free from notions of embedding and shape-functions'.

H2 Einstein equation G_ab = 8 pi T_ab (eq. 11), optionally plus a totally antisymmetric (Kalb-Ramond) torsion. The NEC statements are about the total T_ab contracted with the SAME null congruence that defines the throat.
H3 No symmetry, no asymptotic flatness, no topology and no staticity is assumed. The congruences are surface-orthogonal and therefore twist-free (eqs. 55-57).
H4 Smoothness: theta is Taylor-expanded in the affine parameter near the throat (eq. 38) for the near-throat statements. Degenerate throats are handled by eqs. (39)-(41).
H5 Under SIMPLE flare-out the NEC conclusion is NON-STRICT: T_ab l^a l^b <= 0, 'violated, or on the verge of being violated'. A strict violation needs strong flare-out.
H6 The conclusion is about the NEC (a null contraction of T_ab). It is not about the WEC, negative energy density, or negative Misner-Sharp mass.

H7 The Sec. 7 sentence is a NON-IMPLICATION remark in the Discussion, not a numbered theorem. The paper supports it with three things: the Sec. 4 variational argument (independent null deformations delta u_+ and delta u_-), the Sec. 4.2 static-coalescence proof (eqs. 43-48), and the Sec. 6.1 worked example (eq. 69), in which the spatial 'center' r0 differs from the null throats r*(t).
H8 'Static' in the Sec. 7 equivalence means the constant-Killing-time slice (eq. 43).

audits.lacked_data:
M's hypothesis tested for this result: there is no datum to lack. HV 9802046 is a mathematical statement in classical GR: the Raychaudhuri equation, the Einstein equation and a definition of throat. The Sec. 7 remark is a non-implication, which one counterexample settles, and the script builds one in HV's own metric family. No constant, measurement or extrapolation enters, so no later data can move the conclusion.

What came later is definitional, not observational. Maeda-Harada-Carr 2009 showed that the NEC conclusion depends on defining the throat on NULL hypersurfaces; spatially defined dynamic throats can satisfy the DEC. Hayward 1999 showed that non-strict flare-out admits degenerate 'on the verge' cases. Neither contradicts HV. Both mark the edge of HV's class, and that edge is where the tree's REFUTED row over-reaches. The text-layer discrepancies are misprints or extraction artefacts, and none changes a sign or a conclusion.

On its own, the quoted Sec. 7 statement (with the Sec. 4 embedding remark) would STAND. It is READ verbatim at source, re-derived with an explicit sympy counterexample in HV's family (69), HV's eqs. (72)-(77), (88) and (90) recompute from the metric and agree, and Maeda-Harada-Carr 2009 confirm it.

The grade is NARROWED because the tree rests more on this key than the source carries:

(1) driven.standard_table's REFUTED row ('therefore the corridor needs no negative energy'), PRIOR_ART_REFUTATION and driven.py:84 extend HV's NEC theorems to a spatially defined corridor (Gamma > 1 on a slice). HV's theorems apply only at null-flared marginally anti-trapped surfaces, and HV's own Sec. 7 is why a slice criterion does not reach them. The DEC-satisfying dynamic spatial throat of Maeda-Harada-Carr, re-derived here, shows the gap is real.

(2) HV conclude an NEC statement, which is non-strict under simple flare-out. The tree's row speaks of 'negative energy'.

(3) foliation.py:616, 'REPLACED BY A STRONGER ONE', drops the strict/non-strict distinction.

This is not WRONG for any tree line. The row may still stand on Olum 1998, which it also cites; that is audited under gr-qc/9805003. HV's misprints are discrepancies, not refutations.

To STANDS, either of two changes would do. The first is re-scoping driven.py's REFUTED row and PRIOR_ART_REFUTATION so that they cite HV only for null-flared throats ('suspending the NEC at a dynamic throat destroys the throat'), keep the 'violated or on the verge' qualifier, and leave the corridor's energy requirement to Olum. The second is showing that the corridor contains a marginally anti-trapped sphere with null flare-out, so that HV's T_ab l^a l^b <= 0 applies to it directly.

Those families are general: the conformal Morris-Thorne family with arbitrary Omega(t) and b(r), and the Vaidya-type family with arbitrary psi(v,r) and m(v,r). The audit's line "the Raychaudhuri identity recomputed here rules this out" therefore overstates what was machine-checked. The general identity is textbook but was not recomputed here. audits.published_statement: Frolov & Zelnikov (2011) p.166, restated verbatim in 2605.01811 p.3 as Theorem 1 (Generalized Birkhoff's theorem): 'If the energy-momentum tensor generating a spherically symmetric gravitational field of the form ds^2 = gamma_AB dx^A dx^B + R(x)^2 dOmega^2, where ... R(x) is a non-constant function, obeys the following condition: T_AB = (1/2) T^C_C gamma_AB, then the corresponding solution of the Einstein equations possesses an additional Killing vector field.' With the Maxwell ansatz A = phi(t,r) dt + p cos(theta) dphi, which carries both electric and magnetic charge, the condition holds and the unique solution is f = 1 - 2M/r + (Q_e^2+Q_m^2)/r^2 (eqs 16-18, 62). From p.1: 'A generalization of this theorem to the electro-vacuum case of the Einstein-Maxwell theory gives Reissner-Nordstrom metric as a unique asymptotically flat solution. However, in such a case, there also exists a spherically symmetric but not asymptotically flat solution - the so called Bertotti-Robinson universe', which is AdS2 x S2 with R0 = sqrt(e^2+p^2) (eq 21). Schleich & Witt p.1: generalized Birkhoff theorems 'are local uniqueness theorems ... their corollary is that locally spherically symmetric solutions exhibit an additional local Killing vector field; however this field is not necessarily timelike'.
published_hypotheses: 4D general relativity, G_ab = 8 pi T_ab (Lambda is allowed in the Schleich-Witt and Kubiznak et al. generalizations)
local spherical symmetry: SO(3) with 2-dimensional spacelike orbits; metric gamma_AB dx^A dx^B + R^2 dOmega^2

R(x) NON-CONSTANT (grad R != 0) -- 'The assumption that the radial function R(t,r) is non-constant is crucial' (2605.01811 p.3). R = const gives Bertotti-Robinson when Lambda = 0, and Plebanski-Hacyan or charged Nariai when Lambda != 0
the source obeys T_AB = (1/2) T^C_C gamma_AB. Source-free Maxwell satisfies this, and so does any L(S,P) nonlinear electrodynamics, for the field A = phi dt + p cos(theta) dphi
source-free region (no charged matter); electric and magnetic charge both allowed
the conclusion is local: locally isometric to RN or to BR. The extra Killing vector is timelike only where grad R is spacelike, so staticity is not implied
regularity: C^2 in the classical proof; C^0 piecewise-C^1 per Bergmann-Cahen-Komar 1965 (restated in 2411.09193, not read here)
asymptotic flatness is not a hypothesis of the local theorem; it only excludes BR in the 'unique asymptotically flat' phrasing

audits.lacked_data: The theorem (Hoffmann 1932-33) belongs to classical GR plus linear Maxwell. Its conclusion takes no measured input, so no later datum can move it; E1-E4 hold for arbitrary metric functions and symbolic charges. Four things the 1932 authors lacked were checked: (1) Magnetic monopoles, proposed by Dirac in 1931. Modern restatements include them, and they only replace Q^2 with Q^2+P^2 (E2-E3). (2) A measured Lambda (1998 on; Planck 2018 gives 1.089e-52 m^-2). It changes the frozen formula to m + Lambda R^3/6 and adds Nariai-type exceptions, but m stays frozen, and the term is numerically negligible below about 100 pc (E6, E9). (3) Bertotti-Robinson (1959). It is a real grad R = 0 exception to RN uniqueness, but its m is also frozen (E5). (4) Strong-field QED (Euler-Heisenberg, 1936). The Birkhoff condition holds for any L(S,P) (2605.01811), so the structure survives with a different m(R). Every later datum examined leaves standing that the Misner-Sharp mass of spherical source-free electromagnetism is a fixed function of R. What later knowledge corrects is how complete the statement is (the exception set and the field ansatz), and that is exactly where the tree's wording drifts.

audits.published_statement: FK 1807.03808 v4 p.15: 'Proposed Bound. For all states within the regime of Perturbative Quantum Gravity (PQG), in any dimension d and for locally flat regions, the expectation value of the null-null contracted Stress-Energy tensor, smeared over any achronal null geodesic is bounded by <T^s_kk> >= -B/(G_N tau^2) (36). In (36) B is a constant we have yet to determine and tau is the affine distance over which we are smearing ... The smallest distance we allow ourselves to smear is l_uv, and the largest is such that we remain in a locally flat region.' Precise form, eq.(37): INT f<T_kk> dlambda >= -(B/G_N) INT (f')^2/f dlambda, 'for arbitrary smearing functions f which are smooth and non-negative', with 1/tau^2 = INT (f')^2/f (38). p.4: 'We have not determined the constant B'. Eq.(6): R^s_kk >= -#/tau^2, which 'does not have any factors of hbar'. p.15: 'there are no counter examples to this bound, but whether or not a rigorous proof exists is left for future research.' LL 1808.09970 eq.(1) fixes the coefficient at 1/(32 pi G_N). They prove it for holographic induced gravity on a brane, from the Brane Causality Condition, on a geodesic that is achronal on the support of rho.

audits.lacked_data: FK 2018 lacked three things: B, a proof, and evidence for smearing beyond the curvature radius. Later work supplied B = 1/(32 pi) (LL, holographic), with FKK arguing B << 1. Proofs arrived only in two restricted frameworks (LL; FF 2021). Evidence past the curvature radius came as two examples (FKK 2020). No datum has moved against the published statement, and no counterexample is known. For the tree's use the later data cut both ways. B arrived at its loosest natural value, and every smaller B strengthens the violation (E6), so nothing the authors lacked opens a door. But the violation sits at tau = 1.4-2.0 L_curv, which is exactly the regime FK 2018 excluded for lack of data and which later work reaches only by argument. M's hypothesis is partly borne out: the 2018 statement was incomplete and was completed later, but not overturned. The remaining open part, validity at tau >~ L in curved spacetime, is OPEN, not WRONG.
audits.grade_evidence: The form, the G bookkeeping and B = 1/(32 pi) reproduce the source exactly (E1, E3), and the tree's crossover reproduces to 4e-4 (E5). The tree nonetheless uses the bound on a larger class than was published: (i) its violation appears only at tau = 1.40 L_curv off-axis and 2.0 L_curv on the affine axis geodesic, whereas FK 2018 restrict to tau << L; inside that domain the configuration satisfies SNEC (E8). (ii) It integrates along non-geodesic, non-affine lines, though the affine axis geodesic still violates (E7). (iii) Achronality is unchecked (OPEN). (iv) Its truncated Gaussians print bounds that are off by up to -94%, with verdicts unchanged (E4-E5). The attribution of B to FK is a discrepancy, not a refutation. index3.py:750 over-states SNEC as a theorem. No moved datum reverses the verdict (E6).
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: STANDS: a proof that SNEC holds for tau >~ L in curved spacetime, plus an achronality check of the ray and the rows recast on the affine geodesic. WRONG, for the extension the use needs: a PQG state that violates SNEC at tau ~ L. DATA-DEPENDENT: a controlled derivation of B >~ 3/(32 pi), since E6 gives w_c > 1.5 there.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (snec-freivogel-krommydas, audit grade NARROWED)
verifiers.reason:
NARROWED survives, but its lead piece of evidence, (i) the tau << L domain drift, is overstated, and it is overstated against the tree. The grade still holds on the other hypothesis drifts.

WHAT I READ AT SOURCE (alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1807.03808v4 and 1808.09970v1):

(a) FK 2018 is not self-consistent about its domain. The abstract p.1 and p.4 say the smearing length is 'small compared to the curvature scale'. But p.16, the very passage the audit cites for H2, says: 'we chose to avoid this issue by imposing that our smearing is performed over a region of size comparable to the radius of curvature'. The regime FK actually exclude is the evaporating-black-hole one, 'many times the curvature radius'. The audit writes H2 as a uniform tau << L and concludes that 'inside FK 2018's stated domain the configuration SATISFIES SNEC; the violation sits in a regime FK 2018 excluded'. That reading is selective. I re-checked the curvature scale independently from the full Riemann tensor (orthonormal Eulerian frame, sympy; verify/refute/snec_riemann.py):
- L_Riem = 0.4773 at y = 0.3 and 0.4504 on the axis, which confirms the audit's L_curv = 0.47 / 0.45 computed from max|G_ab|.
- The onset of violation is therefore at tau_c = 1.37 to 1.40 L. That is 'comparable to' L under p.16's wording, and outside the domain only under the abstract and p.4 wording.
- Correct statement: the onset lies at the edge of FK 2018's domain, which the source states ambiguously. The tree's 'EVERY width of order the bubble radius or more' (w = 5 and 20, i.e. tau of about 7 to 30 L) is clearly outside FK 2018's domain. So the narrowing holds for the tree's large-w claims, not for the onset.

(b) The coefficient the tree uses, B = 1/(32 pi), comes from Leichenauer-Levine. Their proven bound carries NO smearing-length restriction:
- eq.(1) holds for 'arbitrary, non-negative smearing function' on a geodesic 'achronal on the support of rho'.
- They let lambda0 go to -infinity and lambda1 to +infinity, and recover the achronal ANEC from it.
- Their Sec. V applies it to long geodesics (Delta lambda ~ 1/G_N).
- Their z0 << eps << l condition constrains the bulk-curve scale eps and the state's curvature against the cutoff. It does not constrain the smearing width.
- So the audit's H9 and its data_at_publication row ('rests on FKK 2020's argued extension') misplace the support. In the holographic induced-gravity framework, a use at tau >~ L is covered by LL's PROOF, subject to achronality. It does not rest only on FKK's two examples.
- Consequence: the domain drift is a drift against FK 2018's wording, not against the result that supplies B.

WHY THE GRADE STILL STANDS AS NARROWED, NOT STANDS:
(ii) anec.py integrates along non-geodesic, non-affine fixed-y lines with measure dx. Both FK eq.(17)/(36) and LL require an affinely parametrised null geodesic. The audit's affine axis-geodesic check (w_c = 1.2689) keeps a violation, so the verdict survives only when restricted to the axis ray. The tau/L of about 2.0 quoted there depends on the normalisation: K = k/(1+v) has Eulerian energy 1/(1+v) inside the bubble.
(iii) Achronality is a hypothesis of both FK eq.(36) and LL eq.(1). It is never checked, so it is OPEN.
(iv) The printed truncated-Gaussian bounds are off by up to -94%. I verified the E4 table against the closed form -2B/w^2. The verdicts are unchanged.
(v) index3.py:750's 'STATE-INDEPENDENT theorems over all Hadamard states' over-states the result. The proof exists only in holographic induced gravity (LL) and in cutoff free-field theory (FF).

CHECKS THAT HOLD:
- The attribution discrepancy is confirmed. FK p.4 says 'We have not determined the constant B'. LL p.1 says 'Freivogel & Krommydas were not able to fix the numerical factor ... in this note we determine it'.
- E1/E3 bookkeeping is confirmed. typefour.py:179 divides by 8 pi, so T = G/(8 pi) and -4B at B = 1/(32 pi) is LL eq.(3)'s -1/4 INT rho'^2/rho.

REQUESTED CORRECTIONS (no grade change):
1. Restate H2 as 'small compared to (p.1, p.4) / comparable to (p.16) the curvature radius'.
2. Replace 'inside FK 2018's domain the configuration satisfies SNEC' with 'the onset tau_c = 1.37-1.40 L lies at the edge of FK 2018's ambiguously stated domain; w >= 5 is clearly outside it'.
3. Record that LL's proof carries no smearing-length restriction, only achronality and the holographic framework. The domain drift therefore does not weaken the use of B = 1/(32 pi) inside that framework.
4. Make (ii) and (iii) the primary grounds for NARROWED.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: run the script, check what it encodes against the published statement, and run the vacuity guard
verifiers.reason:
I copied the script to verify/rederive/ and ran it. It printed SELFTEST OK and reproduced every figure the audit cites: E1 to E8, w_c = 0.9274, affine axis crossover 1.2689, L_curv = 0.4695 and 0.4504, and the -11.5 / -36.1 / -94.3 % truncation errors. The NARROWED grade holds. Three of its supporting numbers do not hold as stated, and they need correcting.

What held (adv_snec.py, adv_snec.out):
- The crossover is fully converged: w_c = 0.9274 on windows [-8,8] and [-12,12] and at n = 1600 and 3200.
- The E7 encoding is right for the tree's own spacetime. typefour.py:138 sets d_t g = 0, so the metric is frozen and stationary, and in it K = k/(1+v) with dlambda = dx. I checked the geodesic equation numerically: max|K.grad K| = 8.5e-7 on the axis, so it is an affine geodesic. On the y = 0.3 line it is 0.37, which confirms that line is not a geodesic.
- The vacuity guard passes: with T = 0 the crossover finder returns inf, and at B = 100 x 1/(32 pi) it also returns inf. So the violation it reports is not an artefact of the finder.
- The curvature scale is corroborated from the Riemann tensor rather than the Einstein tensor: max|R^a_bcd| gives L = 0.4512 on the axis and 0.4818 at y = 0.3.
- The attribution discrepancy is confirmed: the saved FK v4 text has no hit for 32 pi, and line 154 reads 'We have not determined the constant B'.

What did not hold: the checks use a toy of the bound. SNEC quantifies over every smooth non-negative f (FK eq.37), but E5, E7 and E8 test only Gaussians centred at x = 0. So the audit's 'tau_c = 1.40 L', 'tau = 2.0 L on the affine axis geodesic' and 'inside FK 2018's domain (w <= 0.5) the configuration SATISFIES SNEC' hold only for that family.

Two weaker points:

- The frozen-metric caveat is the tree's own, and the audit defers it to the sibling audit. I did not re-audit it here. Note that for a moving bubble the affine factor would be 1/(1 - v_s + v)^2 rather than 1/(1 + v)^2.

Why the grade survives: on the geodesic ray, which is the only one FK's H4 admits, the smallest violating tau lies between 0.69 L and 1.57 L. No f violates at tau << L, since tau > 0.69 L is necessary. So the violation still sits where FK 2018 require 'locally flat' smearing and the curvature is not small. The use therefore still rests on FKK 2020's argued extension, and NARROWED stands. But the margin is of order L, not 1.4 to 2.0 L. How far outside the domain the violation sits depends on which O(1) definition of the curvature radius is used.

Corrections the report needs:
- Replace 1.40 L and 2.0 L with 'between 0.69 L and 1.57 L on the affine geodesic, found by optimising f'.
- Withdraw 'inside w <= 0.5 the configuration satisfies SNEC'. It holds only for centred Gaussians; an optimised f on y = 0.3 violates at tau = 0.97 L.

audits.name: Speed of light in vacuum, exact SI value (c = 299 792 458 m/s)

source.located: The defining statement is the SI: the metre redefinition of the 17th CGPM (1983), with c kept as one of the defining constants in the revised SI of 20 May 2019. Neither document is on arXiv. Read here through CODATA 2022 (Mohr, Newell, Taylor, Tiesinga, arXiv:2409.03787). Table XXXII p.50 and Table XXXIII p.51 give 'speed of light in vacuum c 299 792 458 m s^-1 exact'. p.60 says c, h, e, k and N_A are exactly known 'as a result of the 1983 redefinition of the meter in terms of an exact value of c and the 2019 revision of the SI'. The p.65 list of symbols calls c 'one of the seven defining constants of the SI'.
source.via: CODATA 2022 (arXiv:2409.03787) restates the SI definition exactly. The 1983 CGPM resolution and the 2019 SI Brochure themselves are NAMED-NOT-READ.

audits.published_statement: CODATA 2022, Table XXXII (p.50): 'speed of light in vacuum  c  299 792 458 m s^-1  exact'. p.60: c, h, e, k and N_A are 'exactly known as a result of the 1983 redefinition of the meter in terms of an exact value of c and the 2019 revision of the SI'. The same table gives G = 6.674 30(15) x 10^-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2 with u_r 2.2e-5, a value p.60 says is identical to the 2018 one.
published_hypotheses: H1 (definition): the metre is defined by fixing c at 299 792 458 when expressed in m s^-1, with the second defined by the caesium frequency. So c has no uncertainty in SI units. This is a choice of unit system, not a measurement.

H2 (physical content the definition does not supply): c is the invariant speed of relativity and the speed of light in vacuum. For a real electromagnetic signal to travel at c you need a vacuum path, a massless photon and no vacuum dispersion. These are empirical claims, tested separately (for example LHAASO time-of-flight on GRB 221009A, arXiv:2402.06009).
H3: exactness holds only in the SI. In geometric units c = 1 by convention, and the SI value matters only when converting to m, s or J.
hypothesis_drift: No drift in the value. nonstatic.py:253 ('C = 2.99792458e8  # m/s, exact') and transit.py:142 ('C_SI = 2.99792458e8') are exactly the SI value: Fraction(literal) == 299792458. The integer is below 2^53, so it is stored exactly as a 64-bit float and 'exact' still holds in the code (computed).

Label discrepancy in canonical.json, not in the owner files. The merged key 'si-2019-c' dates the fixing of c to 2019. The source says c was fixed in 1983 and the 2019 revision kept it (CODATA 2022 p.60). Neither owner file states a year: grep for 2019, 1983 and CGPM in nonstatic.py and transit.py finds nothing.

Added physical hypothesis at transit.py:145 ('def arrival_time(D): return D/C_SI  # the classical channel, at c'). The SI definition does not say that a real classical channel arrives in time D/c; that needs H2 plus a vacuum path. A real radio signal through interstellar plasma is slower. Computed cold-plasma delay at 1 GHz over Earth-Proxima: 0.054, 0.540 and 5.40 ms for assumed n_e of 0.01, 0.1 and 1 cm^-3 (n_e was not read at source). This delay is never negative, so it can only push advantage_over_light to zero or below. It cannot move the conclusion that there is no advantage over light.

Observation, not a drift. transit.py:146 defines advantage_over_light(D) = arrival_time(D) - D/C_SI, and arrival_time(D) is D/C_SI, so the result is zero for any positive c. Sympy gives D/c - D/c = 0, and the float result is exactly 0.0 at all four DISTANCES. The printed 0.000 comes from how the channel is modelled; it does not test c.

nonstatic.py:256 ('LY = 9.4607304725808e15  # m, exact (Julian year x c)'): 365.25 x 86400 x 299792458 = 9 460 730 472 580 800 exactly (computed). This equals the literal and is stored exactly as a float, since it is even and below 2^54. No drift.

audits.lacked_data: Testing M's hypothesis on this result: for the value itself, no author lacked any data. Since 1983 c has been a definition, so no later measurement can change 299 792 458 m/s; a better measurement would change how the metre is realised, not c. Evidence: CODATA 2022 lists c as 'exact' with no uncertainty (p.50), and leaves it out of the 2018-to-2022 comparison because it is exactly known (p.60). The tree also leans on a physical claim, at transit.py:145 ('the classical channel, at c'), and that claim is empirical. It has since been tested with data nobody had in 1983: from LHAASO's 2024 E_QG,1 bound (read), any vacuum-dispersion deviation for a GHz photon is at most 4e-35 of c (computed). The one effect the tree does not model is plasma along a real path, and that makes signals slower, never faster. So the conclusion that there is no advantage over light holds either way, and more data would not change it.
audits.grade_evidence: The value and its 'exact' status were read in CODATA 2022 (arXiv:2409.03787 Table XXXII p.50, and p.60). The owner literals at nonstatic.py:253 and transit.py:142 equal it exactly and are stored exactly as floats. Every use that rests on it was re-derived symbolically and numerically, and all 22 checks pass: band_time_seconds, crossing_time_seconds, build_energy, band_ratio, and transit's D23 advantage_over_light. No datum can move a defined constant. Three points are recorded, not repaired. (i) The merged key 'si-2019-c' in canonical.json gives the wrong year: c was fixed in 1983 and kept in 2019. This label is outside the owner files. (ii) transit.py:145 adds the physical assumption that a classical channel runs at c, which the definition does not supply. Every correction to it (dispersion in a medium) makes the signal slower, so it cannot move the tree's conclusion. (iii) advantage_over_light is zero by construction, so its printed 0.000 comes from how the channel is modelled; it does not test c.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: Nothing about the value can change the grade short of a CGPM redefinition of the SI that stops fixing c, and none exists (CODATA 2022). The added assumption at transit.py:145 would make the grade NARROWED only if some conclusion needed arrival at exactly D/c as a time a real channel achieves, rather than as the limit no channel can beat. No conclusion does, because advantage_over_light is zero by construction. A detected faster-than-c vacuum dispersion at radio frequencies larger than about 1e-12 would reopen H2; the bound read here is 4e-35.

audits.published_statement: Mohideen-Roy (physics/9805038, abstract and p.9) used an AFM to measure the force between a flat plate and a metallized sphere of diameter 196 um (Al plus <20 nm Au/Pd), at separations of 0.1-0.9 um. The result is 'consistent with present theoretical calculations including the finite conductivity, roughness and temperature corrections', with an rms deviation of 1.6 pN, which is 1% at the smallest separation. The ideal formula without corrections gives 6.3 pN, which is 5% at the smallest separation. Theory was compared through the proximity force F0 = -pi^3 hbar c R/(360 d^3). Bressi et al. (quant-ph/0203002, eq. 4) measured parallel Cr-coated silicon surfaces over 0.5-3.0 um through the cantilever frequency shift. They found K_C = (1.22 +- 0.18)e-27 N m^2 against pi h c/480 = 1.3e-27 N m^2, a '15% precision'. Lamoreaux 1997 (via Bordag et al. pp.209-210 and 249) used a torsion pendulum with an Au/Cu lens and plate over 0.6-6 um and reported agreement 'at 5%' with the ideal sphere-plate formula. The 1998 erratum corrects the lens radius from 11.3 cm to 12.5 cm (+10.6% in theory) and adds a 22% Au finite-conductivity correction at 0.6 um. Bordag et al. conclude that '(5-10)% accuracy would probably apply at the smallest separations only' and that the temperature corrections 'remain unconfirmed'. For ideal plates (Bordag et al. eqs 2.36-2.37 and 4.31): E/A = -pi^2 hbar c/(720 a^3) and F/A = -pi^2 hbar c/(240 a^4), for perfect conductors at T = 0.
published_hypotheses: The measured quantity is a FORCE: sphere-plate force for Mohideen-Roy and Lamoreaux, plate-plate force gradient for Bressi. None of them measures an energy density or a stress tensor.
The plates are real metals: Al+Au/Pd, Cr, and Cu+Au. Agreement at the 1% level needed finite-conductivity and roughness corrections (Mohideen-Roy eqs 2-4).
The sphere-plate results reach E/A through the proximity force approximation F = 2 pi R E/A(d), with R >> d (Mohideen-Roy eq. 1; Bordag et al. eq. 4.106). Only Bressi is plate-plate.
Separation ranges: 0.1-0.9 um (Mohideen-Roy, absolute separation >= 120 nm), 0.5-3.0 um (Bressi), 0.6-6 um (Lamoreaux).

Electrostatic backgrounds were subtracted by calibration fits. In Lamoreaux the electrostatic force was about 5x the Casimir force, and d0 was fitted to the expected Casimir force (Mohideen-Roy p.3; Bordag et al. p.210).
Room temperature. The thermal correction is negligible for a << hbar c/kT, and Lamoreaux did not confirm it at 4-6 um.
Ideal-plate formula: perfect conductors, flat infinite parallel plates, T = 0, renormalised mode sum.
The uniform energy density -pi^2 hbar c/(720 a^4) between the plates (Brown-Maclay) holds for perfect conductors only. Dispersive plates add a positive position-dependent term (Sopova-Ford eq. 50).
hypothesis_drift: candidates.py:73-74 adds 'measured in the laboratory' to the ideal-plate ENERGY DENSITY. The sources measure a force between real metals. Sopova-Ford quant-ph/0204125 p.15: 'The existence of an attractive Casimir force is not an indicator of whether the energy density at the center of the plates is actually negative or not'; p.16: 'no clear way has been found to directly observe the local energy density'.

tolman.py:483-485 says 'the measured parallel-plate Casimir tensor', which adds 'measured' to the TENSOR. Only the force is measured; rho and p_t come from theory. tolman.py:1317-1322 and 2539-2540 state it correctly ('FORCE is the one MEASURED quantity'; u_0 DERIVED).

tolman.py:506-507 and 2855 (d, R = 1e-8, 1e-3) drop the separation range. Every cited measurement is at d >= 0.1 um, and the only plate-plate one is at >= 0.5 um. The tree evaluates at d = 10 nm, which is below the gold skin depth c/omega_p = 21.93 nm that the tree itself banks (tolman.py:1508-1512, 3044).

tolman.py:1317-1322 names 'ideal parallel conducting plates', but it drops the fact that the measurements confirm Lifshitz theory with finite-conductivity corrections, not the ideal formula at the quoted precision (Mohideen-Roy p.9: 6.3 pN ideal vs 1.6 pN corrected). tolman.py:1317-1322 and 2539-2540 drop the proximity-force step. Two of the three cited experiments are sphere-plate and reach E/A only through PFA.

rederivation.outcome: ALL ASSERTIONS PASS. (A) sympy: E/A = -pi^2 hbar c/(720 d^3) from Bordag (2.36), with the Bose integral Gamma(4)zeta(4) = pi^4/15 confirmed numerically. F/A = -3u_0 = -pi^2 hbar c/(240 d^4). The tensor is traceless, the isotropic average has p = -u0/3, and the raw cell gives a factor 9. u_0(10 nm) = 4.33375e4 J/m^3 and m = -2.019814e-21 kg, so the tree's numbers reproduce. (B) Bressi K_C = 1.30013e-27, pull -0.45 sigma; Lamoreaux radius +10.6%. (C) Plasma-model Lifshitz eta for gold: 0.110 at 10 nm, 0.525 at 100 nm, 0.871 at 600 nm (Lambrecht-Reynaud 0.87), 0.986 at 6 um; nonretarded limit check 0.99994. (D) Sopova-Ford eq. 50: the perfect-conductor limit is recovered to 1%, the sign changes between omega_p a = 90 and 99 (paper ~99), and the gap-centre energy density at gold 10 nm is POSITIVE (+0.0405/a^4). Log at rederive/casimir-force-measurements.out.

later_literature.what: Between plasma-model plates the energy density is a negative constant plus a positive position-dependent term. It is negative at the gap centre only for omega_p a > ~99. The sign of the force does not fix the sign of the energy density, and the local energy density is not directly observable. Reproduced numerically here.

Derives the ideal formulas; gives the Hamaker regime at a << lambda_0; 10-20% conductivity corrections at 1 um; covers the Lamoreaux erratum and '5-10% at the smallest separations only'; reports 62-350 nm measured at 1%.
Au and Cu forces are equal within 1% over 0.6-6 um, with eta_Au(0.6 um) = 0.87 against the erratum's 0.78. This resolves Lamoreaux's Au/Cu discrepancy.
Au sphere-plate over 0.2-8 um. The Drude model is excluded over 0.2-4.8 um and the plasma model is consistent. This confirms the force and contests the material model at finite T.
The Drude/plasma 'Casimir puzzle', 2022-2026. It bears on finite-T real-metal forces, not on the ideal formula or on 10 nm.

audits.lacked_data:
What the authors lacked:
- Lamoreaux 1997 lacked accurate optical data and the correct lens radius (1998 erratum: +10.6% radius, 22% Au correction). His 5% agreement was partly fortuitous: corrections above 20% were 'not observed', and the electrostatic force was 5x the Casimir force (Mohideen-Roy p.3).
- Mohideen-Roy and Bressi lacked later patch-potential characterisation, and Bressi had no model for the 1-2 um residual.

What later data did:
- Harris-Chen-Mohideen 2000 (62-350 nm) and Bimonte et al. 2021 (0.2-8 um) confirmed the force and the Lifshitz theory, narrowed the precision claims, and opened the Drude/plasma question at finite T.
- None of this changes the conclusion the tree takes from these papers: the force is attractive and matches E/A = -pi^2 hbar c/(720 d^3) in the limit d >> lambda_p.

What does change the tree's use was never missing from these authors' work:
- No cited experiment measured at 10 nm, and no experiment measures an energy density.
- At 10 nm, real gold gives E/A = 0.110 of ideal (computed here).
- The plasma-model gap-centre energy density there is positive (Sopova-Ford 2002, reproduced here).

Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: the derivation re-derives exactly, and all three measurements agree with theory within their corrected errors. Evidence for it, narrowly: Lamoreaux's 5% was overstated for lack of data. That is a discrepancy, not a refutation.
audits.grade_evidence:
The published results stand:
- The ideal formula re-derives exactly in sympy.
- Bressi agrees with pi h c/480 at -0.45 sigma.
- Mohideen-Roy agree with corrected Lifshitz theory at 1%.
- Bimonte et al. 2021 confirm the force.
- No refuting counterexample exists.

The tree uses the result more broadly than the sources support, in three places:
1. candidates.py:73-74 and tolman.py:483-485 carry 'measured' onto the energy density and the tensor, which no experiment measures (Sopova-Ford pp.15-16).
2. tolman.py:506-507 and 2855 evaluate at d = 10 nm. That is outside every cited range (>= 0.1 um) and below gold's skin depth. There, real-gold E/A is 0.110 of ideal, and the plasma-model gap-centre energy density is positive (+0.0405/a^4, computed here).
3. The Lamoreaux citation omits its 1998 erratum.

The tree does name 'ideal parallel conducting plates' (tolman.py:1317-1322). So the positive control's VERDICT YES stands: it depends only on the sign of p_r for an ideal-plate construction, and the tree already grants it only test_field_background. What moves is the 'measured' / 'not an invention' provenance at 10 nm, and the magnitude m = -2.019814e-21 kg, which is an ideal-plate construction rather than a number from the measured regime.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade:
Any of these would move the grade:
- **To STANDS:** the tree restricts MEASURED to real-plate forces at d >= ~0.1 um (>= 0.5 um for plate-plate), labels u_0 and the tensor at 10 nm as ideal-plate constructions, and cites the Lamoreaux erratum. Alternatively, it picks d inside the measured range with d >> c/omega_p.
- **To DATA-DEPENDENT:** the verdict or a load-bearing magnitude is made to depend on real-metal E/A at 10 nm. The material model (Drude/plasma/optical data) and the Hamaker constant would then become live inputs.
- **To WRONG:** a measurement contradicts the sign of the force, or the d^-4 law inside the measured range. None was found.
- A direct plate-plate measurement near 10 nm would replace the plasma-model estimate eta = 0.110.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (casimir-force-measurements, audited grade NARROWED)
verifiers.reason:
The NARROWED grade holds. I found one over-statement inside the audit's own evidence. It runs against the tree, and it does not move the grade.

WHAT I READ AT SOURCE (alphaXiv page text):
- Mohideen-Roy physics/9805038 pp.1-9 confirms every figure the audit quotes: sphere diameter 196 um; separations 0.1-0.9 um; absolute separation >= 120 nm; rms deviation 1.6 pN = 1% at the closest point; ideal formula 6.3 pN (5%); F0 = -pi^3 hbar c R/(360 d^3). Their conductivity correction is plasma-model with lambda_p ~ 100 nm (eq. 2).
- Bressi quant-ph/0203002 confirms: eq. (4) K_C = (1.22 +- 0.18)e-27 N m^2; theory pi h c/480 = 1.3e-27; range 0.5-3.0 um; 15% precision; alternative fit 1.24 +- 0.10 (Fig. 4 caption); an unexplained residual at 1-2 um.
- Bordag et al. quant-ph/0106045 pp.207-210 and 249 confirm the Lamoreaux erratum (R 11.3 -> 12.5 cm, +10.6%; 22% Au correction at 0.6 um), the phrase '(5-10)% accuracy would probably apply at the smallest separations only', and 'temperature corrections remain unconfirmed'.
- Sopova-Ford quant-ph/0204125 pp.12-16: eq. (50) is the EXACT collisionless-Drude (plasma-model) expression, not an asymptotic expansion, so evaluating it at omega_p a = 0.456 is legitimate. The centre energy density turns negative at omega_p a ~ 99 (eq. 51, Fig. 4). The p.15 and p.16 quotes the audit uses are verbatim.

WHAT I RECOMPUTED INDEPENDENTLY (verify/refute/casimir_check.py):
- a^4 U at the gap centre: +0.04050 at omega_p a = 0.456; -0.000313 at 99; -0.01369 at 1e5 (the ideal value is -0.013708). This matches the audit.
- The audit's own script passes all its assertions. I checked its integrands against eqs. (34a), (34b) and (50): they match.
- The tree sites match what the audit says:
  - candidates.py:73-74 says 'measured in the laboratory' about the energy density.
  - tolman.py:483 says 'measured parallel-plate Casimir tensor'.
  - tolman.py:1317-1322 and 2539-2540 say the FORCE is the one measured quantity.
  - tolman.py:2855 evaluates at d, R = 1e-8, 1e-3.
- So the hypothesis drift is real. Every cited measurement is at d >= 0.1 um (0.5 um for plate-plate), and the tree evaluates at 10 nm. The grade rests on those two drifts, and both survive.

WHAT IS REFUTED, NARROWLY (a flattening against the tree, which M's two-way rule forbids):
- In data_at_publication the audit labels eta = 0.110 at 10 nm correctly as 'gold plasma model at 9.0 eV'. But grade_evidence and lacked_data restate it as 'real-gold E/A is 0.110 of ideal', and data_at_publication says it moves the magnitude by 'about 9x (m ~ -2.2e-22 kg)'.
- The plasma model is outside its validity at 10 nm. Bordag et al. p.154 limit it to 'the micrometer domain' and p.159 say it omits interband absorption.
- Bordag et al. eq. (5.73) gives the Hamaker constant from gold's optical data as H_Au = (4.4 +- 0.2)e-19 J. The plasma model at 9 eV gives 2.12e-19 J (computed here).

- The same caveat applies to the positive gap-centre energy density: it is a plasma-model result, and the audit mostly labels it so. Sopova-Ford p.15 say another epsilon 'would change the details'. No real-gold local energy density was read or computed here, so for real gold that sign is a model estimate, not established.

WHY THE GRADE STANDS:
- None of this touches the grade's grounds:
  - 'measured' is carried from the force onto the energy density and tensor;
  - d = 10 nm is outside every cited range;
  - the Lamoreaux erratum is omitted.
- The magnitude still moves by a large factor under either material model. The sign of E/A and of the force is untouched. VERDICT YES depends only on the ideal-plate construction.
- No source contradicts the sign or the d^-4 law inside the measured range, so WRONG is excluded. STANDS is excluded by the drifts above.

RECOMMENDED CORRECTION TO THE AUDIT TEXT:
- Replace 'real-gold E/A is 0.110 of ideal' with 'plasma-model eta = 0.110; with the optical-data Hamaker constant H_Au = 4.4e-19 J (Bordag eq. 5.73), eta ~ 0.23-0.27; either way several times below ideal'.

The re-run reproduces every printed value and ends ALL ASSERTIONS PASS. The values: u_0(10 nm) = 4.33375e4 J/m^3; m = -2.0198137e-21 kg; K_C = 1.30013e-27 N m^2 with a pull of -0.445 sigma; plasma-model gold eta = 0.1099 at 10 nm, 0.525 at 100 nm, 0.871 at 600 nm and 0.986 at 6 um; nonretarded check 0.99994; gap-centre a^4 U = +0.0405 at omega_p a = 0.456.

Encoding:
(1) Section A is partly circular. Its 'Bordag (2.36)' line puts in a prefactor, -hbar c pi^2/(3 d^3 (2pi)^4) times Gamma(4)zeta(4), that gives 720 by construction, so A1 is an arithmetic identity, not a derivation. I derived E/A two independent ways, and the theorem stands:
- Dimensional-regularised transverse integral (-m^3/(6pi), sympy) with zeta(-3) = 1/120 and two polarisations gives -pi^2 hbar c/(720 d^3) exactly.
- Exponential-cutoff mode sum minus the continuum (mpmath, lambda = 1e-2) gives d^3 E/A = -0.0137059 against -0.0137078.
(2) Section C: the Lifshitz integrand is the real formula, not a toy. The variables are q = vacuum kappa, kappa_medium = sqrt(q^2 + 1), and k dk = q dq on q >= xi. Two checks it passes: the independent nonretarded Li3 limit, and eta -> 1 at large d.
(3) Section D: the integrand matches Sopova-Ford eq. (50) at z = a/2 term by term. That covers the t^2 r^2 e^{-2u}/(r^2 e^{-2u} - 1) terms, the (1-t^2)[r/(1-r^2 e^{-2u}) + r'/(1-r'^2 e^{-2u})] e^{-u} term with cosh = 1, and the 1/(2pi^2) prefactor. r and r' are exactly eqs (34a) and (34b), with scipy dblquad argument order correct. The perfect-conductor limit is exact: r = -1 and r' = 1 kill the second term and leave -pi^2/720. The 1% offset at omega_p a = 1e4 is the real O(1/(omega_p a)) position-dependent term, about 1.3e-4/a^4 by hand estimate. It is not an integration error.

Vacuity guard (mutation runs, all in verify/rederive/):
- mut_perfect.py negates the plasma hypothesis (omega_p x 1e4, so effectively a perfect conductor). eta(10 nm) becomes 0.9991, D2 turns NEGATIVE, and the script fails with AssertionError. The finite-conductivity findings therefore come from the hypothesis and are not built into the check.
- mut_360.py changes 720 to 360. A1 becomes False and the script fails.
- mut_tm.py corrupts the TM reflection coefficient. It crashes with a math domain error, so the result is not insensitive to the Fresnel form.

Discrepancies found, recorded and not refuting:
(a) The sign change at the gap centre is at omega_p a = 96.61 (brentq, my indep.py). The paper says '~99', '~100' and '>100'. The audit's 'between 90 and 99' is true but loose, and its 2.17 um gold crossover should be about 2.12 um (96.6 x 21.93 nm).

(c) Recomputed from eq. 50, the gap-centre curve peaks at about 0.096 near omega_p a ~ 3. Sopova-Ford Fig. 4 has a y-axis running to 0.2, and its peak value could not be read from the page text. Agreement with the figure's amplitude is OPEN; the equation encoding is verified.
(d) The positive centre energy density at 10 nm holds for the plasma (collisionless Drude) model only. Real gold at omega_p a = 0.456 has interband and dissipative contributions. The audit does label it 'plasma-model', so this is a named hypothesis and not an over-claim, but it should not be quoted as a real-gold result.

Every data row checks out at source. NARROWED holds. Four wording points need tightening, and none of them moves the grade.

WHAT CHECKS OUT (all READ at source through alphaXiv):

- Mohideen-Roy physics/9805038, abstract and pp. 3, 6, 9: rms 1.6 pN, which is 1% at the smallest separation; the ideal formula gives 6.3 pN (5%); absolute separation >= 120 nm. Lamoreaux's electrostatic force was 5x the Casimir force (p. 3); Bordag p. 209 says the same thing inverted: Casimir was about 20% of the residual electrostatic force.
- Bordag quant-ph/0106045, pp. 207-210 and 249: lens radius 11.3 -> 12.5 cm, which is +10.6% (recomputed 0.1062); 22% Au correction at 0.6 um; d0 and beta fitted using the expected Casimir force; 'the temperature corrections remain unconfirmed and the (5-10)% accuracy would probably apply at the smallest separations only'. Page 232 gives 62-350 nm at about 1%, and p. 154 gives 10-20% conductivity corrections at about 1 um.
- Lambrecht-Reynaud quant-ph/9912085: eta_Au(0.6 um) = 0.87, which is 12% above the erratum's 0.78 (0.87/0.78 = 1.115); Au and Cu agree within 1%.
- Bimonte 2104.03857, pp. 1, 28 and 33: Drude excluded at 95% CL over 0.2-4.8 um; plasma consistent over 0.2-8 um; 'generally recognized physical explanation ... is lacking'. Its patch potentials were characterised by Kelvin probe, which supports the lacked_data point that the 1997-2002 experiments had no such characterisation.
- Sopova-Ford quant-ph/0204125: eq. 50 is exact within the collisionless-Drude (plasma) model at T = 0 with sharp continuum interfaces, not an asymptotic form. The sign change is at omega_p a ~ 99 (the paper also writes ~100 and >100). The pp. 15-16 quotes are verbatim.
- Tree sites confirmed at tolman.py:481-485, 1317-1331, 2539-2540 and 2855 (d, R = 1e-8, 1e-3), and at candidates.py:73-74 and 317.
- The rederive script PASSES and reproduces u_0 = 4.33375e4 J/m^3 and m = -2.019814e-21 kg.

INDEPENDENT CHECK (verify/data/casimir-force-measurements-datacheck.py):
- The positive gap-centre energy density at 10 nm is robust. With Drude damping (gamma = 35 meV) a^4 U moves from 0.04049 to 0.04043. It stays positive for every omega_p a from 0.2 to 90. Reaching the negative regime at 10 nm would need hbar omega_p ~ 2 keV, which no metal has.
- The sign flip therefore survives any local-continuum metal model. It rests on the sharp-interface continuum description, and Sopova-Ford say themselves that this description breaks down at the wall.

FOUR NARROWINGS (discrepancies in the audit's wording, not refutations):
1. The magnitude figures (eta(10 nm) = 0.110, 'about 9x', m ~ -2.2e-22 kg) are plasma-model estimates. They sit outside the domain Bordag p. 154 gives the plasma model ('a few tenths of a micrometer' upward), and interband transitions are not modelled at hbar c/a ~ 20 eV. The implied plasma-model Hamaker constant, computed here, is 2.1e-19 J. value_now labels the model, but moves_conclusion states 'about 9x' flatly; it should carry 'plasma-model estimate, interband NOT modelled' as a NAMED hypothesis. The real-gold factor is OPEN here.
2. 'flips the SIGN ... for real plates': the computation is for plasma/Drude continuum plates, so say so. The sign is robust within that class, as checked above.
3. 'partly fortuitous': Mohideen-Roy p. 3 offers a fortuitous cancellation as one of two possibilities, the other being large systematic error. Stating it as a finding over-represents against Lamoreaux.
4. 'Bressi had no model for the 1-2 um residual' is slightly overstated. The alternative fit with a linear drift 'allows for a possible explanation' (Fig. 4 caption); the paper calls the conventional causes unresolved and its work in progress.

M'S HYPOTHESIS: it is answered with evidence both ways, not presumed. The evidence for it is narrow: Lamoreaux's 5% was overstated for lack of optical data and the correct radius, and the Drude/plasma question is still open at finite T. The evidence against it: the formula re-derives exactly, and all three measurements agree with theory within their corrected errors. The moves_conclusion entries follow, with the four narrowings above.

audits.name: Fewster & Osterbrink: no state-independent QEI for the non-minimally coupled scalar (xi > 0); state-dependent QEI for 0 < xi <= 1/4; H-bounds; and the ledger O1 figures computed on their construction

source.located: C.J. Fewster & L.W. Osterbrink, 'Quantum Energy Inequalities for the Non-Minimally Coupled Scalar Field', arXiv:0708.2450v2 [gr-qc], 23 Oct 2007 (J. Phys. A 41 (2008) 025402, reference as printed in 1809.05047 ref.[20] and 2309.10848 ref.[6]). Read: abstract and Sec.1 p.1-3; Sec.2 eqs (1)-(21) p.3-6; Sec.3 eqs (22)-(34) p.6-8 in full; Theorem 4.2 eqs (44)-(45); Theorem 4.3 eqs (52)-(54); Theorem 5.1 eq (65); Sec.5.2 eqs (69)-(72); Theorem 5.3 eq (90); Corollary 5.4 eqs (91)-(92); Sec.6 Conclusion p.20-21.
source.via: alphaXiv get_paper_content(fullText=true) on arXiv:0708.2450. The full extracted text (4,137 lines) is saved at scratchpad/d67/src/0708.2450.txt. Sections 1-3 were read line by line; Sections 4-6 were read at every theorem and corollary and at the conclusion.

audits.published_statement: Sec.3 p.6-8 (massless, xi > 0, 3+1 Minkowski): 'In this section we consider the massless quantised scalar quantum field with xi > 0 in a (3+1)-dimensional Minkowski space ... It will be shown that local averages of the energy density are unbounded from below on the class of Hadamard states.' One-particle states Psi_kappa = a^dag(h_kappa) Omega, with h_kappa(k) = 4 pi sqrt2 (kappa - |k|/3) e^{-|k|/kappa}/kappa^2, <H> = 2 kappa/3 (26) and <rho>(0,0) = -xi (2 kappa)^4/(3 pi^2) (29). The j-particle states give (33) '<rho> < -rho_0 for all x in B(tau')', with total energy (34) '2 j kappa'/3 > 2 pi^2 rho_0/(xi kappa'^3) ... illustrating that the large negative energy density effects also require large positive overall energy, at least in this example.' 'Summarising, we have shown that to any bounded subset O of Minkowski space and arbitrary constant rho_0 > 0 there is a Hadamard state in which the expected energy density is less than -rho_0 throughout O. In particular any smearing rho_quant(f) with a non-negative compactly supported distribution f is unbounded from below on the class of Hadamard states.' Theorem 4.2: for xi in [0,1/4], a globally hyperbolic spacetime and a timelike geodesic gamma, (rho_quant o gamma)(f^2) >= -Q_xi(f), where Q_xi(f) = Q~_A 1 + xi(:Phi^2: o gamma)(Q_B[f]) + xi(:Phi^2: o gamma)(Q_C[f]) (difference type). Abstract and Sec.5.2: 'Q(f) can be bounded by any power of the Hamiltonian greater than 2, while rho(f) cannot be bounded by powers less than 3'. Footnote 1 adds that q might have to be at least 4, and p.19 says p <= 2 is not excluded. Sec.6: '(at least for massless fields in four-dimensional Minkowski space) ... the non-minimally coupled scalar field with xi > 0 admits states with arbitrarily large negative energy density over arbitrarily large bounded spacetime regions. Thus [it] cannot obey QEIs ... in which there is a state-independent lower bound'; 'negative energy effects with large magnitude, while possible over large regions, require more energy to achieve than positive energy densities of the same magnitude and ... the energy budget for these two effects will grow with a different power.' On an absolute QEI: 'one would expect that this can also be adapted to the non-minimally coupled field.'

H2 (Sec.3) four-dimensional (3+1) Minkowski space; the Conclusion says 'at least for massless fields in four-dimensional Minkowski space'

H8 (Sec.5.2 H-bounds, Thm 5.3/Cor 5.4) 4D Minkowski, fixed smearing function f, Hadamard vector states in D(H^{p/2}); q >= 3 is shown with ONE one-particle family, (70)-(72)

audits.lacked_data:
FO Sec.3 is a mathematical theorem, not a fit to data. Its only inputs are the free-field definitions and one explicit state. Every number re-derives exactly, and the printed looseness is conservative. So M's hypothesis finds no datum that moves the theorem on its own hypotheses. What the authors lacked in 2007 was coverage, not data:
(a) Massive and curved cases of the non-existence claim: still unproved. 1809.05047 repeats the N-copy argument 'even in Minkowski space', which supports the extension but does not prove it.
(b) An absolute version: FO say it is 'expected'. 1809.05047 asserts it was shown, but the math-ph/0611058 pages read here show only the difference form.
(c) The field-value dimension: FFKP (2023) show the negative energy is bought with large <:phi^2:>, and that an EFT field cutoff restores a class-dependent state-independent null bound. That does not change FO's theorem. It does limit the tree's 'the bound does not exist in that theory' to the theory without a cutoff.
For O1, the missing information is internal to the tree. f and c0 were never written down, and the threshold-x-ball accounting was never compared with the state's actual negative energy. Doing that moves the ratio from >= 1039.13 to 22.79 (xi = 1/4) and from >= 1803.55 to 102.02 (xi = 1/6).
audits.grade_evidence:
The theorem stands on FO's own hypotheses. FO (26), (28) and (29) re-derive exactly by sympy, and rho(0,0) < 0 for every xi > 0. FO's printed constants are conservative discrepancies (j 16x larger than needed, (34) loose by 2), not errors.
It is narrowed against the tree's use in three ways:
(i) overturn.py:287-289 and candidates.py:161-166 drop 'massless' and '4D Minkowski', which FO state as hypotheses. qeihps.py:86-89 keeps them.
(ii) candidates.py:170-173 applies the replacement bound to every xi > 0. FO's Theorem 4.2/4.3 cover only xi in [0,1/4], geodesic worldlines, difference type.
(iii) The O1 figures at ledger.py:1976-1980 are not FO's. They are the tree's own computation on FO's one-particle family, reproduced to 3e-6 only under a recovered accounting that the tree never states (f and c0 undefined). The same state's actual negative energy gives <H>/|E_neg| = 22.79 and 102.02. So as a statement about the compensating energy of FO's construction, the '>=' figures are contradicted by computation. 'Cannot be outrun' describes one state family, not a theorem.
The grade is not WRONG, because nothing in FO is refuted. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, because no measured datum enters.

(a) With H3 negated (xi < 0), sp.ask(rho00 < 0) returns False. At xi = 0, rho00 = 0. So the sign check depends on xi > 0.
