- It has no vacuity guard of its own. Mine closes that gap.
- The massive case is stated in a comment and not computed. The audit is honest about this: it grades massive and curved backgrounds as unproved, not as refuted.
- The slice scan in 7b covers t in [0,2] only. rho is even in t for real, isotropic h, so negative t adds nothing. Slices with t > 2 are not scanned, but by then the state has dispersed.

TWO SMALL CORRECTIONS TO THE AUDIT'S WORDING (neither moves the grade):
(1) FO's j > 6pi^2 rho_0/(xi kappa'^4) is consistent with their own printed, 16x weaker threshold -xi kappa^4 tau^4/(6pi^2 tau'^4). It is one dropped 2^4 carried forward, not two separate misprints, and every printed statement remains true.

If the premise is negated to M^2 + xi_BV h^2, the check that maps BS's -1/6 to BV's +1/6 fails. audits.lacked_data: Test of M's hypothesis for this result. The MuLan authors (2010-2013) lacked three things: (i) the O(alpha^3) QED term and a modern dispersive hadronic term; (ii) the CODATA 2018/2022 muon mass and the exact hbar; (iii) later lifetime input to the average. All three have since arrived. Eberhart et al. 2026 used them and obtained G_F = 1.16637859(59)e-5, 0.18 ppm below the tree's pin, which this pass reproduced to 2.5e-9. The computed moves are 9.0e-8 in v, 1.8e-7 in rho_EW and 3e-5 decades in the instanton exponent. That is evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: having the missing data did not change the conclusion. One datum is still lacking: an independent G_F at muon-decay precision. The EW-fit and CKM routes are about 1000 times less precise and disagree with G_mu by +2 and -3 sigma (2102.02825), so a BSM admixture in G_mu at the 1e-3 level is OPEN. Even a full 1e-3 admixture moves v by at most 3.8e-4 and the exponent by at most 0.12 decades. What does move the tree's printed digits is an unnamed hypothesis, not missing data: the tree-level / G_mu-scheme choice for v, lambda and alpha_W. The loop-level alternatives were available (Buttazzo 2013, PDG 2024). They move the S11 exponent by up to 6 decades and rho_EW's LO digits by about 25 % (illustrative), and no qualitative conclusion moves.

audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owners name the tree-level / G_mu scheme at higgs.py:262-275 and massform.py:2105-2110, state the exponent as scheme-dependent at the ~6-decade level, and relabel G_F's status as READ (PDG 2024 Table 1.1). To DATA-DEPENDENT: an independent G_F at muon-decay precision confirms a BSM admixture in G_mu, and some tree conclusion turns out to depend on v at the 1e-3 level (none was found). To WRONG: a contradiction of the tree relations at tree level, which sympy A1-A4 exclude, or a qualitative conclusion reversed by the scheme spread, which would take ~160 decades, not 6. Resolving the MuLan 0.27 ppm re-run discrepancy or the Buttazzo last digit would not change the grade.

audits.name: Israel (1966) / Lanczos (1924) thin-shell junction conditions: S_ab = -(1/8 pi)([K_ab] - h_ab [K]) across a non-null hypersurface; static spherical shell sigma = -(1/4 pi R)[sqrt f], p = (1/8 pi R)[(1-M/R)/sqrt f]; 5D brane form [K_ab] - h_ab[K] = -8 pi G_5 S_ab

source.located: W. Israel, Nuovo Cimento 44B (1966) 1; erratum 48B (1967) 463; K. Lanczos, Ann. Phys. (Leipzig) 74 (1924) 518. None of these is on arXiv. Read through exact restatements: (a) Poisson & Visser gr-qc/9506083, eqs (3)-(8) for the junction condition and the sign convention [K]=K+ - K-, (9)-(13) for the dynamic shell and conservation, (14)-(17) for V(a); it cites Sen 1924, Lanczos 1924 and Israel 1966 with the erratum as ref [7]. (b) Mars & Senovilla gr-qc/0201054, Sec. 5-6: the preliminary junction condition (Clarke-Dray), Theorem 9 (at non-null points the singular part of Riemann vanishes iff the second fundamental form is continuous), and eq (86) as 'the Israel conditions [24]'. (c) Shiromizu-Maeda-Sasaki gr-qc/9910076, eq (15), the 5D brane form, and eq (16) under Z2. (d) Davis hep-th/0208205, eq (10), the Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet generalisation, which reduces to Israel at alpha=0.

audits.published_statement: As restated by Poisson-Visser (gr-qc/9506083, eqs 3-8): 'Define [K_ij] = K_ij(+) - K_ij(-). Then R^mu_nu = diag([K^i_j],[K]) delta(eta) ... T^{mu nu} = S^{mu nu} delta(eta), with S^i_j = -(c^4/8 pi G)([K^i_j] - delta^i_j [K]) (6) ... S^i_j = diag(-sigma,p,p) (7) ... in spherical symmetry, G=c=1: sigma = -(1/4 pi)[K^theta_theta], p = +(1/8 pi)([K^tau_tau]+[K^theta_theta]) (8)'. It adds energy conservation, d(sigma A)/dtau + p dA/dtau = 0 (13). Mars-Senovilla (gr-qc/0201054), Thm 9 and eq (86): continuity of the first fundamental form is necessary and sufficient for a continuous metric; at non-null points the singular Riemann part vanishes iff K_ab is continuous; n^sigma[G_sigma lambda]=0 are 'the Israel conditions'. In 5D, Shiromizu-Maeda-Sasaki (gr-qc/9910076, eq 15): '[q_mu nu]=0, [K_mu nu] = -kappa_5^2 (S_mu nu - (1/3) q_mu nu S), [X] := X(+) - X(-)'. Taking the trace shows this is identical to the tree's [K_ab] - h_ab[K] = -8 pi G_5 S_ab.
published_hypotheses: H1: Einstein field equations on both sides (Einstein-Hilbert action; a bulk cosmological constant is allowed). With a Gauss-Bonnet term alpha != 0 the condition changes (Davis hep-th/0208205 eq 10); Israel is the alpha=0 case.
H2: The hypersurface is non-null (Mars-Senovilla Thm 9). Null shells need Barrabes-Israel 1991.
H3: First junction condition: the induced metric is the same from both sides, [h_ab]=0 (M-S eq 49; SMS eq 15).
H4: A thin, distributional (delta-function) surface layer of codimension one (PV eq 5).
H5: Sign convention [X] = X(+) - X(-), with the unit normal pointing from the - side to the + side (PV eq 3; SMS eq 15).
H6: C^2 metrics on each side, with well-defined one-sided limits of their derivatives at the surface.
H7: For the static spherical reduction: spherical symmetry, constant radius, sqrt f positive (areal radius increasing along the normal on both sides) and f > 0 at the shell.
H8: Dimension. Israel 1966 is 4D; the D-dimensional form follows from the D-dim Gauss-Codazzi equations (SMS eq 15 for 5D).
hypothesis_drift: latticectc.py:148-152 (O3_ANSWERED_BY: 'a braneworld whose bulk satisfies its field equations with Israel junction conditions at the brane'). H1 is DROPPED at this site. The bulk field equations are left unspecified, but the Israel form is the correct junction condition only for an Einstein(+Lambda) bulk. For an Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet bulk the correct condition is Davis eq (10). As phrased, O3's answer criterion therefore covers only braneworlds with an Einstein bulk. At latticectc.py:78-80 the condition carries G_5, which implies H1, so there is no drift there. The refusal itself (CODIM1_CTC_IS_BRANEWORLD_RESULT = False) is not affected.
latticectc.py:78-80: H8 ADDED (4D to 5D). This is legitimate: SMS eq 15 restates it exactly, and it is re-derived here from the trace identity [K] = kappa S/(D-2).

latticectc.py:78-80: H5 is not stated (the orientation of the normal and the meaning of [.] are not given). This is harmless: the owner's sign matches PV eq 6 and SMS eq 15, and the condition is used only as a named missing ingredient.

stability.py:16-25, 132-142: H3 and H7 are not stated. Both hold by construction: the shell sits at a common areal radius R; f_in = 1+2m/R > 1 and f_out = 1; the normal points to increasing r on both sides. This is not a drift in substance.

stability.py:16-25: M_in = -m < 0 is NOT a drift from Israel. The formalism is purely geometric and assumes no energy condition on either side (PV apply it to sigma<0 shells). It only needs the metric at r=R- to be Schwarzschild(-m), which is a claim about concentric.py's core.
wall.py:249-256, 483-499: no drift. Minkowski inside, Schwarzschild outside, static, thin, G=c=1, and x<1 so f_out>0. 'Lanczos' is the correct 1924 attribution.

stability.py:48, 65, 246: a wording discrepancy, not a junction drift. beta^2 = 0 with p held at p_0 != 0 (_ms_at) describes a shell at constant pressure, not dust (p=0), but the text calls it 'dust'. Recorded, not repaired. It moves no number.

audits.name: Special-relativistic causality: classical signals travel at <= c

source.located: No single paper. This is the textbook principle (Einstein 1905; Sommerfeld 1907 and Brillouin 1914 on the front velocity), and none of those three is on arXiv. READ at source instead, in two arXiv papers that state the principle and its hypotheses exactly. (a) Liberati, Sonego, Visser, gr-qc/0107091 (Ann. Phys. 298, 2002): p.1-4, 10-13 incl. fn 1, 2, 13; p.16 eq.3.12; p.18. (b) Geroch, 'Faster Than Light?', arXiv:1005.1614 (2010): p.1-13. Also READ: Scharnhorst hep-th/9810221 p.1-7, eq.(3) front velocity and eq.(10) n_perp(0).
source.via: gr-qc/0107091 and arXiv:1005.1614, both READ. Einstein 1905, Sommerfeld 1907 (Phys. Z. 8, 841) and Brillouin (1960 book) are NAMED-NOT-READ; they are cited through LSV refs [6],[8]-[12] and Fearn 0706.0553 p.2.

audits.published_statement: LSV 2002 abstract: 'special relativity can easily accommodate -- indeed, does not exclude -- faster-than-c signalling at the kinematical level. As far as causality is concerned, it is impossible to make statements of general validity, without specifying at least some features of the tachyonic propagation.' p.3-4: 'special relativity only requires, for its kinematical consistency, that there be an invariant speed' (invariant, not maximum). p.2: superluminal group velocities 'do not create any problem of principle, because the signal velocity still has c as an upper bound'. fn 2: signal velocity = front velocity. fn 13: with canonical kinetic terms 'the signal speed is c, regardless of whether the proper mass is positive, zero, or imaginary ... quantum mechanically the signal speed is also limited to c'. Geroch 2010 p.6-8: for 'Maxwell's equations, the Klein-Gordon equation, the neutrino or Dirac equations, the spin-s field equation and Einstein's equation -- the causal cone is precisely the future light cone'; 'solutions ... send signals that always lie within the causal cones'. p.10: the cones of other systems 'could very well lie outside the null cones of special relativity ... None of this would contradict our fundamental ideas about how physics is structured.'
published_hypotheses: H_SR (LSV p.4): homogeneity/isotropy, the relativity principle and pre-causality give an INVARIANT speed C, whose value is fixed by experiment. They give no MAXIMUM speed.

H_cone (Geroch p.6-8; LSV fn 13): signals stay inside the causal cone of each field's hyperbolizable equations. 'Signals <= c' holds exactly when every channel's cone lies inside the light cone. This is shown for Maxwell, KG (either sign of m^2), Dirac, spin-s and Einstein. It is a property of each matter equation, not of SR: a superluminal fluid with dp/drho > 1 is still well posed.
H_front (LSV fn 2; Scharnhorst eq.3; de Rham-Tolley eq.2.1): signal speed means the front velocity c/n(infinity), not the phase or group velocity.

H_vac (LSV fn 1; Scharnhorst p.6): c means light speed 'in unbounded empty space'. The Casimir (bounded) vacuum is argued to have front velocity > c under Kramers-Kronig plus passivity; this is contested (Fearn 2007) and unmeasurable.
H_caus (LSV p.12-18): paradoxes need superluminal signals that can go backwards in time in every frame. A speed fixed in a preferred frame can be stably causal.
hypothesis_drift: OVERSTATED (wording, not numbers): transit.py:44 'IDENTICAL, and provably so.' and transit.py:249 'ZERO, and provably.' The only proof in the tree is the identity advantage_over_light(D) = D/c - D/c (transit.py:145-146), which is 0 for every c (rederive 1a/1b). The physical content is H_cone+H_vac: no available channel beats D/c. The tree neither proves that nor names it, and it is not a theorem of SR (LSV p.3-4, 10; Geroch p.2, 10). The tree's own ledger.py:602-603 (D23) is accurate: 'ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION, not by measurement'.

DROPPED H_cone/H_vac: the canonical hypothesis 'flat spacetime, straight-line D, no metric engineering' (owner transit.py) is weaker than 'unbounded empty space'. The Scharnhorst Casimir vacuum is flat and unengineered, and is argued to have front velocity > c. transit.py:37-38 'through ordinary space at <= c' comes near H_vac but does not name it. COMPUTED effect (rederive 5): along the plates the group velocity is kpar/omega <= c exactly, so the gain is zero for D >> L. Perpendicular to the plates dc/c = 1.59e-32 at L = 1 um, so at most 5.3e-47 s per gap; that bound assumes the conducting plates are opaque, a named assumption. The printed 0.000 (transit.py:42) and tol 1e-9 (transit.py:346) are unaffected.
DECLARED, NOT COMPUTED: transit.py:153 BEATS_LIGHT = False is a constant. The selftest transit.py:345-348 checks an identity that cannot fail and a flag against itself, so neither tests H_cone.
NO DRIFT on H_front: the channel runs at exactly c (transit.py:145), the front-velocity upper bound. Any real channel is slower, so the idealisation errs toward the channel.
NO DRIFT at specthm.py:1184-1212 (R11): it inherits the transit.py flag under H_tele, with the same unnamed H_cone+H_vac.
NO DRIFT on curvature: 'flat spacetime' is named. Curved-space low-energy superluminality is unresolvable (de Rham-Tolley 2020).
OUT OF SCOPE: the canonical 'no-signalling forbids faster readout' is a separate key.

audits.lacked_data: The founders (Einstein 1905, Sommerfeld/Brillouin) had no QED vacuum polarization, no neutrino or GW timing, and no fast-light media. Later data narrowed what the principle means without producing a counter-instance. (a) Superluminal group velocities (2000) left the front velocity <= c, confirming the front/group distinction. (b) QED predicts front velocity > c in a bounded (Casimir) vacuum. That is theoretical, contested and unmeasurable, and COMPUTED here to give zero along-plate advantage and at most about 5e-47 s per micron gap. (c) The only apparent measured counter-instance, OPERA 2011, was instrumental. (d) GW170817 and OPERA 2012 extend H_cone to gravity (1e-15) and to neutrinos (1e-6 level). M's hypothesis for this result: the new data sharpened the hypotheses (front velocity, unbounded vacuum, canonical cones). In a narrowed sense M's suspicion is borne out: 'SR forbids faster-than-c signals' is inaccurate as a statement about SR (LSV, Geroch), because the limit lives in the field equations' cones.
audits.grade_evidence: The published principle holds under H_cone (all channels' characteristic cones inside the light cone; shown for Maxwell, KG, Dirac, spin-s and Einstein, but not a theorem of SR), H_vac (unbounded vacuum; flat spacetime alone is not enough) and H_front. Its only proof is the identity D/c - D/c (rederive 1a/1b), while its own ledger.py:602-603 D23 correctly says 'ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION'. So there is a dropped hypothesis, and the tree's class ('flat spacetime') is wider than the source's ('unbounded vacuum, canonical-cone fields'). NOT WRONG: there is no counterexample to the tree's conclusion. The one flat-spacetime exception (Scharnhorst) gives zero along-plate advantage and at most 5.3e-47 s per 1 um gap (computed). GW170817 and OPERA 2012 confirm the principle. NOT DATA-DEPENDENT: c is exact and cancels. The narrowing is in the wording, not in any printed number; BEATS_LIGHT = False and 0.000 stand for the EM channel in unbounded vacuum.

To WRONG: a measured, resolvable front velocity above c in unbounded flat vacuum for any field that can carry 2 bits (none known), or a macroscopic Scharnhorst channel. Along the plates one is excluded by the computed kpar/omega <= c; across plates only by the named opacity assumption. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a confirmed distance-scaling deviation of any sector's signal speed from c.

audits.name: Cauchy-Schwarz (Cauchy-Bunyakovsky) inequality in the form INT_0^tau_p f_tau^2 dtau >= (INT f_tau dtau)^2 / tau_p = 1/tau_p (formation.py transverse bound)

source.located: The integral inequality is Bunyakovsky 1859, 'Sur quelques inegalites concernant les integrales ordinaires et les integrales aux differences finies', Mem. Acad. Imp. Sci. St.-Petersbourg (VIIe ser.) t. I no. 9. The tree's form is exactly his special case (E), with psi = 1. The discrete form is Cauchy 1821 (Cours d'Analyse, Note II, Th. XVI eq. 30) and the quadratic-form proof is Schwarz 1885 (Acta Soc. Sci. Fenn. 15, 315-362). None of the three has an arXiv copy. Exact restatements: S. Kichenassamy, arXiv:2504.19543 (Ganita Bharati 42 (2020) 1-19), pp. 1, 7, 8; and Labropoulou et al., arXiv:2312.03478v2, pp. 1, 4, 6, 9.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2504.19543 (pp. 1-3, 5-9, 11-12 returned verbatim) and 2312.03478 (pp. 1-10, 12-16). Bunyakovsky 1859, Cauchy 1821 and Schwarz 1885 are NAMED-NOT-READ: they were read only as restated.

audits.published_statement: Bunyakovsky 1859, as restated in arXiv:2504.19543 pp. 1 and 7: (C) INT_{x0}^{X} phi^2 dx * INT_{x0}^{X} psi^2 dx > (INT_{x0}^{X} phi psi dx)^2, 'for continuous functions of one variable'. '(E): Special case of (C) where psi = 1: (INT_{x0}^{X} phi(x) dx)^2 < (X - x0) INT_{x0}^{X} phi(x)^2 dx.' Equality 'holds for psi(x) = lambda phi(x), where lambda is a constant ... also equality for X = x0'. Bunyakovsky writes < and > where we write <= and >=. Schwarz 1885 (p. 8) derives it from the positive-definite binary form INT (alpha phi + beta chi)^2. He assumes the integrals are absolutely convergent, and the inequality is strict unless phi/chi is constant. Modern form (2312.03478 p. 6): INT_a^b f g <= ||f||_2 ||g||_2, with equality iff f and g are proportional. Identity behind the equality case (2504.19543 p. 7): (f,g)^2 = (f,f)(g,g) - 1/2 INT INT (f(x)g(y) - f(y)g(x))^2 dx dy.
published_hypotheses: Bunyakovsky 1859: phi and psi are continuous functions of one real variable on a finite interval [x0, X] (restated in 2504.19543 p.1)
Equality case: psi = lambda phi (for form (E), phi constant), or X = x0 (2504.19543 p.7)
Schwarz 1885: the integrals of phi^2, phi chi and chi^2 converge absolutely; the inequality is strict when phi/chi is not identically constant (2504.19543 p.8)
Modern Hilbert-space form: f and g are in L^2 of the interval; form (E) needs a finite interval length (2312.03478 p.6)
No physical datum: this is a theorem of real analysis

source.located: arXiv gr-qc/0209075 v1 (21 Sep 2002), Anderson, Molina-Paris & Mottola, 'Linear Response, Validity of Semi-Classical Gravity, and the Stability of Flat Space' (LA-UR-02-5809); PRD 67, 024026 (2003) per the owner (journal ref not re-read here). audits.published_statement: Sec. III, p.10: 'We now state our stability criterion for the semi-classical approximation. A necessary condition for the validity of the large N semi-classical equations of motion (2.9) is that the linear response equations (3.4) should have no solutions with finite non-singular initial data for which any linearized gauge invariant scalar quantity grows without bound. Such a quantity must be constructed only from the linearized metric perturbation h_ab and its derivatives, and it must be invariant under allowed gauge transformations of the kind described by eq. (3.11).' Abstract: 'solutions to the semi-classical Einstein equations should be stable to linearized perturbations, in the sense that no gauge invariant perturbation should become unbounded in time.' Sec. V, p.13: 'If, for a given state and background geometry that solves the semi-classical equations, one or more solutions to the linear response equations experience unbounded growth in a gauge invariant sense, then the semi-classical approximation is not valid for that particular geometry, at least not for that particular state. Clearly this is a necessary, though perhaps not a sufficient condition for the validity of the approximation.'
published_hypotheses: P-H1 (p.8) the linear response equation comes from expanding the CTP effective action 'around a given semi-classical geometry g_ab that solves eq. (2.9)'; 'the first variation vanishes by (2.9)'; (p.9) the retarded correlator 'is evaluated in the background geometry of the leading order solution of the semi-classical equations (2.9)'

P-H2 large N: N non-interacting (free) quantum scalar fields of arbitrary mass and curvature coupling are the only matter; (2.9) is the large-N, RG-improved one-loop equation from the action (2.7) (pp.5-6)
P-H3 an in-state |in> (CTP in-in formalism); the verdict is specific to the state ('at least not for that particular state', p.13)
P-H4 renormalised Lambda, G_N, alpha, beta in (2.7)/(2.9); (3.4) needs no counterterms beyond those of (2.9)
P-H5 perturbations have finite non-singular initial data
P-H6 the growing quantity is a SCALAR, built ONLY from h_ab and its derivatives, and invariant under allowed gauge transformations (3.11)

P-H7 allowed gauge transformations: (3.11) for any X^a, EXCLUDING singular gauge transformations in the initial data, and excluding any (3.11) under which the action (2.7) is not invariant (boundary/surface terms) (pp.9-10)
P-H8 status: a NECESSARY condition; sufficiency explicitly left open ('perhaps not a sufficient', p.13)

B (sympy): for ARBITRARY X^a(t,x,y,z), the linearised Riemann tensor of the pure-gauge h_ab = d_aX_b + d_bX_a vanishes in all 256 components, while X_0 = t^2 gives h_00 = 4t, which grows without bound. So growth of components can be pure gauge, and the criterion is well posed only with AMM's restriction to gauge-invariant scalars. C (sympy): the toy x'' = -x, linearised about the non-solution x0 = -(t/2) sin t, carries a residual source r = cos t. Its response from zero initial data, t sin(t)/2, is unbounded although every homogeneous solution is bounded. So a boundedness verdict computed off a solution says nothing about the dynamics, which is why AMM's H1 matters and why the tree can refuse on it. D (z3): Valid -> NoGrowth entails Growth -> not Valid (unsat), does not entail NoGrowth -> Valid (a sat countermodel exists), and with NoGrowth undetermined both Valid and not-Valid are consistent. The tree's NOT EVALUABLE is therefore the correct logical status. Also run: linstab.py --selftest, 72 checks, 0 failed (includes the tree's own W1/W2 witnesses).

later_literature.ref: Hu, Roura & Verdaguer, 'Induced quantum metric fluctuations and the validity of semiclassical gravity', gr-qc/0402029 (2004; PRD 70, 044002)
later_literature.what: Reads AMM's criterion as the stability of the EXPECTATION VALUE of the quantised metric perturbation (Sec. IV.B, p.9) and argues it 'should be generalized'. The n-point correlation functions of h_ab (from n = 2) must also stay bounded, including INDUCED fluctuations driven by the noise kernel, and these cannot be recovered from the linearised semiclassical equation, only from the Einstein-Langevin equation. It also asks (p.8) how AMM's discarding of Planck-scale Fourier modes carries over to time-dependent backgrounds. It argues for, but does not prove, AMM's necessary-not-sufficient status, and it does not refute the criterion. Their own criterion also finds Minkowski stable (abstract). For the tree: a stronger criterion needs MORE (the noise kernel on a solution of (2.9)), so the semiclassical refusal (H1 unestablished) is unchanged.

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this item. The criterion is a DEFINITION with no numerical input (see data_at_publication), so no later measurement can move it. That is evidence AGAINST 'lacked data' here. What AMM lacked in 2002 was theory, not data: the stochastic-gravity treatment of induced metric fluctuations, published two years later (Hu-Roura-Verdaguer 2004), which argues the criterion is incomplete (necessary only). AMM had anticipated exactly that ('perhaps not a sufficient', p.13), so the later work extends the criterion rather than corrects it. Having that work does not change the tree's conclusion. The tree uses AMM only (i) as a necessary condition and (ii) to refuse a semiclassical verdict, because no demand configuration is shown to solve (2.9) (H1). A stronger criterion needs the same solution plus the noise kernel, so the refusal stands and becomes harder, not easier, to lift. The only change the source forces on the tree is scope: the classical radial theorem is not an evaluation of AMM's criterion.

There is no datum to move it, since it is a definition. The z3 check confirms that NOT EVALUABLE is the right logical status for a necessary condition. The later literature (Hu-Roura-Verdaguer 2004) extends the criterion without refuting it. The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS because the tree's USE covers more than the source's class and drops two clauses. (1) The h_ab-only clause of P-H6 and the singular-gauge exclusion of P-H7 appear nowhere in linstab.py (shown by search). (2) The AMM label is put on a classical Israel-shell radial stability theorem (linstab.py:32-33, 357-361; specthm R8). AMM's criterion is defined on (3.4), the linearisation of (2.9), where N free quantum scalars are the only matter, and a classical barotropic shell is outside that class. The canonical entry's 'not sufficient' strengthens AMM's 'perhaps not a sufficient' (p.13); the owner does not make that claim.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS, the owner would have to do one of two things. (a) Relabel the classical radial sector as classical linear stability NOT evaluated under AMM's criterion, and carry the h_ab-only and singular-gauge clauses. Or (b) show that (3.4), extended by classical shell matter, reduces at hbar -> 0 under P1-P4 to stability.py's shell equations, and that R(tau) is a gauge-invariant scalar built only from h_ab (plausible under Birkhoff, not shown here). To WRONG: only a computed contradiction inside AMM's own setting would do, for example a pure-gauge mode that passes AMM's allowed-gauge rule yet makes a gauge-invariant h_ab-scalar grow. None is known or shown. To OPEN: not applicable, because the source has been read and the checkable parts have been checked.

verifiers.reason:
This refutes part of the data claim. It does not refute the grade.

What holds:
- The criterion takes no numerical input. The Sec. III p.10 paragraph was re-read through alphaXiv and contains no measured parameter.
- The O(1)-coefficient input (p.14: "the exact finite number of order unity ... depends on both the matter theory and the values of the renormalized coefficients") belongs to the flat-space key, as the audit says.
- The HRV readings were checked at source and are accurate: p.9 "the stability criterion stated in Ref. [3] should be generalized" (n-point functions, induced fluctuations); p.8, the discarding of Planck-momentum Fourier modes is unclear for time-dependent backgrounds; the abstract says "flat space is stable".
- moves_conclusion = "no" follows.

What is refuted: the audit's row "none ... no datum" and its lacked_data sentence ("evidence AGAINST 'lacked data' here. What AMM lacked in 2002 was theory, not data") are contradicted at source. AMM p.7 (READ via alphaXiv; also found verbatim in the cached text layer) scope the criterion itself: "We are interested in this paper primarily in defining a validity and stability criterion of the semi-classical approximation at length scales l >> l_Pl". They justify the Planck-scale cutoff partly by a stated absence of data: "There is clearly no experimental basis for taking these solutions seriously ... we should regard the Planck scale as the physical UV cutoff which defines the extreme limit of possible validity of semi-classical gravity". The same framing appears on pp.4-5 ("no reliable results can be obtained from this approximation in the Planckian regime").

So the criterion carries a named hypothesis that rests on data being absent. Call it P-H9: scope l >> l_Pl, justified by EFT and by no experimental basis at the Planck scale. It is missing from both published_hypotheses and data_at_publication. Suggested row:
- value_then: no experimental data at the Planck scale.
- value_now: still none as of 2026. The Planck length is fixed by G, hbar and c, known far better than the order-of-magnitude scope needs.
- moves_conclusion: no. The data gap limits the criterion's domain; it does not falsify anything inside that domain.

Answer to M's hypothesis for this item, with evidence both ways: AMM did lack data, namely Planck-regime data, and said so themselves. That gap is still open, so no later measurement can have moved the criterion. Its effect is to restrict scope, which is a NARROWED-type limitation and not a refutation. Separately, AMM lacked the stochastic-gravity theory (HRV 2004). "Theory, not data" should read "theory, and Planck-scale data they explicitly name as absent, which is still absent".

Effect on the tree: linstab.py:125-126 carries the Planck-scale scope for the flat-space result only, not as a hypothesis of the criterion. The tree's D26 semiclassical refusal rests on H1 (no demand configuration shown to solve (2.9)), and the missing scope clause does not touch it. The criterion stands as stated, and the tree's use drifts in the ways the audit records.

Suggested correction: add P-H9 and the data-gap row, and replace "evidence AGAINST lacked data". No numbers change, and no value_then or value_now is wrong except the omission. Record written to d67/verify/data/gr-qc_0209075_criterion_datalens.json.

audits.published_statement: Sec. V: 'suggest that phi^2_max <~ (8 pi G_N |xi|)^-1 ... we will also argue that the quantum theory experiences breakdowns in its perturbative and semi-classical control in both frames when we allow for large field values. In the Einstein frame this breakdown happens in the scalar sector through a tower of irrelevant interactions that become important when phi^2 ~ (8 pi G_N xi)^-1; in the Jordan frame it occurs in the gravitational sector where the gravity path-integral becomes strongly coupled and looses its saddle-point approximation.' On the Jacobian: 'an explicit computation of the Jacobian would be necessary to make the following details exact but this is beyond the scope of this work'. On pNGB / shift-symmetric scalars: 'We do not disallow this possibility. Instead we offer the more conservative conclusion: when viewed as an EFT with field values bounded by |8 pi G_N xi phi^2| << 1, the mapping from Jordan frame to Einstein frame can also be done in the quantum theory.' Sec. V.B: 'our following arguments will apply for the xi > 0'. The constrained saddles are 'not true saddles'. 'as phibar^2 approaches (8 pi G_N xi)^-1 the action approaches zero'. Once the path integral is dominated by the one-loop term, 'We regard this as a manifestation of the breakdown of the semi-classical path-integral'. On xi < 0: 'the gravitational action moves to weaker coupling', the zero-mode integral 'diverges', and 'there is no natural reason to associate this field cutoff with the Planck scale'. Sec. I: 'This result provides a justification for our EFT requirement for xi >= 0. We do not have a similar argument for xi <= 0'.
published_hypotheses: P1 One free scalar, action (109) with V = 0 in the constrained analysis (112)-(113). The Einstein-frame expansion (106)-(107) is for n = 4.

P2 It is an ARGUMENT, not a theorem: the paper says 'suggest', 'argue' and 'points of evidence'. The Jacobian is not computed, and the Einstein-frame tower is dimensional analysis with M_cutoff ~ M_Planck.

P3 The Jordan-frame breakdown is argued for xi > 0 only. For xi < 0 the coupling weakens at large field, and the only signal left is that the zero-mode integral cannot be normalised; the paper gives no Planck-scale association for that case.

P4 Euclidean constrained instantons at a fixed constant zero mode, which are not true saddles. Compact boundary conditions, a bare Lambda > 0 (footnote 11), and the case analysed is Lambda_eff > 0. z_1-loop is only schematic.
P5 A shift-symmetric pNGB scalar with super-Planckian field values is explicitly left open ('We do not disallow this possibility').
P6 The conservative conclusion is |8 pi G xi phi^2| << 1. The '<~' form is an order-of-magnitude suggestion.
P7 Units hbar = c = 1 and G_N (not reduced). In the sign convention of (109) the effective Planck mass^2 goes as 1 - 8 pi G xi phi^2, so FFKP's xi < 0 is the Higgs-inflation sign.

SIGN OF xi DROPPED, at candidates.py:221, CANDIDATES at candidates.py:453-455, and ledger S4 at ledger.py:1558-1560. The Jordan-frame breakdown is argued only for xi > 0. THE PAPER'S OWN EXCEPTION DROPPED, at candidates.py:218-225: FFKP leave shift-symmetric scalars with super-Planckian field values open (P5). The tree presents the field bound as universal.
SCOPE P4 DROPPED, at candidates.py:222-223: the tree names none of the Euclidean, compact, bare Lambda > 0, constant zero mode and V = 0 conditions.

(3) sentence does not share that hypothesis ('when M^2_cutoff is Planckian or sub-Planckian ... the two metrics are close'). audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis was tested. Sec. V is an EFT argument, not a measurement or an extrapolation from data. Its only constant is G_N, which is unchanged from CODATA 2018 to 2022 and cancels in Planck units. What the authors lacked is not data but three things they name themselves: a computed Jacobian and one-loop factor, a measured xi, and an argument for xi < 0. Evidence that this matters: the sign of xi already changes the conclusion (A9-A10), and the paper explicitly leaves shift-symmetric scalars unexcluded. Evidence that it does not matter for the tree's xi > 0 use: every computable step re-derives exactly, and the breakdown at x -> 1 is exact in the constrained saddle (I -> 0, G_eff -> infinity, and the Einstein-frame map is singular). No datum was found that moves the xi > 0 conclusion.
audits.grade_evidence: Source READ (v1). All closed-form steps re-derive exactly (23/23 sympy checks), so there is no WRONG and no misprint. The one datum, G, has not moved. The grade is NARROWED because the tree applies the result to a larger class than the source supports. (1) The Jordan-frame breakdown is argued for xi > 0 only, and the trend is the opposite for xi < 0, while S4 and CANDIDATES carry no sign. (2) The tree states as fact what the paper offers as an argument with an uncomputed Jacobian. (3) FFKP's shift-symmetry exception is dropped. (4) 'Fails on the EFT field cutoff' is not carried by the field bound alone. Closure points with 8 pi G|xi|phi^2_max < 1 exist at l_UV between 1.0057 and 2.0919 l_P (check C2). The exclusion rests on the tree's own Planckian-momentum-cutoff hypothesis, and at the tree's N = 1 point the bound is exceeded by only a factor 1.17 (check C4). Under FFKP's conservative condition, eps << 1, closure needs l_UV <= 1.0468 l_P, so the tree's qualitative conclusion survives.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS for the tree's use: restrict S4 and the CANDIDATES row to xi > 0 and to scalars without shift symmetry, label the breakdown as FFKP's argument, and attribute the Planckian-momentum-cutoff exclusion to the tree, or to a source that proves it. Toward WRONG for the source: a computed Jacobian or a true-saddle analysis showing the xi > 0 path integral stays semiclassical as phibar^2 -> (8 pi G xi)^-1. Toward OPEN: reading the SciPost version shows a change to Sec. V. The later-literature search that was not run (quota) could narrow or contest the result further.

I refute the audit on two counts: its grade and one of its checks. The numbers the tree uses survive.

(1) The grade. The audit graded OPEN only because the source could not be read. It can be read now: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries returned arXiv:1808.08677v2, pp.1-10.
- The abstract (p.1) prints, word for word, the sentence the tree holds at massform.py:1381-1383: "A quarter of the trace anomaly gives a 23(1)(1)% contribution to the proton mass based on the sum rule, given 9(2)(1)% contribution from the u, d, and s quark scalar condensates". It gives quark and glue energy as 33(4)(4)% and 37(5)(4)% in MS-bar at mu = 2 GeV.
- p.5 prints "32(4)(4)% and 36(5)(4)% ... With the quark scalar condensate contribution of 9(2)(1)% [3], ... a quarter of the trace anomaly contributes 23(1)(1)% with N_f = 2 + 1". The tree's recorded abstract/p.5 divergence (massform.py:903, :1379-1380) is confirmed.
- The sum rule is eq. (2), M = <H_m> + <H_a>, with the gamma_m term inside H_a (eq. 4). The audit's H-TRACE-SR is therefore the source's own equation, not an assumption.
- The audit's own condition for STANDS ("If they read as held, the grade becomes STANDS for the tree's use") is met.
- Proton versus nucleon: <H> is defined over "the nucleon state |N>" (p.1), and the light sea quarks are degenerate (Table I). The calculation is in the isospin limit, so the paper has no proton/neutron difference to print. The tree's step from proton to nucleons, which it names itself, is covered by the source's isospin-limit hypothesis.
- Hypotheses to name: N_f = 2+1 (no charm in the sum rule), the isospin limit, and that the 9% is imported from ref. [3] (chiQCD 2016, arXiv:1511.09089, NOT READ), not computed in this paper. p.2 cites 46(7)(2) MeV for sigma_{u+d} from that reference. The implied sigma_s is 9% x 938.272 - 46 = 38.4 MeV; that is computed here, not read. None of these narrows what the tree uses.

(2) The encoding of check C2 is a toy, and it fails the vacuity guard.
- C2 treats the four shares as having independent errors and accepts any excess below 8.9 points. It would also accept a 5- or 8-point excess, so it cannot tell a rounding difference from a real inconsistency.
- In the source the sum is exact by construction. Eqs. (5) and (6) together with the normalisation x_q + x_g = 1 give exactly 1. The p.3 fractions 0.307 + 0.160 + 0.051 + 0.482 sum to exactly 1.000.
- From those READ fractions: H_E = 0.75(0.518 - 0.09) = 32.10% and H_g = 0.75 x 0.482 = 36.15%. Both reproduce p.5's 32 and 36. The construction then forces E + G = 68.25.
- The abstract's 33 + 37 = 70 lies outside the rounding tolerance of two integers (67.25 to 69.25). Getting 33 would need f_m <= 8.47%, and getting 37 would need x_g >= 0.4867.
- So the audit's statement that the abstract/p.5 difference is "arithmetically a rounding difference" is wrong. The abstract's quark and glue figures are inconsistent with the paper's own body and equations.
- Per the fluctuation.py precedent, this is a discrepancy between the abstract and the body, recorded and not repaired. It is not a refutation. The tree uses neither the 33/37 nor the 32/36 figures.

(3) The other checks hold.
- The re-run of the audit's script gives OVERALL PASS, reproduced exactly.
- A1-A5 and B are not vacuous. Negating the sum rule gives 25% for M = <H_a> and 91% for the misread form, not 23. A quote naming the nucleon fails A5.
- D and E are internal to the tree and correct: the chiQCD row, 9% against Ji's 17.04%, cannot move C2.

Grade the evidence supports: STANDS for the tree's use, with N_f = 2+1, the isospin limit and the imported-from-[3] provenance named. The abstract-versus-body divergence in quark and glue energy is recorded as a discrepancy in the source. The lattice computation itself is not reproduced here.

This pass got the source that the audit could not. alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries returned the full text of arXiv:1808.08677v2 (pp.1-10). It also returned its condensate input, arXiv:1511.09089v3, and two later papers, arXiv:2411.18402v2 and arXiv:2401.05496v3. The audit's OPEN rested only on the source being unread, so that basis is gone.

WHAT THE SOURCE CONFIRMS
(1) value_then, as held. The abstract (p.1) prints 33(4)(4)% quark energy and 37(5)(4)% glue energy (MS-bar, mu = 2 GeV). It prints 23(1)(1)% for a quarter of the trace anomaly "based on the sum rule, given 9(2)(1)%" from the u, d, s condensates. p.5 prints 32(4)(4)% and 36(5)(4)%. So the tree's abstract/p.5 divergence (massform.py:903) is confirmed at source. The four components sum to 102 in the abstract and 100 on p.5: a discrepancy between two printings, not an error.
(2) H-TRACE-SR is not just a named hypothesis. It is the source's own Eq.(2), M = <H_m> + <H_a>, with 1/4 <H_a> in Eq.(1). So 23% = (100-9)/4 = 22.75% is READ, not assumed. Row 2 therefore holds at source.
(3) The 9(2)(1)% is not computed in the 2018 paper. p.5 imports it from ref [3], which is arXiv:1511.09089. That paper gives sigma_piN = 45.9(7.4)(2.8) MeV and sigma_sN = 40.2(11.7)(3.5) MeV, and uses the physical 938 MeV as normaliser. Computed: 86.1 MeV is 9.18(1.48)(0.48)% of 938.27 MeV, or 8.97% of the lattice M = 960(13) MeV. Both round to 9. So row 1's "chiQCD's own inputs NOT READ" is now answered. Its sigma_piN of 45.9 sits between the Wilson-lattice value (~37) and Roy-Steiner (59.1), inside the FLAG tension, as the audit supposed. Not checked: whether chiQCD16 is itself one of the inputs to FLAG's Nf=2+1 average. If it is, the audit's "sits with the 2+1 average" is partly circular.
(4) The proton-to-nucleon drift is weaker than the audit frames it. The source uses degenerate light sea quarks (Table I, an isospin-symmetric setup) and defines <H> on the nucleon state |N> (p.1). Its proton value is therefore the isospin-symmetric nucleon value by construction. The isospin part is the source's own hypothesis, not something the tree added.
(5) moves_conclusion "No" follows in every row. rederive/1808.08677.py was re-run and reports OVERALL PASS.

WHAT THE AUDIT GOT WRONG
(a) The later-literature characterisation is wrong at source. The audit calls 2411.18402 "a direct lattice calculation of the anomaly term, where 1808.08677 inferred it". But its Eq.(3) is <H_a> = m_H - sigma_H, which is the same sum-rule inference. Wang et al. is arXiv:2401.05496 (PRD 109, 094504); the audit said the id was not obtained. It fixes its effective beta/2g from the nucleon sum rule using chiQCD16's <H_m> (Eqs.8-9). So its forward value is not independent either. Neither paper can move the grade to DATA-DEPENDENT in the way what_would_change_the_grade proposes. Only arXiv:2601.13070 (gradient flow) claims to test the sum rules, and it remains NOT READ.
(b) M's hypothesis can now be answered with evidence rather than "nothing either way". CLQCD 2411.18402v2 Table III, nucleon: 14 ensembles and 3,340 configurations against the 2018 paper's 4 ensembles. Its values:
- sigma_H = 94.2 MeV of m_N = 937.6 MeV, so a condensate share of 10.05(2.07)(0.23)%.
- <H_a> = 843.4 MeV, so a quarter anomaly of 22.49(0.58)(0.23)%.
These sit 0.34 and 0.33 combined sigma from 9(2)(1)% and 23(1)(1)%. The 10.05% is 3.4 of its own error below the 17.04% at which C2 would move. So later, larger data did not change the result. Caveat: same group and shared co-authors (Yang, Liu), so it is not fully independent. It is also still sum-rule based.

GRADE
Proposed STANDS for the tree's use. The audit's own criterion was "if they read as held, STANDS with proton->nucleon named", and the source reads as held. The hypotheses stay NAMED:
- Nf = 2+1, isospin-symmetric.
- The 9% is imported from 2016 sigma terms and carries about 17% relative error; the tree uses the central value only, as disclosed.
- The 23% is inferred from the sum rule, not measured.
The lattice computation itself cannot be reproduced here.

verifiers.reason:
The audit graded the result OPEN for one reason only: the source could not be read. That reason no longer holds. I read 1508.07161v1 in full through alphaXiv (answer_pdf_queries and get_paper_content with fullText=true). The audit set its own test: the grade becomes STANDS for the tree's use if the source confirms the abstract value, the Sec. VII value, the susceptibility definition and the input masses. The source meets that test, with the caveats below.

What is READ at source:
(1) Abstract, p.1, verbatim as the tree quotes it at massform.py:1119-1121: "width of only ~ 5 GeV ... maximum of the susceptibility of the Higgs condensate, with the result T_c = 159.5 ± 1.5 GeV".
(2) Sec. VII, p.8: "T_c = 159.6 ± 0.1 ± 1.5 GeV, where the first error is due to the statistical accuracy of the lattice computation and the second one is the estimated uncertainty of the effective theory approach [16, 26]". The tree's quote is exact except that it drops the citation brackets. The tree's page reference, p.8, is correct.
(3) Footnote 1 is verbatim.
(4) Sec. IV, p.4, eq.(15): the pseudocritical temperature is defined as the maximum of the susceptibility. The continuum limit is T_c = 159.58 ± 0.06 GeV (eq.(16), p.5). The crossover region is 157-162 GeV (pp.2, 7, 8).
(5) H2 and H3 are confirmed. The theory is a 3d SU(2)xU(1) + Higgs effective theory, matched to SM parameters (α_S(M_W), G_F, M_H, M_W, M_Z, M_top) "through a set of 1- and 2-loop matching relations [16]". Its accuracy is "~1% level" (p.2), which is 1.6 GeV at 159.6. The 1.5 GeV is "a conservative estimate of the uncertainty of the effective theory description".

Caveats found at source, which the grade should carry:
(a) H5 is only partly confirmed. The paper names which parameters enter the matching but prints no numeric values for them. The only mass it gives is m_H: "physical Higgs mass of 125 GeV", with ATLAS+CMS 125.1 ± 0.3 cited. So m_t, m_W and m_Z stay a NAMED hypothesis. The audit's input sensitivity is RECONSTRUCTED from a one-loop estimate and was never READ.
(b) There is a discrepancy inside the source that the audit missed. The audit calls the gap between the abstract and Sec. VII "0.067 sigma, the size of a rounding". It is not a rounding. The body's own figure is 159.58, which rounds to 159.6, not 159.5. The abstract's 159.5 ± 1.5 is the same figure the introduction (p.1) attributes to ref. [20] = 1404.3565 ("reported to be T_c = 159.5 ± 1.5 GeV"). p.9 attributes it the same way ("central value ... 159.5 GeV"). But 1404.3565, which I also READ, prints T_c = (159 ± 1) GeV in its abstract (p.1), its body (p.3) and its conclusions (p.4). This is a citation discrepancy of 0.5 GeV. Under M's rules it is recorded as a discrepancy, not a refutation. The value the tree uses sits inside every band and moves no verdict.
(c) One of the auditor's computations overstates its margin. "T* < T_c holds by 18.5 sigma" drops T*'s own ±2.3 GeV. That error is READ in the 1404.3565 abstract and on p.4, though the rederivation script had it as not read. The combined margin is 27.8/sqrt(1.5²+2.3²) = 10.1 sigma. The inequality is still decisive. The audit's other checks reproduce: the 1.851e15 K conversion, the 0.28 sigma agreement with 159 ± 1, and 0 failures in 12 checks when I re-ran them.

The audit's hypothesis drifts stay recorded against the tree, and nothing I found moves them:
- the sharp-threshold wording at massform.py:544 and in S11;
- the effective-theory systematic that is cited at massform.py:544-545 and not stated there;

I used F&T's own (5.14): at mu a = 1, N+1 = floor(u/C), so the bound is C^4 N^2 (N+1)^2 in place of u^4. I checked this against the p.11 page text. - Palasantzas, van Zwol and De Hosson (arXiv:0809.1779), pp. 1-6: the transition from the Casimir to the van der Waals regime sits at about 10-12% of lambda_p for gold. Experimentally it lies below 18 nm, and theory puts it at about 22 nm. 'For separations below 10 nm vdW forces dominate.' The 10 nm row is therefore in the van der Waals regime, not the ideal Casimir regime.

(3) The census datum is no longer OPEN. It is READ, and it is consistent with the tree. Svetovoy et al. (arXiv:2006.03849, 2020), p. 4: 'the shortest jump-to-contact distance was 12 nm for the AFM experiment'; high-precision experiments start between 40 and 150 nm; the surface force apparatus reached 'about 8.5 nm' for Au-Au; 'only two measurements exist at these short separations'. So '10 nm, state of the art' holds at order of magnitude. It is slightly generous to the apparatus: it is a force-measurement floor reached with a micrometre-scale sphere and plate, not a precision Casimir apparatus. One discrepancy between the sources is recorded, not resolved: the 2020 paper says the 8.5 nm SFA work was 'in vacuum', while the 2008 paper describes the same work (Tonck et al.) as Au-air-Au. The same 2020 paper (p. 3) adds that rough solids in contact stay about 10 nm apart, which makes the 0.1 nm 'atomic floor' even more generous than the audit says.

(4) One small correction, which does not move the grade. The audit's plasma-model Hamaker constant (2.10e-19 J) is below the values in the sources read: 2.6-4.5e-19 J, with 29.4e-20 J measured and 4.5e-19 J cited for Au-Au in arXiv:2006.03849 p. 17. The direction is unchanged, since every value is far below the ideal 433 J/m^2. The audit's '~14 nm transition' takes 10% of 137.8 nm; the paper's own figures are 12% of about 155 nm, with the transition observed below 18 nm. That is a gloss on the summary it had, not an error.

The grade is not STANDS, because the hypothesis the owner drops (gap > lambda_p) changes the printed density by about 9x at 10 nm, and continuum theory is invalid at 0.1 nm. It is not WRONG, because the drift only strengthens the conclusion 'not an engineering programme', and the census value is now corroborated at source. The audit should update its census row and its later_literature entries from NAMED-NOT-READ to READ, with the pages cited above.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: run the script myself, check whether it encodes the published statement or a toy of it, and run the vacuity guard
verifiers.reason:
RE-RUN. I copied the script to verify/rederive/ and ran it. It exits 0 with ALL PASS and gives the same numbers: b = 6.4551e20 m at 10 nm and 6.4551e16 m at 0.1 nm; 720/pi^2 = 72.951252, and its square root is 8.54115; eta = 0.9188 at 1 um, 0.5253 at 100 nm and 0.1099 at 10 nm (Drude 0.1093); the corrected b is 1.948e21 m, a factor of 3.017; H_eff = 2.102e-19 J; the core is 8630 AU. research/warp-drive was still git-clean afterwards. I checked the tree lines myself: achievable.py:134-135 and :417 apply casimir_density, docstring 'The measured effect', at 10 nm and 0.1 nm; scale.py:142-143 states the condition gap > lambda_p; tolman.py:1142 gives 9.0 eV (CITED). So the claim that H1 was dropped is READ in the tree, not inferred.

ENCODING. I checked the Lifshitz T=0 formula by hand. The variable change q = kappa_0, y = qd, zeta = xi d/c and the Fresnel coefficients r_TM = (eps y - kappa)/(eps y + kappa) and r_TE = (y - kappa)/(y + kappa), with kappa^2 = y^2 + (eps-1) zeta^2, are standard. With r = 1 the integral is -pi^4/180 / (4 pi^2) = -pi^2/720.
- Independent integrator (vacuity_and_encoding.py): it uses different variables (k_perp and zeta, a rectangular domain) and gives eta(1 um) = 0.9188 and eta(10 nm) = 0.1099.
- Plasma-model large-gap expansion, eta_E = 1 - 4 delta/d + (72/5)(delta/d)^2 with delta = c/omega_p: at 5 um it matches to 4e-6 (0.982733 vs 0.982737), and at 20 um to 1e-6.
- Non-retarded Hamaker: closed form H = (3 hbar omega_p / (4 sqrt2 pi)) * Int Li3((1+t^2)^-2) dt = 2.12e-19 J, matching the audit's 2.10e-19. My own first pass was off by a factor of 2; that was my slip, corrected.
So the integrator is the real Lifshitz T=0 result, not a toy.

VACUITY GUARD. I negated the dropped hypothesis by restoring H1: omega_p x 1e4 makes gold effectively a perfect conductor at 10 nm. The script's ratio then goes to 0.99912. The ~0.11 deficit therefore comes from d < lambda_p, not from the integrator. The script's 'eta < 1' check alone is weak, because it would pass at 0.999 as well. The information is in the magnitude, and the magnitude is guarded by the r = 1 self-check and the asymptotic match.

TWO OVER-STATEMENTS IN THE AUDIT. Both concern magnitude, not direction or grade.
(1) The audit says 'real gold gives 0.1099 of the ideal', but 0.1099 is plasma-model or Drude gold: free electrons only at 9.0 eV, with interband transitions omitted. That is an unnamed hypothesis, H4. Its own unread snippet value, H = 28e-20 J, is already 1.33 times the plasma-model H. A sensitivity check (interband_sensitivity.py) adds one Lorentz oscillator at 4 eV. This is a named toy, not a fit to gold. With the oscillator raising H to 2.4-3.2e-19 J, eta(10 nm) becomes 0.120-0.149: the ideal formula is 8.4x to 6.7x too large, not 9.1x, and the corridor factor falls from 3.02 to 2.89-2.59. The audit should write 'plasma-model gold; about 7-9x, model-dependent'.
(2) Encoding proxy. The audit scales casimir_density, an in-gap energy density, by the ratio of interaction energies per area. That is the same as using (E/A)/d. For ideal plates the two coincide; for dispersive plates they do not. I derived the in-gap <T00> from the gap Green's function. It has a uniform term, which is termwise no larger in magnitude than the ideal value since r^2 x/(1-r^2 x) <= x/(1-x). It also has a position-dependent term proportional to (y^2 - zeta^2)(r_TM + r_TE), and I proved r_TM >= -r_TE for eps >= 1, so that term is non-negative. Computed at the midpoint for plasma-model gold, it is less negative than the ideal value, and even positive. My derivation reproduces the perfect-conductor midpoint to 0.2% but only 3.4% at d/4, and I did not read it against a source (e.g. Sopova and Ford 2002, NAMED-NOT-READ). So the exact figure is unverified. What it does show is that the 0.1099 and 3.017 figures depend on the proxy. The direction holds, and if anything strengthens: real plates give a less negative density than the ideal row.

NET. The arithmetic reproduces. The finding that H1 was dropped (the ideal formula used below lambda_p and labelled MEASURED) stands, by READ tree lines plus a computation checked independently. The 0.1 nm row is below the 0.288 nm nearest-neighbour distance, outside continuum validity, as stated. Every correction increases the required corridor. The '10 nm state of the art' census datum stays OPEN: the audit correctly does not quote it as a READ. The grade NARROWED is supported. The audit's quantitative wording should be narrowed from 'real gold, 9.1x, factor 3.017' to 'plasma-model gold; about 6.7-9.1x depending on the interband response; corridor factor about 2.6-3.0; in-gap density proxy'. None of this reverses the direction or reaches WRONG or STANDS.

verifiers.reason:
The NARROWED grade survives, and so does its direction: the owner drops the perfect-conductor hypothesis, and every correction makes the corridor longer. Three data rows need correcting, and one needs a sharper statement. Two papers were READ at source this time through alphaXiv; in the audit's stage both were NAMED-NOT-READ.

(1) The census row ('10 nm state of the art'). This can move from OPEN-unread to READ and consistent, as of 2008. Palasantzas, van Zwol and De Hosson (arXiv:0809.1779), READ p.3-6: an AFM measured Au-Au down to about 12 nm, and 'Below 12 nm the cantilever jumps to contact' under ambient conditions. The paper restates Tonck et al. 1991 (SFA, Au-air-Au, d > 8.5 nm); that classic is NAMED-NOT-READ. The same paper (p.2) says that below 10 nm van der Waals forces dominate. The datum is still undated as a present-day state of the art. It does not move the conclusion.

(2) Gold hbar omega_p. The audit's value_now, 'About 8.9-9.0 eV', is incomplete. Svetovoy et al. (arXiv:0801.1384), READ p.1, 7, 15: real evaporated films have omega_p from 6.8 to 8.4 eV. The 9.0 eV value is a free-electron, single-crystal estimate (Lambrecht-Reynaud) that 'was largely adopted by the community'. 0809.1779 measured 7.9±0.2 eV. So the relevant spread is about 25%, not 1%. Recomputed here at 10 nm: the plasma-model ratio is 0.1099 at 9.0 eV, 0.0984 at 7.9 eV and 0.0865 at 6.8 eV, giving a corridor factor of 3.02, 3.19 and 3.40. The audit's 'moves_conclusion: No' still follows, but its reason (a 1% change) understates the range.

(3) The 'real gold' density at 10 nm. The audit states 0.1099 x ideal = 4.76e3 J/m^3 as what real gold gives. That figure is the pure plasma model, which leaves out interband transitions, and those matter at the characteristic frequency c/2d of about 10 eV. 0809.1779 measured A_H = (29.4±0.6)e-20 J in the regime below 18 nm (Lifshitz with measured optical data gives 26-32e-20 J). Extrapolated to 10 nm, E_pp/A = A_H/(12 pi d^2) gives about 0.18 x ideal, which is about 7.8e3 J/m^3 and a corridor factor of about 2.4. So 'off by about 9x' should read 'about 5.5-9x, depending on the optical model'. Every value is still below 1. The |r| <= 1 upper-bound argument in lacked_data holds for any passive identical plates, interband transitions included. It is therefore model-independent, and it answers M's hypothesis with evidence: the omitted datum strengthens the refusal and cannot rescue the apparatus.

(4) The non-retarded estimate at 0.1 nm. Recomputed with the Li3 form: A_H = 2.12e-19 J at 9.0 eV, against the audit's 2.10e-19 J; |E/A| = 0.563 J/m^2; a corridor of about 189 ly. These agree. With the measured A_H of 29.4e-20 J the corridor is about 160 ly. All of these are outside continuum validity, as the audit says.

Checks that hold as stated:
- Ideal densities 4.334e4 and 4.334e12 J/m^3.
- lambda_p = 137.76 nm.

- Corridor 1.948e21 m, a factor of 3.017.

- 8630 AU.

A minor framing point. The decisive scale for the perfect-conductor limit is the skin depth c/omega_p = 21.9 nm, not lambda_p. The leading correction goes as delta/d, and tolman.py:1508-1511, which the audit itself cites, warns against reading the crossover against lambda_p. The H1 finding is unaffected, because 10 nm is below both scales. The paper's measured transition (about 12% of lambda_p, below 18 nm) agrees with this.

None of this repairs anything in the tree. These are recorded discrepancies in the audit's data rows, not errors in achievable.py beyond the ones the audit already names.

audits.name: Borde, 'Topology change in classical general relativity' (arXiv:gr-qc/9406053v1, 30 Jun 1994), Sec. IX bullet 5 with Theorem 1 (Sec. IV): under causal compactness, topology change forces a closed timelike curve even if incomplete geodesics are admitted. So the 'singularity escape' fails, under the standard incomplete-geodesic definition.

source.located: arXiv:gr-qc/9406053v1. The quotation is in Sec. IX 'Concluding Comments', 5th misconception bullet, which reads 'Closed-universe topology change leads either to closed timelike curves or to a singularity'. The theorem behind it is Sec. IV Theorem 1, with the non-time-orientable variant in Sec. VII. Definitions are in Sec. II.A (interpolating spacetime: smooth Lorentz metric, S1 and S2 spacelike, compact timelike tube T), Sec. III.B (causal compactness: the closure of I(p) is compact for every p) and Sec. III.E (open universes, 'externally simple'). 'The very end of this paper', which the bullet points to, is IX.C (degenerate metrics). Tipler 1977 and Geroch 1967 are NAMED-NOT-READ: they are known here only as Borde restates them.
source.via: The full text was read from scratchpad/d67/src/gr-qc_9406053.txt (md5 17c67ada52d92fc44065246ef92fee8c, checked as C0). A sibling stage of this same run saved that file from alphaXiv get_paper_content(fullText=true) on arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9406053: 3,090 lines, the whole paper. This stage's own alphaXiv calls (get_paper_content, answer_pdf_queries, discover_papers) all returned 'quota exceeded', and the egress proxy refuses direct arxiv.org access (403). Sections II, III.B-E, IV, VII and IX were read in full. The passages the grade rests on are asserted verbatim by the script (C1, C2).

audits.published_statement:
Sec. IX, bullet 5: 'Closed-universe topology change leads either to closed timelike curves or to a singularity. The truth of this depends on the definition of a singularity. If the standard incomplete-geodesic definition is used, then this statement is not true: as long as the causal compactness condition is met, causality violations have to occur when the topology changes, even if incomplete geodesics are admitted. But, other definitions of a singularity may make the statement true: this is briefly discussed at the very end of this paper.'

Sec. IV: 'By "causality violation" it is meant that there is at least one closed timelike curve.'

Theorem 1: 'Let M be a (time-oriented) causally compact spacetime that interpolates between an initial surface S1 and a final surface S2. Suppose that M has no closed timelike curves. Then, M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1] (and, in particular, S1 is diffeomorphic to S2).'

Sec. VII: 'a causally compact spacetime that interpolates between non-empty boundaries S1 and S2 and which does not have closed timelike curves must (a) be diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1], and (b) hence be time-orientable.'

Abstract, on Theorem 3 (a different, dynamical theorem): 'it does not permit topology change even at the price of singularities (of the standard incomplete-geodesic variety)'.
published_hypotheses: M is a connected n-manifold with boundary S1 u S2 u T, where T is compact and possibly empty. M is smooth, Hausdorff and paracompact, and no dimension is assumed. If T is non-empty, it meets each S_i in that surface's boundary, the boundaries of S1 and S2 are diffeomorphic, and T is diffeomorphic to (boundary of S1) x [0,1] (Sec. II.A).

There is a SMOOTH, non-degenerate Lorentz metric in which S1 and S2 are spacelike and T is timelike (Sec. II.A). Borde names relaxing this as a way out: Sec. VIII (C^0 metrics) and IX.C (degenerate metrics).
Causal compactness: the closure of I(p) is compact for every p in M (Sec. III.B).
Theorem 1: M is time-oriented. Sec. VII extends the result to non-time-orientable metrics when S1 and S2 are both non-empty. When one boundary is empty, a non-time-orientable metric can avoid CTCs.

For open or asymptotically flat universes: M is the causally compact region of a larger 'externally simple' spacetime, i.e. outside that region the initial and final surfaces are diffeomorphic (Sec. III.E).
Topology change means S1 is not diffeomorphic to S2.
There is NO geodesic-completeness assumption.

'The escape fails' holds under the STANDARD incomplete-geodesic definition of singularity. Borde says 'other definitions of a singularity may make the statement true' and points to IX.C, metrics that degenerate at isolated points.
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED (a boolean with the definition condition stripped): create.py:187 SINGULARITY_ESCAPES = False keeps Borde's condition only in a code comment, '# Borde: not under the standard defn'. The check at create.py:289 prints 'accepting a singularity escapes it ... False' with no condition (C6b). Borde makes the claim conditional on the definition of a singularity (C1d, C1e). The other definition he points to is IX.C, degenerate metrics, which he says 'might well prove to be the correct approach'.

DROPPED (causal compactness left out of a prose summary): create.py:341-342 says 'causality violations occur even if incomplete geodesics are admitted' without 'as long as the causal compactness condition is met' (C6d). The rest of the file keeps the condition, at create.py:69-71, 200-202 and 290 (C6c). The condition matters because a singularity that removes a point or leaves a hole breaks causal compactness, and then IX.A applies (C4b: with causal compactness dropped, 'no CTC' is satisfiable). The tree keeps that case separate as specthm.py:1658-1665 W-create-ncc.

CONFLATED (a kinematic quote carrying a dynamical conclusion): index3.py:884 says 'accepting a singularity does NOT buy topology change' and supports it with the kinematic sentence. That sentence says only that a singularity does not AVOID a CTC. Kinematically, topology change can still be had, at the price of a CTC (Sec. III). The claim that topology change is not permitted even at the price of singularities is Theorem 3's (abstract; C1g), and Theorem 3 adds three conditions: dimension >= 3, the null generic condition (i) and the null convergence condition (ii).

DROPPED (from the sibling audit; re-confirmed here): the smooth, non-degenerate Lorentz metric. H_cc (specthm.py:614-615) and the GEROCH-BORDE fact (specthm.py:1838-1844) encode created & cc -> ctc without it. z3 finds a countermodel without 'smooth' (C4d), and the fact is entailed once smooth plus (time-oriented or non-empty boundaries) are added (C4e).

UNSTATED SCOPE: for a throat in open space, Theorem 1 requires the change to sit inside a causally compact region of an EXTERNALLY SIMPLE spacetime (Sec. III.E; C2d). An intra-universe handle, R^3 -> R^3 # S^1xS^2, meets this. That is the case create.py:24 describes ('R^3 IS SIMPLY CONNECTED AND A WORMHOLE IS NOT'). Creating a NEW asymptotic region is not compactly supported, and Theorem 1 as stated does not reach it. The 'created' literal at specthm.py:1651-1652 does not say which kind of throat is meant.

SCOPE TRANSFER (licensed; recorded): the quote sits under a closed-universe bullet (C1c), and the tree applies it to an open case. That transfer is licensed by Theorem 1 together with Sec. III.E, not by the bullet itself.
UNDER-CLAIM (harmless): specthm.py:1910 PROP_TEXT 'ctc' reads 'a closed causal curve'. Borde concludes a closed TIMELIKE curve (C1f), which is the stronger statement.

KEPT CORRECTLY: create.py:200-202 and create.py:65-66 are verbatim (C1a, C1b). 'Even if incomplete geodesics are admitted' follows from Theorem 1, which has no completeness hypothesis (C2a). The CTC is placed in the interpolating region, not at the seat (specthm.py:1655-1657, 1910-1911), as Theorem 1 places it.

rederivation.outcome:
33 of 33 checks agree, exit 0. Output is in rederive/gr-qc_9406053_causal-compactness.out.

C0: the source md5 matches.

C1a-h: the quotations are verbatim, and their context is confirmed: the closed-universe bullet header, the condition 'standard incomplete-geodesic definition', the caveat 'other definitions', CTC as the meaning of 'causality violation', and the abstract's 'even at the price of singularities' belonging to Theorem 3.

C2a-e: Theorem 1's statement has no completeness or geodesic hypothesis. Its hypotheses are time-oriented, causally compact, interpolating, and no CTC. The smooth-metric requirement and the externally-simple scope are both in the text.

C3 (sympy): the Clifton-Pohl torus g = 2dxdy/(x^2+y^2) mod (x,y)~2(x,y) is compact, and so causally compact by Borde III.C. On it, x = 1/(1-t), y = 0 is an affine null geodesic that crosses infinitely many fundamental domains before t = 1, so it is incomplete. Also on it, c(s) = 2^s(1,-1) is a smooth closed timelike curve with g(c',c') = -(ln 2)^2. So compactness and geodesic incompleteness coexist, and the CTC is present anyway. This illustrates the clause; it does not prove Theorem 1.

C4 (z3), on the propositional skeleton of Theorem 1 plus Sec. VII:
- tc & cc & smooth & to & ~ctc is UNSAT whether 'incomplete' is true or false.
- Dropping cc makes it SAT.
- S1 empty with a non-time-orientable metric makes ~ctc SAT.
- The tree's created & cc -> ctc is not entailed without 'smooth', and is entailed with it.

C5: every trapped flow line in 8,476 finite flows (N <= 5) closes up.

C6: the drifted tree sites are confirmed, read-only.

Not machine-checked: Theorem 1's full proof. It is infinite-dimensional (limit points of integral curves in a compact closure of I+(b)).

audits.lacked_data:
The result is a theorem in Lorentzian differential topology with no numerical input, so M's hypothesis does not bite here. Theorem 1 uses no field equation, no energy condition, no measured constant and no completeness assumption (C2a; Borde: 'purely kinematical'). No later datum can move it, and the empty data list is by inspection, not omission.

What came later was not data but relaxed hypotheses: degenerate (Morse) metrics (Dowker-Surya 1998; Garcia-Heveling 2022), which give topology change without CTCs. Borde anticipated this himself ('other definitions of a singularity may make the statement true'; IX.C). The 1994 conclusion is unchanged on its own terms. The later work changes only the reach of the tree's unconditional boolean, which is a hypothesis issue, not a data issue.
audits.grade_evidence:
Borde's statement STANDS as published:
- It is verbatim (C1a, C1b).
- Theorem 1 has no completeness hypothesis (C2a).
- The z3 skeleton is UNSAT with or without incompleteness (C4a, C4a').
- A compact, geodesically incomplete Lorentzian manifold with an explicit CTC exists (C3), so the clause is not vacuous.
- No datum enters.

The tree's use is narrower than it states, at four named sites:
1. create.py:187 and 289 make SINGULARITY_ESCAPES = False unconditional in the check output. Borde conditions it on the standard incomplete-geodesic definition and names degenerate-metric singularities (IX.C) as a way out. Garcia-Heveling realises that route without CTCs.

audits.lacked_data: G&O (2007) had no experimental datum to lack. The conjecture is about semiclassical QFT, and its 'data' are calculations of <T_kk>. Four things came later. (a) Urban-Olum 2010's fixed-background achronal violation (search summary only) would CONFIRM G&O's self-consistency requirement, not overturn it. (b) Flat-space ANEC was proved for interacting QFT (Faulkner et al., Hartman et al.), and Kontou-Olum proved achronal ANEC on curved backgrounds that obey NEC (restated in 1807.03808:328-333). Both strengthen the base without reaching the self-consistent case. (c) Wall 2010's GSL derivation gives conditional support. (d) GJW 2016's wormhole escapes by non-achronality, exactly as G&O's hypothesis allows. Evidence either way: no READ source reports a counterexample to the SELF-CONSISTENT achronal ANEC, and none proves it in general 4D. So M's hypothesis is not borne out for this result. Later work narrowed which version can hold (on the search summary, the fixed-background version fails) and added conditional support. Nothing found moves G&O's conclusion. The errors found are in the tree's USE of the result. The one computed error, the converse, cuts against M, not for M.

(1) 'No-wormhole results' is confined by READ restatements to wormholes joining disconnected regions, or short causality-violating ones (GJW p.2; 2309.10848). (2) The row called 'Graham & Olum's hypothesis' and marked OPEN drops self-consistency (anecscope.py:30-34,169-171; necindex.py:238). The tree does name the self-consistent version separately, and the evidence that the fixed-background version is violated is search-summary level only. (3) The achronality test used the converse of the conjugate-point theorem (achronal.py:41-43; obstruct.py:185-186). Rederive C2 shows that converse false. The error runs against M and is already struck. (4) 'Graham & Olum proved it in flat spacetime' is a misattribution: 1807.03808:325-327 credits Wald-Yurtsever 1991. (5) 'No proof' omits restricted and conditional proofs (Kontou-Olum; Wall via the GSL). composite.py's direction (past a conjugate point, chronal) agrees with C1. anecscope's scope finding stands as a conditional scope finding, as its owner already states (REFUTES_ACHRONAL_ANEC = False, NOT_RUN). The audit said the source was not reached. This pass did reach it: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries('0705.3193') returned 0705.3193v2, all 8 pages. Read at source, the source confirms NARROWED, so the grade is not refuted. It does change three parts of the audit's case.

What the source confirms:

(a) Condition 1 (p.2) is the SELF-CONSISTENT condition: "There is no self-consistent solution in semiclassical gravity in which ANEC is violated on a complete, achronal null geodesic." It is explicitly a conjecture ("We conjecture..."). G&O say they add self-consistency because "this approach avoids a potential violation due to the scale anomaly" (Sec. III). So the fixed-background "achronal ANEC" that anecscope.py:30-32 and :169-171 call "the hypothesis of Graham & Olum" is a mislabel, now READ at source rather than resting on a search summary. Two qualifications. The tree names the self-consistent version separately (anecscope.py:34-36, necindex.py:242). And G&O themselves report no actual fixed-background achronal violation, only the anomaly concern; Urban-Olum is still not read.

(b) The converse at achronal.py:41-43 ("achronal exactly up to its first conjugate point") and obstruct.py:185-186 is false at source. G&O Sec. II gives compactified Minkowski, a flat geodesic with no conjugate point that "returns infinitely often to x=y=z=0, and thus is chronal". Lemma 1 (p.3) runs only one way: obeys ANEC plus generic implies conjugate points, which implies chronal. Rederive C2 (b = 2/3 > L/2) is correct; I re-ran it and all 10 checks pass. One caveat for the record: G&O p.7 loosely says a chronal half-geodesic "would have such a conjugate point". Their own Sec. II example shows that does not hold in general, so it gives the tree's converse no cover.

(c) The misattribution is confirmed at source. G&O p.2 credits Wald & Yurtsever [5] with proving Condition 1 for a massless scalar in 1+1 dimensions. On p.3 G&O say their own proof "will have to await future work". So achronal.py:126-127 ("Graham & Olum proved it in flat spacetime in 2007") is wrong as written. This is an attribution discrepancy, not a refutation. It may be a garbled reference to Fewster-Olum-Pfenning, PRD 75 025007 (2007), which is G&O's ref. [3], an ANEC proof in a flat tube.

(d) The reach is confirmed. The abstract says "wormholes connecting different asymptotically flat regions". The WebSearch summary the audit used had dropped this qualifier. Theorem 1 (p.5) requires a simply-connected, asymptotically flat, globally hyperbolic spacetime that obeys the generic condition. G&O say outright that wormholes connecting a region to itself are not ruled out, citing Ford's long-throat counterexample. On CTCs, Theorem 2 (Tipler) concludes only null geodesic incompleteness, and Theorem 3 (Hawking) concludes no compactly generated Cauchy horizon.

Where the audit goes too far, against the tree:

(e) The 'WIDENED H5' drift misreads the tree. anecscope.py:32-33 says achronal ANEC "is what the topological-censorship and no-wormhole results actually use", and necindex.py:242 says "topological censorship uses it". These are claims about the PREMISE of those proofs, not about their reach, and G&O Sec. IV states exactly that: "The proofs of these theorems only require that ANEC hold on achronal geodesics". The real fault is narrower: the tree omits the theorems' extra hypotheses (simple connectedness, the generic condition, global hyperbolicity) and the inter-region-only reach. That is an omission of named hypotheses, not a widening of what is used. Grade-evidence item (1) should be restated that way.

(f) The audit's hypothesis list lacks the generic condition, which both Lemma 1 and every theorem need, and the semiclassical, sub-Planck regime restriction (p.3).

(g) The audit's what_would_change test is now settled, and in the NARROWED direction. The condition IS stated with self-consistency, and the wormhole implication is NOT proved for every wormhole. So the anecscope/necindex use does not move toward STANDS.

Items (b), (c) and the 'no proof' wording run against M or are discrepancies of attribution. None is a refutation of G&O, and nothing in the paper is shown wrong. read_status should be raised from READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT to READ for G&O. Notes are at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude-Method-Works/6d820e7d-6d3c-5ac7-8067-527dc14c2847/scratchpad/d67/verify/refute/0705.3193.notes.txt.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: copied rederive/0705.3193.py to verify/rederive/ and re-ran it, checked each encoding against what it claims to check, ran vacuity guards with the hypotheses negated, and added a stronger counterexample.
verifiers.reason:
My re-run reproduces the audit's result: ALL PASS, 10 checks, exit 0, under sympy and z3. As the script's docstring says, it does not test Graham & Olum's conjecture, which is not finite. It tests the conjugate-point and achronality lemma the tree used to apply G&O, plus the printed numbers. That is the right target for a NARROWED grade on how the tree uses the result.

Three of the 10 checks carry no real evidence:
- C1b (`(s2-s1)-(s2-s1)==0`) is a tautology.
- C2c (z3 on `Not((b-a)^2-(b-a)^2<=0)`) is also a tautology. The audit's line 'z3 proves the uncompactified line achronal' oversells it: the claim is true but trivial.
- C4a is bare arithmetic.

C1a hard-codes the far-side distance 2pi-s, a formula valid only on (pi, 2pi), but its pass condition expects the interval (pi, oo).

I re-did these checks properly in verify/rederive/0705.3193.vacuity.py, which passes all 10:
- V1 uses the true great-circle distance min(s, 2pi-s). z3 finds no chronal pair anywhere on the arc [0, pi] (unsat), so C1b now holds without the tautology. It also finds every point on (pi, 2pi) chronal relative to the pole.

Vacuity guards, all behaving correctly:
- Cylinder: with b-a <= L/2 there is no chronal pair (unsat), so chronality needs the wrap-around.
- Uncompactified line: unsat.
- C3 with the tidal term removed: J = lambda, so no conjugate point.

The audit's one load-bearing computation is C2, which refutes the converse stated at achronal.py:41-43 and inferred at obstruct.py:185-186. One could object that the flat cylinder is not simply connected, while the tree's corridor is R^4. To close that, I built a simply-connected counterexample: R x prolate spheroid with a=1, c=2.
- sympy gives the Gaussian curvature on the equator as 1/4.
- The Jacobi field along the equator is J = 2 sin(lambda/2), so the first conjugate point is at 2pi.
- For s in (pi, 2pi), the other way round the equator is shorter (2pi-s < s), so the null geodesic is chronal with no conjugate point (z3 sat, witness s=4).
- Oblate control: there the conjugate point comes before the half-equator, so it gives no counterexample.

So the general claim 'achronal EXACTLY up to its first conjugate point' is false in a simply-connected static spacetime too. I did not compute an asymptotically flat counterexample.

C1 is one instance of Hawking-Ellis 4.5.12, not a proof of it. The audit only claims agreement with composite.py:93-95, which is accurate. C3 is a toy with constant K, but it is adequate for its claim that a conjugate point needs no T_kk.

C4b's 547.76 AU against spec.py's 547.6 is a choice of constants. spec.py:65 gives f = 8.1923e13 m. It does not bear on G&O.

None of this moves the grade. The script supports items 3 and 4 of the grade evidence; items 1, 2 and 5 rest on the READ restatements, which this lens does not test. The conjecture itself stays OPEN and ungraded. Only the tree's use is NARROWED.
