audits.name: Whitehead: every point of a (non-degenerate) Lorentzian manifold has a convex normal neighbourhood

source.located: J.H.C. Whitehead, 'Convex regions in the geometry of paths', Quart. J. Math. Oxford 3 (1932) 33-42. It predates arXiv and has no arXiv copy. The consequence the tree needs is restated in Fewster & Smith gr-qc/0702056 p.7 ('As every point x in M has such a neighbourhood U_x', where 'such' means a globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood). FFKP 2309.10848 Sec. IV assumes it (a small sampling domain 'contained in a globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood of M').
source.via: Whitehead 1932 itself was not read. Attempts to reach it or a restatement all failed: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries x3, get_paper_content x1 and discover_papers x1 all returned 'alphaXiv assistant quota exceeded'; arxiv.org, export.arxiv.org, alphaxiv.org and semanticscholar through curl and WebFetch were refused by the egress proxy (403 / EGRESS_BLOCKED). What was READ came from texts cached in the scratchpad by earlier alphaXiv pulls: Fewster-Smith gr-qc/0702056 src/0702056.pages.txt:900-909 (p.7) and :1590-1593 (p.17, the definition of a small sampling domain), and FFKP 2309.10848 src/2309.10848.txt:2820-2821. Neither names Whitehead or states a regularity class, so neither restates Whitehead's theorem. Whitehead therefore stays NAMED-NOT-READ, which is also how the tree marks it (qeihps.py:105 'NAMED, not computed').

audits.published_statement: NOT READ at source (see source.via). The standard statement, NAMED-NOT-READ: on a manifold with an affine connection, every point has a neighbourhood U that is a normal neighbourhood of each of its points, and any two points of U are joined by a unique geodesic lying in U. The Levi-Civita connection of a sufficiently regular non-degenerate metric of any signature qualifies. The form READ in the tree's own sources is Fewster-Smith 0702056 p.7, stated for a globally hyperbolic M: 'every point x in M has such a neighbourhood U_x', where 'such' means a globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood.
published_hypotheses: An affine connection on a manifold; here, the Levi-Civita connection of the metric. The theorem does not depend on signature. [standard statement, NAMED-NOT-READ]

The connection must be regular on an OPEN NEIGHBOURHOOD of the point, enough for geodesics to be unique and the exponential map to be a local diffeomorphism. Classically this is a smooth or C^2 metric; later literature extends it to C^{1,1}, and below C^{1,1} it can fail. [NAMED-NOT-READ; the failure below C^{1,1} is rebuilt and machine-checked here, rederive section B]

The conclusion is local and gives no size: it asserts some neighbourhood exists, not a radius. [standard statement; the tree agrees, qeihps.py:115 calls the size a 'CAVEAT, not a hypothesis of the theorem']
The 'globally hyperbolic' qualifier that FFKP and FS need is NOT part of Whitehead's theorem. It is a further standard result, READ only as an uncited assertion in Fewster-Smith 0702056 p.7.
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED: the regularity hypothesis is dropped. qeihps.py:103-105 and :436-439 test only f(0) > 0 and r(0) > 0, i.e. non-degeneracy at a single point; the 'MET LOCALLY' verdict at qeihps.py:439 is computed from (f0 > 0 and r0 > 0) alone. The theorem needs a connection that is C^{1,1} or better on an open neighbourhood. That the point test is not enough is computed in rederive B: the metric -f dt^2 + dl^2 with f(l) = 1/(1+|l|^(3/2)) is non-degenerate at l = 0 (f(0) = 1) and C^1 but not C^{1,1}, and it has two geodesics, l = 0 and l = s^4/256, with the same initial point and velocity, so exp_p is undefined. The tree itself records TAYLOR_RADIUS_OF_CONVERGENCE_PROVED = False (qeihps.py:338): off the throat, HPS's metric is known only as a Taylor jet plus HPS's numerical solution. Regularity on a neighbourhood is therefore a hypothesis the tree does not state; it is plausible for HPS's smooth ODE solution but is not established in the tree.

ADDED BY FOLDING: Whitehead is made to deliver qualifiers it does not state. qeihps.py:101-105 meets FFKP's requirement ('M globally hyperbolic, f supported in a small sampling domain: an open set inside a globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood, one hyperbolic chart') by citing Whitehead alone. Whitehead supplies convexity and normality only. Global hyperbolicity of a small convex normal neighbourhood is a separate result (asserted without citation in FS 0702056 p.7, READ). The hyperbolic-chart clause (FS p.17 and FFKP 2309.10848 Sec. IV.B, both READ) is not addressed at these lines. The 'LOCALLY' in the verdict is consistent with FS p.7, which says Hadamard states restrict to open globally hyperbolic subsets, so 'M globally hyperbolic' can be met by restricting M; but that route does not come from Whitehead.

ADDED, harmless: qeihps.py:103 and the canonical hypothesis say 'Lorentzian', but Whitehead's theorem holds for any affine connection regardless of signature [standard statement, NAMED-NOT-READ]. This does not narrow anything.

A SIZE CLAIM is attached to the neighbourhood at qeihps.py:114-117: 'the convex normal neighbourhood about the throat is set by a curvature radius of 0.0243 l_P, so any sampling domain it admits is sub-Planckian'. Whitehead states no size, and the tree correctly labels this a CAVEAT. Rederive D computes the following. The throat sphere is totally geodesic with sectional curvature 1/r0^2, so angular geodesics reach conjugate points at pi r0 = 0.0763 l_P; that bounds the neighbourhood's angular extent from above. But the tidal tensor R^a_{tbt} vanishes exactly on the throat worldline l = 0 for all t; this uses only f'(0) = f''(0) = r'(0) = 0, which are HPS's data (9). So nothing computed bounds the time extent of a worldline sampling domain by r0. 'Any sampling domain ... sub-Planckian' is established here for the angular directions only. This is a discrepancy of scope: recorded, not repaired, and not a refutation, since a convex neighbourhood long in t is not constructed here either.

data_at_publication.value_now: 1/sqrt(540 pi) = 0.0242789 l_P (sympy exact, agrees). Over HPS's range -1 <= L < 0, r0 lies in (0, 0.0297354] l_P.
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: no: the metric stays non-degenerate for every L in -1 <= L < 0. It degenerates only at the excluded endpoint L = 0, where r0 = 0. The size caveat scales with r0 and stays sub-Planckian over the whole range.

rederivation.outcome: All 17 checks pass. (A) The tree's pointwise premise agrees: r0 = 1/sqrt(540 pi) = 0.0242789 l_P, f(0) = 0.513417, det g at the throat = -f0 r0^4 = -1.784e-7 (non-zero), and the metric is non-degenerate on all of -1 <= L < 0. (B) Pointwise non-degeneracy is not sufficient: the C^{1,1/2} Lorentzian 1+1 metric f = 1/(1+|l|^{3/2}), with f(0) = 1, has two geodesics l = 0 and l = s^4/256 with identical initial data (sympy exact), so no normal neighbourhood exists. The regularity hypothesis the tree drops is load-bearing. (C) On the HPS fourth-order throat jet, which is a smooth metric, all 64 Christoffel symbols vanish at the throat point (theta = pi/2). Whitehead's convexity lemma, d^2|x|^2/ds^2 = 2|x'|^2 - 2 x_k G^k_ij x'^i x'^j > 0, holds on the coordinate ball |x| < 0.7177 r0 = 0.01743 l_P (eps * sup ||G||_F < 1). 60 RK4 geodesics spot-check it (minimum ratio 1.75 > 0). This is a lower bound, and it checks the lemma, not the full theorem. (D) The throat sphere is totally geodesic with sectional curvature exactly 1/r0^2 (conjugate distance pi r0 = 0.0763 l_P), and the tidal tensor R^a_{tbt} is exactly 0 on l = 0. (E) A read-only import of qeihps shows that, as seated, the FFKP 'domain' row is MET LOCALLY and FFKP's status is OPEN. Relabelling the row as a named conditional keeps OPEN. Relabelling it a bare NOT-ESTABLISHED flips qei_status to REFUSED, because qei_status maps every non-MET form row to REFUSED. The throat verdict is NOT A TEST either way.

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for Whitehead 1932: the theorem is pure differential geometry and takes no physical input. No measured constant or observation enters it, so no later data can move it, and nothing the author lacked bears on it. What has changed since 1932 is knowledge about regularity, not data: the theorem was later shown to hold down to C^{1,1} metrics and to fail below that (the Hartman-Wintner mechanism, rebuilt and machine-checked here in section B). That narrows the tree's use of the theorem, not the theorem itself. qeihps.py checks non-degeneracy at one point, and the tree does not establish that HPS's metric is regular on a neighbourhood of the throat (TAYLOR_RADIUS_OF_CONVERGENCE_PROVED = False, qeihps.py:338). The data the tree does use, f(0) = e^(-2/3) and r0 = 0.0242789 l_P, are model inputs; they are re-derived exactly here, and no admissible value in HPS's range -1 <= L < 0 changes non-degeneracy. So for this result the evidence runs entirely against M's hypothesis, because the theorem has no data input. The limitation that does exist is the regularity hypothesis, which belongs to the tree's use and is named here.
audits.grade_evidence:
Nothing computed here contradicts the theorem; its convexity lemma is verified on the HPS throat jet (rederive C). The tree's use narrows it in three ways.

(1) The regularity hypothesis is dropped. The tree rests 'MET LOCALLY' (qeihps.py:103-105, 439) on f(0) > 0 and r(0) > 0 at a single point. Rederive B builds a Lorentzian metric that is non-degenerate at the point (class C^{1,1/2}) and has two geodesics with the same initial data, so non-degeneracy at a point does not give a normal neighbourhood. The tree's own flag TAYLOR_RADIUS_OF_CONVERGENCE_PROVED = False (qeihps.py:338) leaves the regularity of HPS's metric on a neighbourhood unproved.

(2) Whitehead does not supply the 'globally hyperbolic' qualifier or the hyperbolic chart that FFKP require (FFKP 2309.10848 Sec. IV and FS 0702056 p.17, both READ). FS p.7 asserts the globally hyperbolic version without a citation.

(3) A discrepancy of scope, not a refutation: the caveat 'any sampling domain it admits is sub-Planckian' (qeihps.py:115-117) is bounded by computation only in the angular directions (conjugate distance pi r0 = 0.0763 l_P). On the throat worldline the tidal tensor is exactly zero.

Why not WRONG: nothing in the theorem is refuted, and the downstream FFKP status stays OPEN if the row is relabelled as a named conditional (rederive E). Whitehead 1932 itself was NOT READ, because the alphaXiv quota was exhausted and arXiv is blocked by the egress proxy. The grade therefore rests on the tree's own lines, the READ FS and FFKP texts, and the machine checks, not on the unread source.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS, the tree would need two things. First, a proof, or a theorem READ at source, that HPS's metric is C^{1,1} or better on an open neighbourhood of the throat: for example a proved Taylor radius (TAYLOR_RADIUS_OF_CONVERGENCE_PROVED becoming True) or an ODE regularity argument for HPS's system. Second, a READ citation for the globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood and for the hyperbolic chart (for example Minguzzi's 2019 Living Review, read at source), with the owner line citing these rather than Whitehead alone. To OPEN: if the audit is held to require reading Whitehead 1932, or a restatement that names it, the source-reading half is open, because neither was reachable in this session (alphaXiv quota, egress block); the drift findings would still stand. Nothing foreseeable moves it to WRONG: the theorem has no data input and the lemma checks agree.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (either direction): whitehead-convex-normal-neighbourhoods, audited NARROWED
verifiers.reason:
The NARROWED grade rests mainly on one claim: that the tree drops a regularity hypothesis it cannot meet. The evidence below meets that hypothesis. Two other parts of the audit misstate their sources. The alphaXiv quota that blocked the auditor was available in this session, so the papers were READ at source.

(1) The regularity hypothesis is met. It is computed here, not merely plausible. HPS gr-qc/9701064 was READ at source (pp.4-7). Its tt and theta-theta field equations (5) and (7) are fourth order, and the coefficients of (f''''/f, r''''/r) form the matrix [[16+16 ln f, -64-32 ln f], [-16-8 ln f, 16 ln f]]. Its determinant is -256(3 ln f + 4) (sympy). That is non-zero over HPS's whole range -1 <= ln f(0) < 0, and it is exactly the (3L+4) denominator in the tree's own formulas at qeihps.py:1112-1115. Solving the READ equations at the throat with data (9) reproduces the tree's f''''(0)/f(0) = 259200 pi^2(-L-1)/(L(3L+4)) and r''''(0)/r(0) = 129600 pi^2(2-L^2)/(L^2(3L+4)) exactly (script: verify/refute/whitehead-hps-regularity.py). So HPS's system is a normal-form ODE x' = F(x), with F C^infinity (indeed real-analytic) wherever f > 0, r > 0 and 3 ln f + 4 != 0. That open set contains the throat data. Picard-Lindelof (NAMED, standard) plus the usual bootstrap then makes f and r C^infinity on an open interval of l about 0, so metric (2) is smooth on a neighbourhood of the throat.
- The auditor's counterexample is correct as mathematics but does not apply here. It is a C^{1,1/2} metric with two geodesics from the same initial data; I re-checked it: l = s^4/256, l'' = (3/4)E^2 l^{1/2}, norm -1 conserved. HPS's metric is not of that class.
- TAYLOR_RADIUS_OF_CONVERGENCE_PROVED = False concerns the size of a convergence radius (analyticity, quantified). It is not evidence that the metric is irregular on a neighbourhood. Reading it that way was an overreach.
- What remains is a documentation discrepancy: the owner line tests only f(0) > 0 and r(0) > 0 and does not state the regularity, which nonetheless holds. That is not a narrowing of what the result delivers.

(2) The globally hyperbolic qualifier is now READ at source, no longer only an uncited assertion. Minguzzi arXiv:1308.6675 (Monatsh. Math. 2015) was READ:
- Abstract, p.1: 'arbitrarily small globally hyperbolic convex normal neighborhoods do exist.'
- Lemma 4, p.53: S(c1', c2') is 'strictly convex normal and globally hyperbolic', for a C^{1,1} Lorentzian metric.
- Theorem 4, p.12: the convex normal set can be taken to be a coordinate ball B(p, delta) in any chart.
The hyperbolic-chart clause is FFKP 2309.10848 Sec. IV.B: d/dx^0 future-pointing timelike, and c|u^0| bounds the spatial components of causal vectors. In the static chart near the throat, d/dt is timelike because f > 0, and on a compact ball where f and r are bounded away from 0 the bound follows from the causal inequality f (u^t)^2 >= (u^l)^2 + r^2|u_angular|^2. I derived that bound by hand; it is not machine-checked.
- So the qualifiers FFKP need are met, by results other than Whitehead's. Citing Whitehead alone at qeihps.py:101-105 is an attribution discrepancy, to be recorded and not repaired. The conclusion 'MET LOCALLY' it supports is true.

(3) The audit misstates Whitehead's own hypothesis. It says the classical theorem needs a smooth or C^2 metric and that later work extended it to C^{1,1}. Two later papers READ at source say otherwise:
- Kunzinger-Steinbauer-Stojkovic arXiv:1306.4776 p.2: in Whitehead's paper the Gamma^k_ij 'are merely supposed to be Lipschitz', and '[11, Sec. 3]' proves that every point has a simple region.
- Minguzzi 1308.6675 p.9: 'The local injectivity of the exponential map for Lipschitz connections was proved by Whitehead [62].'
What the later work added at C^{1,1} is that exp_p has a Lipschitz inverse (it is bi-Lipschitz) and that totally normal / convex normal neighbourhoods exist. The regularity floor itself was already Whitehead's. Whitehead 1932 stays NAMED-NOT-READ, but it is now restated, and named, in two READ sources. That also removes the audit's own 'to OPEN' route, which relied on the claim that nothing restating Whitehead could be reached.

(4) The size caveat at qeihps.py:114-117 stays as the audit records it. It is bounded only in the angular directions, by the conjugate distance pi r0 = 0.0763 l_P, and the tidal tensor is zero on the throat worldline. This is a scope discrepancy in something the tree itself labels a CAVEAT, not a hypothesis. It does not bear on the grade.

Net: the result as the tree uses it (a globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood exists about the throat, so the FFKP domain row is MET LOCALLY) is supported by computation plus sources READ at source. The remaining issues are discrepancies (attribution to Whitehead alone; an unstated but satisfied regularity premise; the angular-only size bound), not limitations on the result. That gives STANDS, with those discrepancies recorded. It is not WRONG: nothing is refuted. The auditor's checks A-E all re-run and pass (17/17). One small note on check C: its sup ||Gamma||_F is taken over a 161x161 grid, not a rigorous bound.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: copied the script, re-ran it, checked its encoding against the published statement, and ran vacuity guards on sections B and C
verifiers.reason:
The audit holds up under re-running, and the NARROWED grade stands. There are two precision notes and one caveat, and none of them is a refutation.

RE-RUN. I copied the script to verify/rederive/wh.py and ran it: all 17 checks pass, with the same figures the audit reports. r0 = 1/sqrt(540 pi) = 0.0242789 l_P, f(0) = 0.513417, det g = -1.784e-7. The C^{1,1/2} metric has two geodesics with the same initial data. All Christoffel symbols vanish at the throat. eps = 0.7177 r0, and the RK4 minimum ratio is 1.7512. The throat sphere has curvature 1/r0^2, and the tidal tensor on l = 0 is 0. Section E gives OPEN as seated, OPEN under the conditional relabel, and REFUSED under a bare NOT-ESTABLISHED. Section E imports qeihps with dont_write_bytecode, and the existing qeihps .pyc files predate this run, so nothing was written to the tree.

ENCODING.
- (B) is a correct toy counterexample, not an HPS statement. In the metric -f dt^2 + dl^2 the geodesic equation is l'' = (E^2/2) d(1/f)/dl. l = s^4/256 solves it, and I checked independently that it also satisfies the energy constraint l'^2 = l^{3/2}, so it is a genuine unit timelike geodesic. It shares its initial data with l = 0. B therefore shows that non-degeneracy at a single point does not by itself give a normal neighbourhood. It does not show that HPS's metric is irregular.
- (C) checks Whitehead's convexity lemma, d^2|x|^2/ds^2 > 0 under the bound eps * sup||Gamma||_F < 1. The bound is valid because the Frobenius norm bounds the operator norm. It is checked on the 4th-order throat jet, not on HPS's actual metric, and it covers only the convex-sphere ingredient, not unique joining geodesics or exp being a diffeomorphism. The audit says this itself ('checks the lemma, not the full theorem').
- (D)'s formulas check out. The sectional-curvature expression is R^psi_{phi psi phi} g_psipsi/(g_psipsi g_phiphi), and Rm[a,0,b,0] is R^a_{tbt}.

VACUITY.
- (B) discriminates. With 1/f = 1 + |l|^p, a non-zero power-law solution with the same initial data exists for p = 3/2, 7/4 and 19/10. For p = 2, 5/2 and 3 the right-hand side is Lipschitz at 0, so the solution is unique (Picard-Lindelof). The non-uniqueness appears exactly below C^{1,1}.
- (C) discriminates. Evaluating the same convexity quantity at 2000 random points and directions per shell on the HPS jet gives a minimum of +1.34 for |x| in [0.05, 0.70] r0, -0.16 in [0.70, 1.20], and -53.7 in [1.2, 2.0]. The check does fail outside the ball, and the Frobenius bound of 0.718 r0 sits close to where convexity actually fails. A comparator with higher curvature (r = 1 + 50 l^2) already fails in [0.2, 0.7].

PRECISION NOTES, not refutations.
(i) The grade evidence cites TAYLOR_RADIUS_OF_CONVERGENCE_PROVED = False (qeihps.py:338) as leaving regularity unproved. That flag is about convergence of the Taylor series, i.e. analyticity, not C^{1,1}: a smooth metric that is not analytic still satisfies Whitehead. Narrowing (1) is therefore correctly an unstated regularity hypothesis about HPS's ODE solution, plausible but not established in the tree. It is not evidence that the metric is irregular, and the flag supports it only indirectly.
(ii) Section D's 'no conjugate points for any duration' along the throat worldline is a linearised (Jacobi-field) statement. Nonlinear refocusing of nearby geodesics in the l^4 well is not examined. The audit does not claim that a convex neighbourhood long in t exists, so the stated scope finding stands as worded.

READING. I read the cached passages at source. FS 0702056 p.7 (lines 898-909) and p.17 (lines 1588-1594), and FFKP 2309.10848 (lines 2818-2822), match the quotes. Neither names Whitehead (grep finds no match), which is consistent with marking Whitehead 1932 NAMED-NOT-READ. Narrowing (2) is confirmed: FS and FFKP require a globally hyperbolic convex normal neighbourhood and a single hyperbolic chart, and qeihps.py:101-105 meets both by citing Whitehead alone.

GRADE. NARROWED is what the evidence supports. The source-reading half stays OPEN until Whitehead 1932, or a restatement that names it, is read, as the audit's own what_would_change_the_grade already says.

verifiers.reason:
I checked every data row against HPS's own text. All of them hold, and none of the moves_conclusion verdicts is wrong.

Row 1. HPS p.7 eq. (9) gives '-1 <= ln f(0) < 0', and the plotted solution has 'ln f(0) = -2/3'. HPS p.6 requires f(0) > 0. e^(-2/3) = 0.513417. The verdict 'moves_conclusion: no' follows, because f(0) = e^L > 0 for every real L.

Row 2. HPS p.4 gives 'K^2 = 1/(5760 pi)' and eq. (9) gives r(0) = sqrt(-16K^2 ln f(0)). I re-derived this independently from HPS's ll-equation (6) at l = 0 with every derivative from first to third set to zero. It gives r0^2 = -L/(360 pi), which is 1/(540 pi) at L = -2/3, so r0 = 0.0242789 l_P. That agrees with HPS's 'r(0) ≈ 0.02 l_P' on p.7. At L = -1, r0 = 0.0297354 l_P. The metric is therefore non-degenerate at the throat over the whole range -1 <= L < 0, and the caveat stays sub-Planckian over that range, so 'no' follows.

Row 3. I took HPS's tt and θθ equations (5) and (7), transcribed them from the cached text, substituted data (9) at l = 0, and solved the resulting linear system for f''''/f and r''''/r. This route does not use qeihps.py. It reproduces the tree's two expressions exactly: 259200 pi^2 (-L-1)/(L(3L+4)) and 129600 pi^2 (2-L^2)/(L^2(3L+4)). At L = -2/3 they give (2/9)/r0^4 and (7/9)/r0^4. Neither expression has a pole in the range, since the pole sits at L = -4/3. The row correctly says no measured datum enters.

I re-ran the audit's own script and all 17 checks pass. Its Section B example also checks out by hand: with f = 1/(1+|l|^(3/2)), the geodesic equation reduces to l'' = (3/4)|l|^(1/2) sgn(l), and l = s^4/256 solves it exactly.

lacked_data. M's hypothesis gets a real answer here, not a presumed one. The theorem is pure differential geometry with no empirical input. The only inputs the tree uses are HPS model data, now re-derived from HPS's equations. No value in HPS's admissible range changes non-degeneracy.

Two wording caveats, neither of which moves the grade:
(a) 'The evidence runs entirely against M's hypothesis' slightly overstates the case. Strictly, the hypothesis is inapplicable to this result, because the theorem has no data input. The evidence does not test it and come out against it. Calling it 'not applicable' would avoid over-representing the point in either direction.
(b) The claim that the theorem 'takes no physical input' rests on the standard statement, which is NAMED-NOT-READ, because Whitehead 1932 was not read. The same applies to the C^{1,1} literature (Minguzzi, Kunzinger-Steinbauer-Stojkovic, Hartman-Wintner): those arXiv ids are from memory and those papers were not read. Only the failure below C^{1,1} is actually computed here.

From the data lens, NARROWED is supported. Nothing in the data refutes the theorem, and the narrowing comes from the hypotheses the tree's use drops, not from any datum.

audits.published_statement: Huang-Lee 1706.03732v3 p.2: 'The special case k = 0 is often called the Riemannian positive mass theorem. In this case, |P| = 0 and the dominant energy condition is reduced to the condition that the scalar curvature of g is nonnegative everywhere. R. Schoen and S.-T. Yau proved the Riemannian positive mass theorem E >= 0 in dimension less than eight ... a separate argument is used to give a characterization of the equality case that if E = 0, then (M, g) is isometric to Euclidean space. In the case k != 0 ... These results also show that if E = 0, then (M, g, k) can be isometrically embedded in Minkowski spacetime with the second fundamental form k.' Thm 1: 'Let 3 <= n <= 7. Let (M, g, k) be an n-dimensional asymptotically flat initial data set that satisfies the dominant energy condition and has E = |P| ... Then E = |P| = 0.' Cor.4 adds, for n = 3, tr_g k = O(|x|^-s) with s > 2, for the embedding into Minkowski. Shi-Tam p.1: '(M, g) is actually flat if the ADM mass of one of the ends is zero.'
published_hypotheses: initial data set: M connected, smooth, WITHOUT BOUNDARY (HL Def.2.5), with a COMPLETE C^2_loc RIEMANNIAN (positive-definite) metric g and a C^1_loc symmetric k (EHLS Def.3)
asymptotic flatness: (g - g_E, k) in C^{2,alpha}_{-q} x C^{1,alpha}_{-1-q}, q in ((n-2)/2, n-2), mu, J in C^{0,alpha}_{-n-q0}; multiple ends allowed (HL Remark 2.7)
DEC on the slice mu >= |J|_g; for k = 0 (a static slice) this is R_g >= 0
E is the ADM flux of the chosen end (HL Def.2.8)

conclusion (k = 0): slice isometric to Euclidean space, and with several ends a zero-mass end forces a single end and flatness; (k != 0): E = 0 => embeds in Minkowski; E = |P| => E = |P| = 0 (HL, n <= 7), embedding for n = 3 needs tr k = O(r^-s), s > 2
the conclusion concerns the INITIAL DATA SET; 'the spacetime is Minkowski' needs one more step
low regularity: Shi-Tam Thm 3.1 needs EQUAL mean curvatures across a Lipschitz corner; the H_- >= H_+ version (Miao 2002) is NAMED-NOT-READ
no empirical data

It is positive definite only for m < m* = a R_s/(2(R_s - a)) = 0.0100010 at a = 0.02, R_s = 200. There the slice is not an initial data set, and the theorem and its contrapositive are silent. concentric.py:139-141 flags the window edges as INDICATIVE because of linearisation, but not this consequence. Recorded, not repaired. Any positive monotone completion u = f(Phi), such as exp(-Phi/2) (RECONSTRUCTED), keeps E = 0 and R(0) < 0 at every m in the window (R10), so the tree's CONCLUSION survives.

DROPPED, satisfied by the device (harmless): asymptotic flatness, completeness, no boundary, one end. None is stated in concentric.py; pair.py:308 carries 'asymptotically flat', 'nonsingular' and the DEC. For m < m*, psi lies in [0.50005, 1.0] at m = 5e-3, g - delta = O(r^-3) inside the fall-off window, and R = O(r^-5) is in L^1. WEAKENED REGULARITY, closed for this device by derivation: psi' jumps by -2m/R_s^2 at R_s, so g is Lipschitz there, below the C^2 of EHLS Def.3 / HL Def.2.5. Shi-Tam Thm 3.1 needs H_- = H_+, while the device has H_+ - H_- = -2m/(R_s^2 psi^(3/2)) < 0, so Shi-Tam does not cover it. Elementary rigidity for conformally flat Lipschitz data on R^3 runs as follows. R >= 0 <=> Lap u <= 0. E = -(1/2pi) Int d(Lap u) = 0 then gives Lap u = 0, so u is harmonic, and Liouville gives u == 1. z3 discharges the finite step (R6); Weyl's lemma and Liouville are named. verifiers.reason:
The audit is not refuted, and the evidence supports NARROWED. Two mild over-statements about what z3 proved are noted below; neither changes the grade.

RE-RUN. I copied the script to verify/rederive/ and ran it. It finished OVERALL OK, exit 0, with 46 [ok] and 0 FAIL in about 13 s. Its output is byte-identical to the banked rederive/positive-mass-theorem-rigidity.out.

ENCODING VS THE PUBLISHED STATEMENT. I checked the inputs against the tree. Phi = m/sqrt(r^2+a^2) - m/max(r,R_s) matches concentric.py:44. The slice (1-2Phi)dx^2 matches composite.py:35-36. a = 0.02 and R_s = 200 match concentric.py:155-156. The window 5e-3..4e-2 and the best lead at 2e-2 match concentric.py:77-78, 82 and 360.

The substantive checks compute the real quantities. R1 derives scalar curvature from Christoffels. R2 takes the ADM flux limit. R3 finds the threshold psi(0) = 0 at m* = aR_s/(2(R_s-a)) = 0.0100010 and computes the mean-curvature jump. R4 gives R(0) in closed form. R5 does the bookkeeping: core -m, shell +m, sum 3e-18, with quadrature equal to the flux. R8 is the incomplete counterexample with E = 0 and R > 0. R10 tests completions u = f(Phi).

My independent second code path agrees on every point:
- X1: the Cartesian conformal formula R = -e^{-2w}(4 Lap w + 2|grad w|^2) reproduces R(0) = -12m/a^3/(1-2m/a+2m/R_s)^2 = -2.9994e4 exactly.
- X3: the standard ADM flux (1/16pi) oint (d_j g_ij - d_i g_jj) dS^i, rather than the u-form, gives E = 0.
- X4: the Plummer core alone gives E = -m.
- X6: m* = 0.0100010, and psi(0) = -0.9998 at m = 2e-2 and -2.9996 at m = 4e-2.

So the NARROWED finding is computed, not interpreted. The literal linearised slice is not Riemannian at m >= m*, inside the window the tree's rigidity VERDICT covers (concentric.py:352-355). R10's general argument is also sound: for f > 0 and f' < 0, grad Phi(0) = 0 and Lap Phi(0) = -3m/a^3 give R(0) < 0. The tree's conclusion therefore survives.

VACUITY. R6 carries its own guard: SAT once R >= 0 is dropped. I added guards on R7:
- THM & device does not entail DEC.
- The device without THM does not entail not-DEC.
- THM & device with FLAT does not entail not-DEC.
- THM & device without E0 does not entail not-DEC.

All four come out as required. X5 adds a sign control: flipping the device (core +m, shell -m) gives R(0) > 0 and a shell jump of +2m/R_s^2. The DEC failure then moves to the shell. This confirms that rigidity says only that the DEC fails somewhere; the audit's R4 places it at the core by direct computation.

TOY PARTS (noted, not grade-moving).
1. The z3 work in R6 and R7 proves trivial lemmas: nonpositive reals summing to zero are all zero, and modus tollens. R7's "dropping AF / completeness / regularity blocks it" holds by construction, because those atoms sit in THM's antecedent. That is no evidence the hypotheses are load-bearing; R8 and Volkov carry that weight. The grade_evidence wording "reproduced independently ... (R6, z3)" over-represents this slightly. The analytic content (distributional sign of Lap u at the Lipschitz shell, Weyl's lemma, Liouville) is NAMED, not machine-checked. The script's own docstring says so honestly.
2. Side observation, outside the audit's claims: with the tree's completion psi^(1/4), R > 0 for r of about 1 to 200 (+1.3e-4 at r = 1). This is an O(Phi^2) gradient term. It does not affect any conclusion here, since R(0) < 0 suffices.

GRADE. The external rigidity clause STANDS as read in the restatements (Huang-Lee, EHLS, Shi-Tam). The tree's application drops "g is Riemannian", and that hypothesis fails at the tree's m = 2e-2 and 4e-2. The tree also leaves completeness, AF and one end unstated. NARROWED, as the audit grades it.

audits.name: Gao & Wald 2000, Jacobi matrix equation (eq. 11): A'' = -T A, conjugate point at det A = 0

source.located: Gao & Wald, 'Theorems on gravitational time delay and related issues', CQG 17, 4999 (2000), arXiv gr-qc/0007021v2, p.7, eqs.(11)-(13). Eq.(11) quoted verbatim from the full text: d^2A^mu_nu/dlambda^2 = -R_{alpha beta sigma}^mu k^alpha k^sigma A^beta_nu, A|p = 0, dA/dlambda|p = delta, in Wald's index convention. Eq.(12): G = sqrt(det A). Eq.(13): G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma_ab sigma^ab + R_ab k^a k^b]. Independent restatement: Osorio Morales & Santillan, arXiv:2004.12523v4 (2022), sec.2.1, eq.(2.1), same initial data: 'q = gamma(lambda_0) is said to be conjugated to p if and only if det(A(lambda_0)) = 0', and det A = 0 'implies that there exist some initial conditions such that eta(q) = 0, thus q is a conjugate point to p in the usual sense' (p.5).
source.via: Every alphaXiv call this stage made (answer_pdf_queries, get_paper_content with fullText, discover_papers) was refused with 'alphaXiv assistant quota exceeded'. The egress proxy refuses arxiv.org, export.arxiv.org, alphaxiv.org and semanticscholar (CONNECT 403). Eqs.(11)-(13) therefore come from two places. (a) The verbatim quotation in the sibling audit audits/gr-qc_0007021.json, which READ gr-qc/0007021v2 in full at source in this docket (alphaXiv full text). (b) The full text of arXiv:2004.12523v4 cached at scratchpad/d67/src/osm_flat.txt, read here, which restates eq.(11) and the det A = 0 criterion exactly. The Jacobi equation itself is also re-derived symbolically here (E1).

audits.published_statement: Gao & Wald (2000) eq.(11): take a null geodesic from p with affine parameter lambda and tangent k. The Jacobi matrix obeys d^2A^mu_nu/dlambda^2 = -R_{alpha beta sigma}^mu k^alpha k^sigma A^beta_nu, with A|p = 0 and dA/dlambda|p = delta. This is the geodesic-deviation equation eta'' = -R(k, eta)k. On a transverse screen it reads eta_i'' = -K_ij eta_j with K_ij = R_{k e_i k e_j} (MTW sign). A point q is conjugate to p where det A = 0; 2004.12523 eq.(2.1) restates this in those words. Eq.(13), G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma^2 + R_kk] with G = sqrt(det A), follows from the Raychaudhuri equation, which the paper quotes from ref.[10]. Eq.(11) is a kinematic identity of Lorentzian geometry and assumes no energy condition. Gao-Wald's Lemma 1 and Theorem 1 add NEC and the null generic condition only to guarantee that det A does reach zero.
published_hypotheses: H1: a null geodesic, affinely parametrised, with tangent k. 2004.12523 adds the normalisation k.t = -1.
H2: a congruence from a point, A|p = 0 and dA/dlambda|p = delta. It is twist-free by construction, so eq.(13) has no vorticity term.
H3: a smooth Lorentzian metric. Eq.(11) itself needs no energy condition, symmetry or field equation.
H4: four dimensions, for the coefficient 1/2 in eq.(13) and for G = sqrt(det A). For the literal 4x4 matrix, det A = lambda^2 det A_perp (sibling audit B2).
H5: the sign of the curvature term is tied to a convention (Wald's R_{abc}^d with the deviation equation's minus sign). An implementation must pair its Riemann convention with the matching sign.
H6: this is for the achronality consequence and is not part of eq.(11). A null geodesic is not achronal past a point conjugate to p (Hawking-Ellis Prop. 4.5.12, NAMED-NOT-READ).
hypothesis_drift: SIGN. A discrepancy in the tree's implementation, shown by computation. Eq.(11) is eta'' = -K eta with K_ij = R_{k e_i k e_j}. composite.py:233 defines T_ij = -R_{m a n b} k^m e_i^a k^n e_j^b using a standard MTW Riemann (composite.py:172-187), so T = -K (E2). composite.py:256 then evolves A'' = -T A = +K A, which is the opposite sign to eq.(11). A convention-free check confirms it (E3/E3b): with parallel starting data, the sign in eq.(11) reproduces the owner's own geodesic separations, while composite's sign returns the two transverse axes swapped. For a diagonal traceless T the sign flip changes neither det A nor any conjugate point (E4). The tree therefore silently adds the hypothesis R_kk = 0 and T_yz = 0. concentric.py:207 copies the same loop. On a ray through matter the flip matters (E9): 191.76 against 232.56, and seat against no seat at m = 5e-3.

ADDED, valid: composite.py:37-40 and 243-246 replace the 4x4 matrix with a 2x2 system on a transverse screen. This is legitimate in 4D: det A = lambda^2 det A_perp, and K is unchanged by e -> e + alpha k.

WEAKENED, and recorded by the owner: the screen is carried along by a first-order Euler step, which leaks about 1% (composite.py:328-330). The screen vectors are not normalised by g. Independent RK4 on an exact screen agrees to within one coarse step (E5).

Page 7 prints eq.(11) as d^2A^mu_nu/dlambda^2 = -sum R_{alpha beta sigma}^mu k^alpha k^sigma A^beta_nu, with A|p = 0 and dA/dlambda|p = delta. It says q is conjugate to p "if and only if det A = 0 at q". It gives G = sqrt(det A) as eq.(12) and G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma^2 + R_ab k^a k^b] as eq.(13), citing [10]. SIGN DRIFT, CHECKED INDEPENDENTLY. I did not use the auditor's script. I ran a sandbox copy of composite.py, with typefour.py copied beside it so it imports. At closest approach (b = 0.3, M = +2e-3, e1 = y radial, e2 = z), composite.tidal returns T = diag(+0.2213, -0.2212). I then took the coordinate acceleration difference of neighbouring geodesics from composite's own Christoffels. It gives eta_y''/eta_y = +0.290 (diverging) and eta_z''/eta_z = -0.146 (converging). Adding the connection term analytically brings this to magnitude 0.222, with those signs. Positive mass stretching rays radially and squeezing them transversely is the physically expected pattern. composite evolves acc = -T A (composite.py:256), which converges y and diverges z. That is the reverse sign, so composite integrates A'' = +K A where eq.(11) gives A'' = -K A. For context, T is the lensing optical tidal matrix, whose usual Jacobi equation is D'' = +T D. The drift is real and computed. It is not a misreading or a misprint, so STANDS is not supportable. The tree's implemented equation agrees with eq.(11) only on a smaller class, which is the rubric's NARROWED. WRONG is excluded because nothing in the source is contradicted.

CORRECTION 1: the narrowing condition is smaller than the audit states. The audit says the tree silently adds 'R_kk = 0 and T_yz = 0', and its E4a shows invariance only for a diagonal traceless T. T_yz = 0 is not needed. For any traceless symmetric 2x2 T, a constant 90-degree rotation R gives R T R^T = -T and R I R^T = I. So A' = R A R^T solves the flipped equation with the same initial data, and det A' = det A for any lambda-dependent T. I checked this numerically with a time-varying traceless T with off-diagonal terms, integrated by RK4 to lambda = 12 (verify/refute/eq11/flip.py). The determinants under the two signs agree exactly; maximum relative difference 0.0. The hypothesis the code adds is R_kk = 0 alone. This widens the safe class, but every standing caller is already inside it.

CORRECTION 2: 'silently' overstates. composite.py itself states that its rays are trace-free (VALIDATION 2, 'R_kk = 0', and limitation 3, 'The tidal matrix is traceless'). What it does not state is that the correctness of its integration depends on that condition, and the docstring at :37-40 presents A'' = -T A as eq.(11) in general. Dropping H5, the pairing of the Riemann convention with its sign, therefore still stands as a drift.

CORRECTION 3: this belongs to the sibling eq.(13) audit, not to this key. Gao-Wald p.6 says 'our results hold in any spacetime dimension'. Eq.(13) with G = sqrt(det A) is exact only for n = 4. Raychaudhuri gives G''/G = theta^2[1/4 - 1/(2(n-2))] - (1/2)(sigma^2 + R_kk), and the first term is positive for n > 4. The audit's H4 is therefore right. Against the paper's own dimension claim, this is a recorded discrepancy, not a refutation; it does not touch eq.(11).

THE AUDIT'S NUMBERS STAND. E4b (an identical window at all nine masses, both signs) follows from the rotation argument above and needs no diagonal assumption. The two rests_on_it items, the composite window with 'SEATS AND EARLY' and SR3's seats = True, survive. In concentric.py:207 the copied loop uses the same acc = -T A. I confirmed that it is copied and that concentric carries a withdrawal header (LEAD_IS_INTERIOR_ONLY). I did not separately confirm that its a = 0.5 corridor is the withdrawn one. concentric is also not listed as an owner of this key.

NET: the grade is NARROWED. Eq.(11) stands at source, and the tree's implementation equals it only where R_kk = 0. The audit's 'T_yz = 0' should be struck and its read_status raised to READ.

audits.published_statement: NOT READ AT SOURCE. The usual textbook form, given as the standard statement and not quoted from a source: (weak) if U is bounded and open in R^n, u is C^2 on U and continuous on its closure, and Laplacian(u) = 0 on U, then max and min of u over the closure are attained on the boundary. (strong) If U is also connected and u attains an interior max or min, then u is constant on U. Mean-value property: if u is harmonic near a closed ball B(x0, rho), then u(x0) equals the average of u over |x - x0| = rho. In R^3, Laplacian(1/|x|) = 0 for x != 0. The tree uses the local corollary (no strict interior minimum) and the 3-D kernel fact. Both are re-derived here rather than quoted.
published_hypotheses: u is C^2 with Laplacian(u) = 0 on an open set U (the source-free region)
Strict-extremum corollary: a closed ball around the point lies in U. This is local; connectedness is not needed.
Strong principle (no non-strict interior extremum unless u is constant): U connected, and the conclusion is 'constant on the component'
1/r is harmonic only in three spatial dimensions (in R^n the radial kernel is r^(2-n)), and only away from the sources
[All four are the standard form and were NOT READ at source]

The tree is 3-D throughout, so there is no consequence; recorded so the limitation is named.

The step from there to 'NO static configuration is stably in equilibrium' (stability.py:118-119) also needs the converse of Lagrange-Dirichlet. That step is not part of this result; it belongs to the sibling entry earnshaw-1842-theorem.

The mean-value identity is linear in the m_i, and a harmonic function has neither a strict minimum nor a strict maximum. So the claim holds under either negative-mass dynamics convention. Numerically: S3a on 40 random mixed-sign configurations (worst relative deviation 3.1e-15), and S6 on 41 mixed-sign equilibria, all with indefinite Hessians.

Encoding: this is the theorem for the tree's class, not a toy of it. S2c and S2d derive the spherical mean of 1/|x-z| symbolically and exactly: 1/d when the source is outside the sphere, 1/rho when it is inside. The mean-value property for any finite signed sum then follows by linearity, and S8 extends it to the uniform shell. S3b, the contradiction step, is printed rather than machine-checked. It is the standard valid two-line argument: a strict local min forces the sphere mean above the centre value, and that contradicts mean = centre. S4 (z3) is the second-order shadow of the same result and is encoded correctly (Sylvester criterion for positive definite; all principal minors for positive semidefinite). I read stability.py:114-123, chain.py:136-160 and chain.py:318-340 and 410-420 directly; the quoted sites match.

Vacuity guards (hfmp_v/hfmp_vacuity.py). Each one detects the change when a hypothesis is negated:
- V1, a source inside the ball: the mean-value deviation rises to 8.9e-4 to 1.8e-1, against 3e-15 for the source-free ball.
- V2, a Yukawa kernel in place of 1/r: deviation 1.2e-2 to 7.7e-1.
- V3, the S6 pipeline with a non-harmonic k|x|^2 term added: 211 of 244 equilibria are positive definite, against 0 of 41 for the harmonic control. So S6 is not vacuously 'all indefinite'.
- V4, dropping trace-0 in z3: positive semidefinite and nonzero becomes SAT, and positive definite with trace 1 becomes SAT. Trace-0 with negative definite stays UNSAT, so a strict max is excluded too, which supports 'whatever their signs'.
- V5, Cartesian Laplacian of 1/r, computed independently of S1c's radial formula: non-zero at n=2 and n=4, zero at n=3.
- V6: for u = |x|^2 the sphere mean exceeds the centre value by rho^2, so the S3b argument does detect a strict min when one exists.

One point narrows the audit's own text, not the grade. The audit's 'WORDING DISCREPANCY' (stability.py:118-119, 'DEGENERATE case, constant potential') is overstated. By the strong principle, a harmonic function has any local minimum, strict or not, only if it is constant on a neighbourhood. S5's x^3 - 3xy^2 rebuts a pointwise-degenerate reading that the text does not require. It is still fair to record as loose labelling, not as an error.

NOT DONE HERE.' O5_ANSWERED_BY at :174-176 reads '... Closed only by an existence theorem for the static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat class'. The closest READ external statements are these. Sanders 2007.14311v2 p.2: 'It appears, however, that the static solutions of the semi-classical Einstein-Klein-Gordon system have not been studied before (except the Minkowski vacuum).' Sanders sec. 7: '...or even in general static spacetimes.' HPS p.3: 'numerical evidence for the existence of Lorentzian wormholes'. HPS p.8: 'The redshift function however, does not approach a constant value as l -> infinity, so the metric as a whole is not asymptotically flat.' 2604.01047 (2026) names nonlinear existence only for cosmological spacetimes and names no static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat existence theorem.
published_hypotheses: H1 (tree) The class is static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat solutions of G = 8 pi <T>. H3 (tree) 'which nobody has' is a universal negative. Its status word is 'none (NOT DONE HERE)' and no search record is attached.
H4 (tree) 'closed ONLY by': O5 can be settled by nothing but such a theorem.

Sanders (READ): the full semiclassical Einstein-Klein-Gordon system with a free scalar, solved rigorously. Static solutions 'not studied before (except the Minkowski vacuum)'. His own existence result covers R x S^3 only.
HPS (READ): the AHS approximate <T>, xi = 1/6, m = 0, zero temperature, throat data from eq. (9). The results are numerical 'local solutions', and the published one is not asymptotically flat.

Sanders had rigorous tools only for compact ultrastatic slices, and calls the non-compact case 'more challenging, because the symmetry group becomes non-compact'. Second, 'closed ONLY by' fails as logic (z3, C3); hpscentre.py:303-308 has already superseded it. These are discrepancies in the wording, not refutations, so they do not make the grade WRONG. They do mean the best grade reachable is NARROWED, not STANDS.

Both conditions are now gone. alphaXiv works again, both papers were READ at source, and the sweep ran. What they show goes past the ceiling the audit itself set for NARROWED.

(1) Juarez-Aubry arXiv:2412.08402v2 (dated 1 Dec 2025), READ, pp.1-6.
- Thm 1 proves unique local analytic existence for semiclassical gravity at xi = 1/2, for a special class of Hadamard two-point functions, in a causal normal neighbourhood N of C, with no symmetry assumed.

- Schwarzschild is non-flat, static, spherically symmetric and asymptotically flat. I checked in sympy that it is Ricci-flat with Riemann^t_rtr = 2M/(r^2(r-2M)) != 0. With every alpha = 0 it therefore solves eq. (IV.1a): G = I = J = 0 (script verify/refute/no-existence-theorem-ssaf.check.py, PASS).

(2) Juarez-Aubry arXiv:2011.05947v2 (AHP 2021), READ, pp.1-3, 14-22.
- Static semiclassical gravity reduces to constraints on the state's initial data (Thms 10-11).
- Prop. 9 is a no-go: 'for conformally-coupled fields in Ricci-flat spacetimes semiclassical gravity only admits solutions in Minkowski spacetime'.

(3) The discover sweep (1 call) turned up only approximate or numerical SSAF work.
- arXiv:2212.08089 (equation-of-state closures) says 'there are currently no systematic techniques available to address the full question'.
- arXiv:2501.09784 covers the interior only and says the exterior semiclassical system 'is currently unknown'.

- (a) exact renormalised <T> in a POSITIVE Hadamard state;
- (b) outside the xi = 1/2 quantum-stealth sector, for example HPS's xi = 1/6 AHS system, which is the case the tree's paragraph concerns;

- It is not WRONG. 2412.08402 is not a theorem for the tree's class: it fixes xi = 1/2, leaves positivity open, and is local. The tree's wording is a discrepancy, not a refutation.

It passes all 12 checks and exits 0, and its numbers match the audit's report: flat-space residuals [0,0,0], control residual 0.13079, F(1e3)=123.457, F(1e6)=2277.409. The 2026 paper 2604.01047v1 names no static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat existence theorem and cites Juarez-Aubry AHP 23 (2022) 1451 as ref [61]. The HPS row is right. HPS gr-qc/9701064v1 p.8 prints 'a = 5.3 and b = 25.5' and 'so the metric as a whole is not asymptotically flat'. The two computed values are correct: F(1e3) = 123.457 and F(1e6) = 2277.409. F has a zero at l = e^(b/a) ≈ 122.9 and then grows like ln^2 l. So that row's moves_conclusion = No follows.

The literature-state row is wrong as stated, and its conditional moves_conclusion is superseded by text now READ at source. I read three papers live through alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2026-10-02; the quota is back.

(1) The audit's 'confirms' from 2604.01047 rested on an incomplete harvest. The harvested file has no page 13, and its body never cites [61], [62] or [94]: Juárez-Aubry static, Juárez-Aubry stealth, and Sanders. Those three appear only in the bibliography. So the reading was an absence over pages nobody had read. I read page 13 live: 'simplifying assumptions are often imposed on the studied spacetimes [60, 61, 94], on the expectation value of the state [22, 62]' and 'a general theory for the well-posedness of the Cauchy problem on arbitrary background and for arbitrary Cauchy data is missing'. The conclusion survives, now on evidence. It names no theorem for the static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat class.

(2) 2412.08402v2, which the audit had as NAMED-NOT-READ, is now READ. Abstract: xi = 1/2, a special class of Hadamard two-point functions, 'the first well-posedness result for semiclassical gravity without spacetime symmetries'. Theorem 1 gives a unique analytic evolution. The two-point function is reconstructed only in a causal normal neighbourhood N of the Cauchy surface. Sec. VI: 'local semiclassical gravity solutions exist for every (analytic) vacuum solution of ... general relativity!, modulo state positivity'. Positivity is 'an important open question'. Schwarzschild is a non-flat, static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat analytic vacuum solution, so the audit's own conditional fires: 'If the stealth class contains a non-flat SSAF member, the claim narrows'. 'Nothing READ shows that it does' is therefore no longer true. The member is only partial: xi = 1/2, positivity open, the state built only on N, renormalisation constants chosen. It is not a theorem for positive Hadamard states.

(3) 2011.05947v2 is now READ. Prop. 9 is a no-go: a static, Ricci-flat, globally hyperbolic spacetime other than Minkowski admits no states for the conformally coupled field (m = 0, xi = 1/6) that solve the equations, for any alpha and beta. It names Schwarzschild explicitly. It also says 'even the existence of the vacuum state in a given spacetime is not guaranteed'. Its examples are hyperbolic ultrastatic, de Sitter and toroidal flat; none is non-flat and asymptotically flat. This is a partial no-go that the row omits. It supports the tree in HPS's coupling, xi = 1/6, but it covers only Ricci-flat geometries.

(4) A minor misreading of Sanders. 'or even in general static spacetimes' (sec. 7) refers to whether the ground state's special role persists for general states. It does not say that existence of static solutions is open. The quote 'more challenging, because the symmetry group becomes non-compact' is about open Einstein static universes. It is acceptable as cited in lacked_data.

The lacked_data answer is supported with evidence, not presumed. The question is mathematical and bibliographic, and what was missing was technique (HPS numerics with the AHS approximation; Sanders' compact slices). The two later papers confirm this: the 2022 paper reduces the static case to constraints and proves a no-go, and the 2024/2026 paper gets existence only by restricting the state. No measured quantity enters.

Proposed grade: NARROWED. 'Which nobody has' holds as NOT-FOUND only under named hypotheses:
(a) exact renormalised <T> in a positive Hadamard state;
(b) outside the xi = 1/2 stealth sector, with a xi = 1/6 Ricci-flat no-go in hand;
(c) non-trivial members only;
(d) a global solution, not one on N alone;
(e) 'only' dropped (C3).
It is not WRONG, because no READ paper proves the claimed theorem for positive Hadamard states. It is not OPEN, because the papers that decided the audit's own grade conditions are now READ. I did not run discover_papers myself. The universal negative remains a floor, not a proof.

audits.name: Causality proxy: surface EOS slope beta^2 <= 1 as subluminal sound speed

source.located: The reading is not one paper's theorem. It is a convention of the thin-shell literature, and these sources state it together with their own caveats: E. Poisson & M. Visser, arXiv:gr-qc/9506083v1, PRD 52, 7318 (1995), sec. IV (pp. 3-4); M. Ishak & K. Lake, arXiv:gr-qc/0108058v2, PRD 65, 044011 (2002), sec. II.D; E. F. Eiroa et al., arXiv:2408.14328v3 (2024), after Eq (42). The causal content it borrows is textbook: a barotropic relativistic perfect fluid has characteristic speed sqrt(dp/deps), and is causal iff that is <= 1. That content is MACHINE-CHECKED here for the shell's 2+1 worldvolume, not read. The radial criterion that beta^2 is compared with is cross-checked against Pitre, Schneider & Poisson, arXiv:2604.05980v1 (2026) Eqs (3.11)-(3.16c). Their surface fluid is a thermodynamic polytrope, so its sound speed is defined. Later context: Simmonds & Visser, arXiv:2606.01061v1 (2026) sec. 2.6; Curiel, arXiv:1405.0403v1 (2014). Ellis, Maartens & MacCallum, GRG 39, 1651 (2007), arXiv:gr-qc/0703121 is NAMED-NOT-READ.

In this stage every live alphaXiv call (answer_pdf_queries x2, get_paper_content, discover_papers) returned 'quota exceeded', and the egress proxy refuses arxiv.org (CONNECT 403).

audits.published_statement: PV 1995 sec. IV: 'Under normal circumstances one might (naively) try to interpret beta0 as the speed of sound in the exotic matter located at the wormhole throat. Furthermore, under normal circumstances one would require beta0 to lie in the interval beta0 in (0, 1]. (One would normally deduce beta0 > 0 from the assumed stability of matter, and argue that beta0 <= 1 based on the requirement that the speed of sound should not exceed the speed of light.) ... there is no guarantee that beta0 actually is the speed of sound. A detailed microphysical model for the exotic matter would be necessary in order to settle such issues with any certainty. We therefore conclude that wormhole configurations with |beta0^2| > 1 should not be ruled out a priori.' Ishak-Lake 2002 sec. II.D: 'Phenomenologically, for timelike Sigma, P'/sigma'(R) represents the square of the speed of sound on Sigma and so one would normally expect 0 <= P'/sigma'(R) < 1. However, one could also construct Sigma out of (say) fields for which P'/sigma'(R) need not even be positive.' Eiroa et al. 2024: 'although kappa is the squared speed of sound in the case of ordinary matter, for which 0 < kappa <= 1, this may not be the case for exotic matter [PV 1995].'
published_hypotheses: S1: beta^2 = dp/dsigma is a PARAMETER of the linearised equation of state. Reading it as c_s^2 is an interpretation: PV call it 'naive', Ishak-Lake 'phenomenological'.
S2: the reading is offered for ORDINARY matter (sigma > 0). For exotic matter all three sources say it may fail, and none of them imposes beta^2 <= 1 there.
S3: settling whether beta is the sound speed needs a microphysical model of the shell matter (PV sec. IV). No source supplies one.
S4 (implicit; made explicit by PSP 2026): the shell matter is a barotropic, isentropically perturbed 2D perfect fluid, so the slope along the perturbation is (dp/deps)_s.
S5: the bound is the perfect-fluid one, characteristic speed <= light speed. Ishak-Lake write a strict '< 1'; PV and Eiroa write '<= 1'.
hypothesis_drift: KEPT (S1/S3): wall.py:201-203 calls beta^2 the thin-shell EOS slope, 'not identical to the microphysical sound speed ... The causality reading beta^2 <= 1 is the standard one and is a proxy.' That is the sources' own caveat, carried.

KEPT (S2): the wall is ordinary matter. sigma_0 = (1-s)/(4 pi R) > 0 and p_0 = (1-s)^2/(16 pi R s) > 0, which matches PSP Eq 3.12 (check C3). The exotic-matter exemption in PV and Eiroa does not arise.

WEAKENED where the conclusion is stated: the proxy qualifier from wall.py:201-203 is dropped at wall.py:39-40 ('WITH A SUBLUMINAL SOUND SPEED'), wall.py:33 ('the causal ceiling'), wall.py:292 ('superluminal sound'), wall.py:558, wall.py:676-683 (table columns 'c_s / c' and 'causal?', then 'every window ... is causal'), warpshell.py:72-73 and restatus.py:155. The wording drifts; the arithmetic does not.

DROPPED (S4, shear-free fluid; not named in the tree): beta^2 = c_s^2 and the bound c_s <= 1 are exact only for a perfect-fluid surface (C4). The radial mode is a uniform change of area, so it sees only the bulk response. For an elastic wall beta^2 = K/(eps+p), while longitudinal waves have c_L^2 = beta^2 + mu_s/(eps+p) (RECONSTRUCTED from linear elasticity, C5b). The causal ceiling therefore falls to 1 - mu_s/(eps+p). The window stays open iff mu_s/(eps+p) < 0.92067 at x=0.3, 0.63397 at x=2/3, 0.26393 at x=4/5. wall.py:195-196 does list 'anisotropic elastic matter' as not treated, but as a question of clearing the stability threshold, not of the causal ceiling. Le's Bowers-Liang wall (wall.py:195) is an anisotropic fluid and the Einstein-Vlasov model is collisionless, so the models the tree actually works are untouched.

DROPPED (S4, isentropic perturbation): off an adiabatic perturbation, as in the RADIATING shell, the EOS slope is not the sound speed (Simmonds-Visser 2026 sec. 2.6 makes this point in general). Partly carried: wall.py:199-200 leaves the flux-coupled stability open, but not as a condition on the causality reading.

DIRECTION, carried: in a finite-thickness wall beta^2 is a positive-weight average of the local c_t^2 (C5a). So beta^2 <= 1 is necessary for local causality but not sufficient: beta^2 = 0.46 can coexist with a layer at c_t^2 = 1.5. restatus.py:156-157 keeps this open ('Open: admissible matter at that stiffness').
DISCREPANCY, immaterial: the sources differ on '< 1' versus '<= 1'. The boundary sits at x* = 0.84374, outside the operative window x < 4/5, so the difference changes nothing.

audits.published_statement: Baumann 0907.5424, p.20: 'Eqns. (21) and (22) may be combined into the continuity equation d rho/dt + 3H(rho + p) = 0 (23). This may also be written as d ln rho / d ln a = -3(1+w) (24), if we define the equation of state parameter w = p/rho (25). Eqn. (24) may be integrated to give rho ∝ a^{-3(1+w)} (26).' Problem (113): 'Derive the continuity equation from nabla_mu T^mu_nu = 0.' Bousso hep-th/0203101, Sect. 7.1: 'We will assume, for now, that the universe evolves adiabatically. Thus, the physical entropy density is diluted by cosmological expansion: sigma(eta) = s/a(eta)^3 (7.5). The comoving entropy density s is constant in space and time.'
published_hypotheses: A homogeneous, isotropic FLRW metric with any k. The stress tensor is the perfect-fluid form T_mu_nu = diag(rho, -p, -p, -p) in the comoving frame (Baumann eq 20).
A perfect fluid: no shear viscosity, no bulk viscosity, no heat flux.
EITHER the Friedmann equations (21)-(22) OR local conservation nabla_mu T^mu_nu = 0 (Problem 113). Either one is enough for continuity.
For the closed form rho ∝ a^{-3(1+w)}: w = p/rho is constant (Baumann integrates (24) with w fixed).

For dS = 0: adiabatic evolution is ASSUMED (Bousso 7.1, 'We will assume, for now'). The thermodynamic route needs a Gibbs relation T dS = dE + p dV - mu dN in local equilibrium, with mu dN = 0 (Masoumi-Mathur eq 24 writes T dS = dE + p dV, i.e. fixed N).

source.located: Classic: J. Ackeret, 'Zur Theorie der Raketen', Helv. Phys. Acta 19 (1946) 103. It predates arXiv, and the attribution comes from the canonical entry's name; arrival.py cites no source for the formula. The restatement/generalisation that was READ: An T. The paper introduces the lemma with 'The corresponding mass cost follows from the relativistic rocket equation [16]', where [16] = Henriques & Natario, 'The rocket problem in general relativity', J. Optim. Theory Appl. 154 (2012) 500, arXiv:1105.5235.
source.via: Ackeret 1946 is NAMED-NOT-READ. In this stage alphaXiv discover_papers and get_paper_content both returned 'alphaXiv assistant quota exceeded', so no fresh read was made. What was READ is alphaXiv page text of arXiv:2606.22531v4 that an earlier step of this workflow harvested and cached at scratchpad/d67/src/casmag/all/2606.22531v4.txt: lines 315-361 for Lemma 2.1 and its proof, lines 1941-1944 for refs [15] and [16]. Lemma 2.1 strictly generalises the tree's formula (any momentum path, any causal exhaust), and its equality case is exactly the photon-rocket formula; the re-derivation script carries out that reduction symbolically. audits.published_statement: Classic form (NAMED-NOT-READ at source): for a rocket whose exhaust is light, the rest-mass ratio needed to go from 0 to beta (or from beta to 0) is M0/M1 = sqrt((1+beta)/(1-beta)). The READ generalisation, Le 2606.22531v4 Lemma 2.1, verbatim: 'Let P(s) be a C1 future timelike momentum on a finite interval in one Minkowski vector space, with F = -dP/ds future causal or zero. Set M = sqrt(-P^2), V = P/M, w = log(M_i/M), and E = -V.F. For E > 0 define eta = sqrt((F - E V)^2)/E, and set eta = 0 when E = 0. Then 0 <= eta <= 1 and L := Int sqrt((dV/ds)^2) ds = Int eta dw, d := arcosh(-V_i.V_f), log(M_i/M_f) - d = (L - d) + Int (1 - eta) dw >= 0. In particular, M_f/M_i <= e^{-L} <= e^{-d}. Equality in the first bound requires null nonzero flux almost everywhere with respect to dw; equality in the second requires a geodesic velocity path traversed without reversal, allowing coasts.' The paper then explains: 'Here eta is the magnitude of exhaust momentum per unit emitted energy in the instantaneous rest frame.' For a straight burn from beta to rest, d = artanh(beta) and e^d = sqrt((1+beta)/(1-beta)). The tree's formula is therefore the equality case, and the lemma makes it a floor on M_i/M_f.
published_hypotheses: (Le L2.1) one Minkowski vector space: special relativity, flat spacetime. The GR extension Le cites is Henriques-Natario 1105.5235 (NAMED-NOT-READ).
(Le L2.1) P(s) is C1 and future timelike: the vehicle is a massive body with a well-defined total 4-momentum.
(Le L2.1) F = -dP/ds is future causal or zero: the only change in the vehicle's 4-momentum is emission of future-causal momentum (exhaust). Nothing is absorbed and no external momentum acts.

(Le L2.1, equality in the first bound) the exhaust is null almost everywhere (eta = 1): massless and collimated in the instantaneous rest frame. Any angular spread pushes eta below 1; Le eq 2.6 says 'equality requires a single emission direction'.
(Le L2.1, equality in the second bound) a geodesic velocity path with no reversal: the burn runs along one straight line in velocity space.
(classic, restated) M is REST mass, so the mass ratio counts all rest mass converted to exhaust.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED at arrival.py:13: 'This is a floor: no propulsion does better per unit energy.' The floor holds only under Le L2.1's condition that F = -dP/ds is future causal, i.e. the vehicle exchanges momentum only through its own exhaust. Propulsion driven by external momentum falls outside that class. The same file prices two such routes that brake with zero rest-mass loss: the reverse slingshot (arrival.py:7-10) and the magsail (arrival.py:14-15). The verdict built on this (arrival.py:160-161) is correctly conditioned on the slingshot but not on the magsail or on externally supplied momentum; those alternatives are not evaluated here.

WEAKENED WORDING at arrival.py:13, 'per unit energy': the result bounds the rest-mass ratio, not energy. The two coincide only under the tree's own 100%-conversion hypothesis (arrival.py:127). Under that hypothesis the wording is not an error; it is named here.

IMPLICIT, not stated in arrival.py: flat spacetime during the burn. This is consistent with Le's 'one Minkowski vector space'.

audits.lacked_data: The result is a closed-form consequence of special-relativistic 4-momentum conservation and uses no measured datum. It depends only on beta, and c is now exact by definition. Ackeret lacked three things. (i) Modern precision tests of Lorentz invariance (Will 1403.7377, READ as cached text): these confirm his input rather than move it. (ii) A realistic account of what annihilation produces: proton-antiproton annihilation goes largely to pions, and part of that energy ends up in neutrinos and uncollimated gammas. No source for this was READ here, so it is only NAMED. By Le L2.1, any such loss pushes eta below 1, which can only raise the mass ratio, so it strengthens the 'floor' reading. (iii) The GR and arbitrary-path generalisations (Henriques-Natario, NAMED-NOT-READ; Le Lemma 2.1, READ): these extend the result and reduce to it in the tree's regime. Nothing found moves the conclusion. What changes is the class of propulsion it applies to, and that comes from a hypothesis the tree drops at arrival.py:13, not from a datum the authors lacked.
audits.grade_evidence: The formula itself stands. It is re-derived symbolically from 4-momentum conservation, cross-checked numerically to within 1.5e-10, and identified as the equality case of the READ Lemma 2.1 in Le 2606.22531v4; no datum can move it. The result holds for self-contained rocket propulsion, a smaller class, and the owner's own file prices two counterexamples to the unconditioned sentence (the slingshot and the magsail). verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (relativistic-rocket-photon-exhaust, audit grade NARROWED)
verifiers.reason:
The NARROWED grade holds, and the evidence supports it more strongly than the audit says. Two parts of the audit's reasoning are wrong, though, and should be corrected.

(1) A source the audit marked NAMED-NOT-READ has now been read. I called alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1105.5235 and got the page text of Henriques & Natario v2, which is the source Le cites as [16]. Its Sec. 2, Thm 2.1 reads m1 = m0 exp(-(1/v) Int |nabla_c' c'| dtau). The exhaust flux J there is restricted only to 'timelike or null and future-directed', and v = 1 is called 'a photon rocket'. Its ref [4] is Ackeret, Zur Theorie der Raketen, Helv. Phys. Acta 19, 103-112 (1946), which confirms the attribution. Ackeret's own paper stays NAMED-NOT-READ. In 1-D Minkowski, Int |a| dtau is the rapidity change chi, so m0/m1 = exp(chi/v), and v = 1 gives sqrt((1+b)/(1-b)) exactly. The cost the paper minimises is rest mass ('fuel consumption'), not energy. So the formula stands, at source, under the hypothesis the audit names: a future-causal exhaust and no other momentum exchange. In Le's terms that is F future causal.

(2) The audit treats 'per unit energy' (arrival.py:13) as WEAKENED WORDING: 'not an error' under 100% conversion, and a sentence that would STAND if read as 'no self-contained rocket does better'. That is wrong. I ran a check, verify/refute/rocket_energy.py. It stays inside Le L2.1 and H-N Thm 2.1's own class (self-contained, future-timelike exhaust at rest-frame speed u < 1) and integrates stepwise, agreeing with exp(chi/u) to about 1e-4. Braking 1 t from 0.866c, a rocket that uses its fuel energy to throw inert propellant at u = 0.65 needs only 1.58 t c^2 of converted energy, against the photon rocket's 2.73 t c^2. It loses more rest mass (6.58 t, of which 5.00 t is inert). So the photon rocket is the floor on the rest-mass ratio M0/M1, which is what both READ sources bound. It is not a floor on energy, and not a floor on antimatter: the antimatter share in pairs is about 0.79 t, not 1.37 t. The sentence 'no propulsion does better per unit energy' is false even for self-contained rockets, unless 'energy' means total rest mass lost, or the tree's own 'perfect antimatter, all lost mass converted' hypothesis (arrival.py:127) is imposed. That hypothesis forbids inert propellant by fiat. The audit's route to STANDS therefore does not work: the wording must become 'per unit rest mass' or 'with no inert propellant'. This is a second, independent ground for NARROWED, on top of the audit's external-momentum ground (the slingshot and magsail, which I confirmed from the code). It does not push the grade to WRONG, because the formula and the mass ratio of 3.73 in the verdict (arrival.py:161, 'mass ratio of 3.73 at 100% conversion') are correct and correctly conditioned.

(3) I re-ran the audit's arithmetic and it holds. The re-derivation script exits OK. The fuel-per-tonne ratio is 55.99, not '76x'. The 3.7314 literal is 7.3e-5 from 3.73167 and matches neither the beta = 0.866 value nor the exact gamma = 2 value. The 2.73 t is the total mass converted. All of these are discrepancies in the tree's own text, recorded and not repaired. Running arrival.py also confirms the magsail mismatch between prose and table (810 AU and 2.6 ly in the prose, 2002 AU and 0.08 ly in the table); that belongs to the magsail entry. The literature search (discover_papers) remains NOT RUN, so its absence of contradicting papers is not evidence.

Corrections to carry into the entry: Henriques-Natario 1105.5235 is now READ (Thm 2.1, cost = rest mass, ref [4] = Ackeret); the 'per unit energy' wording is a hypothesis drift that matters, not harmless wording; and drop 'STANDS if read as no self-contained rocket does better', replacing it with 'STANDS only if :13 is read as a floor on rest-mass ratio for self-contained exhaust propulsion'.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: run the script, check that what it encodes matches the published statement, run vacuity and mutation guards
verifiers.reason:
I copied the script to verify/rederive/rr.py and re-ran it. It exits 0 and its output matches the audit line for line: C1-C4 pass, the discrepancies come out as 55.99 against '76x', 3.7314 against 3.73167 and 2+sqrt3, and 2.7317 t against 1.3658 t, and slingshot dv = 0.6236c. The cached Le 2606.22531v4 text at lines 315-361 matches the audit's verbatim quotation of Lemma 2.1. The physics is encoded correctly. In C2, the rest-frame balance M dchi = -u dM is the right law for collimated exhaust at speed u, so eta = u. In C3, braking means forward emission with dE = dP. The formula is right and the grade holds. Three things in the encoding are overstated, and none of them moves the result.

(1) C1's third check, M0/M1 = exp(artanh b), is not verified symbolically. Its sympy branch returns False, and the check passes only on its numeric fallback at 4 points. The outcome's phrase 'all identities verified symbolically' is therefore too strong. I closed the gap in verify/rederive/sym.py: the derivatives of log sqrt((1+b)/(1-b)) and artanh(b) differ by exactly 0 and both vanish at b=0, so the identity is proved. Le's d = arcosh(gamma) = artanh(b) is not checked anywhere in the script. I checked it numerically to 8e-15 at four betas, but sympy did not simplify the derivative difference, so it is not machine-proved.

(2) C3 is not an independent integration. The update E -= ds; P -= ds is linear and preserves E - P exactly, so the same answer comes out with n=1 steps as with n=200000. The 1.5e-10 'agreement' is floating-point roundoff, not a separate confirmation. As a substitute I ran a genuinely independent non-linear RK4 in beta using the rest-frame law dM/M = -dbeta/(1-beta^2). It agrees with the closed form to 1e-13 at 0.0476 and 0.866, and to 6e-9 at 0.99 with n=2000.

(3) C5 is chk(..., True). It is vacuous by construction, and the audit correctly calls it an illustration only.

The vacuity guards bite. With the causal-exhaust hypothesis negated (u > 1), C2's floor check fails, with a minimum excess of -11.69. With the emission direction negated (backward photons), C3 never brakes and returns nan instead of agreeing. Two mutant formulas are rejected by the C3 check: gamma alone gives 1.9998 and (1+b)/(1-b) gives 13.93. A massive or uncollimated exhaust always lands above the floor: eta = 0.9 gives 4.32 and eta = 0.5 gives 13.93, against 3.73. So the checks are not vacuous.

On theorem against toy: the script checks only the 1-D equality case and the collimated eta = u family. It does not check Le's general path-length inequality (L >= d, turns, non-collimated exhaust). That is enough for the tree's straight 1-D braking. The broader lemma rests on the READ text, not on any machine check here.

The NARROWED grade rests on the dropped hypothesis at arrival.py:13, 'no propulsion does better per unit energy'. Le's condition F = -dP/ds future causal is what makes the floor hold, and arrival.py's own slingshot and magsail fall outside it. I confirmed that sentence reads exactly so at lines 11-13. That grade is supported by the evidence.

The '76x' remains unexplained. Fuel ratio 55.99, kinetic-energy ratio 881 and momentum ratio 36 do not match. 18^1.5 = 76.37 is a numerical coincidence I noticed, and I am not claiming it as the explanation.

The data rows hold up at source and the grade stands. I found three corrections; none of them moves the grade.

WHAT HOLDS:

(2) Row LLI: the Will 1403.7377 quote is verbatim in the cached page text (p.12): '|f(3)| < 10^-4' and the UHECR spectra 'show no evidence for violations of Lorentz invariance'. One weakness: value_then names Michelson-Morley, Kennedy-Thorndike and Ives-Stilwell without any READ source. (3) Row tree-inputs: I recomputed every value independently (1.0487888, 1.1055416, 1.3870748, 2.0714742, 3.7316716, 14.106736). The rederive script exits 0 with all checks ok. 3.7314 differs from the computed value by 7.28e-5 relative, as recorded.
(4) moves_conclusion = 'No' follows for every row. The result is kinematic and uses no measured datum.

CORRECTION 1: Henriques-Natario 1105.5235 is no longer NAMED-NOT-READ. The quota had recovered and I READ it via answer_pdf_queries. Its Theorem 2.1 gives m1 = m0 exp(-(1/v) Int |covariant acceleration| dtau), and says v = 1 is 'a photon rocket'. Its eq (1)-(3) state 'The only a priori restriction to J is that it must be timelike or null and future-directed', with exhaust as the only momentum sink. That is a second READ source for exactly the hypothesis the audit says arrival.py:13 drops. The NARROWED finding is therefore corroborated, not presumed. H-N's ref [4] is 'Ackeret, J.: Zur Theorie der Raketen. Helv. Phys. Acta 19, 103-112 (1946)'. That corroborates the attribution, which the audit took only from the entry name. Ackeret himself stays NAMED-NOT-READ. In 1-D Minkowski space the H-N cost integral equals the rapidity, so the tree's formula is the v = 1 case. The GR form changes only flat acceleration to covariant acceleration, which does not move the tree's flat-spacetime use.

CORRECTION 2: lacked_data (ii) is no longer only NAMED. Keane & Zhang 1205.2281 (READ) gives evidence for it:
- 'much of the energy goes into electrically neutral particles which contribute nothing to the thrust'
- realistic charged-pion effective exhaust is ve ~ 0.69c (0.81c x 85% nozzle)
- Morgan's 1974 <v±> = 0.92c was revised down to 0.81c with modern data.

So M's hypothesis is answered with evidence: earlier workers did lack data. But the correction runs AWAY from the photon floor. At ve = 0.69c, braking from 0.866c needs M0/M1 = 6.74, against the floor of 3.73 (my script). This strengthens the 'floor' reading and does not touch the formula. The audit's conclusion here is right, and it is now evidenced rather than named.

CORRECTION 3: the audit's recorded discrepancy (a) is mischaracterised. The audit says 'no reading tried gives 76', and its script asserts 'no reading of the photon formula yields 76'. In fact 76 reproduces as a mixed ratio: M0/M1 at 0.866c divided by fuel-per-tonne at 0.0476c gives 3.7317/0.04879 = 76.49, and the tree's printed figures give 3.73/0.049 = 76.1. The tree's '76x' is still a discrepancy, because it divides a mass ratio by a fuel fraction and the like-for-like fuel ratio is 55.99. But it should be recorded as 'mismatched quantities', not 'unreproducible'. This is about precision in recording a discrepancy, and it sits in the tree's own arithmetic, not in the external result.

None of the three moves the grade. The formula stands in its class, and the unconditioned 'no propulsion does better' at arrival.py:13 remains the only reason for NARROWED, now supported by two READ sources (Le L2.1 and H-N eqs 1-3).

audits.lacked_data:
M's hypothesis, tested on this composite. What the authors lacked: ICRP 23 (1975) lacked in vivo data for women, the later anatomical review (ICRP 89, 2002) and the voxel tissues (ICRP 110, 2009). Lodders 2003 lacked the post-2003 CI N budget (LBP25, 1965 ppm) and returned-sample data. A09 lacked the 3D non-LTE Li analysis with complete UV opacity behind AAG21's 0.96.

EVIDENCE THAT HAVING THE DATA CHANGES THE CONCLUSION: each of the three later data, substituted alone, flips a binder identity that D25 prints. AAG21 Li (READ as a data file) moves the photosphere to Li (2138.5 > 1894.4). LBP25 N (carried) moves the CI chondrite to N (13.07 > 11.25). The ICRP 110 bulk (carried) moves the photosphere to Li and the CI chondrite to C. The fragility was also visible in the older data: A09's own Li +- 0.10 spans the 9 % margin, and PON14's 2014 N band spans the CI crossover.

EVIDENCE THAT IT DOES NOT: no datum refutes any of the three measurements as made for their defined objects (Reference Man, the CI group means, the present-day solar photosphere). The moves are refinements, a changed reference population, or a contested revision. The MAGNITUDES survive every substitution run here: the photosphere stays within 1752-2157 kg/kg (within 1.23x of 1911) and CI within 9.02-13.07 kg/kg (order ten, as printed). D25's own status (OPEN: the gate is unchecked at the destination) and specthm R11, which cites that status, do not depend on the binder identity.

Net: the authors' data were incomplete in exactly the elements the tree's binder label rests on (Li, N, P). Having the later data moves the LABEL, not the scale, and not D25's OPEN verdict.

The photosphere column is solar_hybrid, which uses photospheric values where determined and meteoritic ones otherwise. The CI column is the un-normalised CHONDRITE table. These are the tree's own transcriptions, so the check is independent arithmetic, not independent data. The A09 values were read at source by the sibling audit.

I checked the AAG2021.dat columns myself. The file's header is Number,atm,ab_phot,err_phot,ab_CI,error_CI, so column 4 really is meteoritic and the AAG21 hybrid is encoded correctly. I also read the pyrolite files directly:
